knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\) be priority queues containing generated, unexpanded propagated states, with each state assigned to at least one queue. At iteration \(t\), a scheduler selects a nonempty queue \(Q_{i_t}\), removes its best state according to that queue's key, tests it, and inserts its exhaustive nonfailed children according to the assignment rule. Duplicate states are expanded at most once. Stop at a solution or when all queues are empty. If the scheduler is fair—every continuously nonempty queue is selected infinitely often—and at least one component ordering is complete, the interleaving is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple best-first queues are alternated fairly; completeness follows when duplicates are controlled and at least one fairly scheduled component ordering is complete.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many component queues.
The scheduler is fair and node processing terminates.
At least one component ordering is complete for the generated search tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fair interleaving preserves the completeness of a complete component traversal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: “Interleaved best-first search” is not uniquely defined. Completeness also depends on how generated children are assigned to queues and how duplicate suppression interacts with the complete component ordering. The exact local variant needs a source.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative-Deepening Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth-first iterative deepening on a finite propagation-guided search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rooted search tree of maximum depth \(D<\infty\), set \(L=0\). For each limit \(L\), perform depth-first search from the root, applying propagation at every node and pruning inconsistent nodes, but do not expand a node of depth \(L\). Stop and output a solution when one is encountered; otherwise increment \(L\) and restart. If the depth-limited pass proves that no unpruned node was cut off by its limit, return infeasible. With \(L=0,1,\ldots,D\), every unpruned node is eventually visited.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly run propagation-guided depth-first search with increasing depth limits. On a finite tree, this eventually finds a solution or establishes infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The propagated search tree is finite and has maximum depth \(D\).
Branching and propagation are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure is complete and uses \(O(D)\) search-stack space, excluding propagation state.
review_flags: Exact CP-specific source locator is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the iterative-deepening leaf, and the finite-tree completeness statement is mathematically plausible. However, the record cites no source or inspectable locator for either the traversal or its O(D) stack-space conclusion, so it cannot pass evidence review.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Bounded Complete Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete traversal under bounded resident memory through resumable subtree descriptors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a finite rooted search tree and let memory hold at most \(M\geq 1\) active node records. Search nodes using sound propagation. Whenever admitting a child would exceed \(M\), replace one or more resident subtrees by finite descriptors from which their unexplored portions can be regenerated, and schedule those descriptors fairly. Output the first solution found; output infeasible only after every resident node and descriptor is exhausted. If descriptor creation and regeneration preserve all unexplored children, the traversal is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store only a bounded active frontier, replacing displaced subtrees by regenerable descriptors. Fair resumption preserves completeness on a finite tree.
assumptions_latex: The search tree \(T\) is finite.
Descriptors losslessly identify unexplored subtrees.
Descriptor scheduling is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible leaf is eventually examined while at most \(M\) active node records are resident.
review_flags: The title admits several distinct algorithms; this record states a generic complete regeneration scheme.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is plausible, but the title does not identify a unique established method. The proposed lossless-descriptor regeneration scheme needs a source that establishes its identity, bounded-memory model, fairness condition, and completeness claim.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Using Constraint Programming and Local Search Methods to Solve Vehicle Routing Problems
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Using Constraint Programming and Local Search Methods to Solve Vehicle Routing Problems

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Limited Discrepancy Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical LDS for a finite ordered binary search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a heuristic-preferred child at every internal node of a binary tree of maximum depth \(D\). A discrepancy is a choice of the nonpreferred child. For limits \(k=0,1,\ldots,D\), restart depth-first search at the root and explore every root-to-node path having at most \(k\) discrepancies, applying sound propagation and pruning failures. Stop at the first solution; after the pass \(k=D\) is exhausted, return infeasible. Earlier paths may be revisited in successive passes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart depth-first search with discrepancy limits zero through the tree depth, eventually covering every path despite revisiting paths allowed by earlier limits.
assumptions_latex: The ordered binary search tree has finite maximum depth \(D\).
Propagation and failure pruning are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: By the pass \(k=D\), every unpruned root-to-leaf path has been explored.
review_flags: A direct authoritative locator for classical limited discrepancy search is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits classical limited discrepancy search, and the binary finite-tree formulation is coherent. A direct authoritative locator is still required to confirm that the stated at-most-k restarting convention is the intended classical variant.

children.title: Improved Discrepancy Search
children.top_down_role: Refinements that alter how discrepancy layers or previously explored regions are revisited.

knowledge_statements.title: Improved Discrepancy Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Improved LDS using exact discrepancy layers to avoid cross-iteration duplication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a finite ordered binary tree of maximum depth \(D\), define a path discrepancy as a nonpreferred branch choice. For \(k=0,1,\ldots,D\), perform a depth-first traversal that visits a leaf only when its path contains exactly \(k\) discrepancies; prune a partial path once it has more than \(k\) discrepancies or cannot reach exactly \(k\) before termination. Apply sound propagation at each node. Stop upon finding a solution, and return infeasible after all exact-discrepancy layers are exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search leaves in exact discrepancy layers. This avoids revisiting leaves from smaller layers while retaining complete coverage of a finite ordered binary tree.
assumptions_latex: The ordered binary tree has maximum depth \(D<\infty\).
Layer pruning preserves every path capable of attaining exactly \(k\) discrepancies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each unpruned leaf is assigned to exactly one layer and is visited at most once across all layers.

notation.meaning: exact discrepancy count for the current pass

review_flags: The intended published variant and its exact pruning convention require a source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the container, but “Improved Discrepancy Search” is a specific published variant whose exact-layer traversal and pruning rules cannot be validated without an authoritative source and precise locator.

children.title: Depth-Bounded Discrepancy Search
children.top_down_role: Discrepancy search restricted by the depths at which deviations may occur.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-Bounded Discrepancy Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrepancy search that progressively enlarges the depth region permitting heuristic deviations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an ordered search tree have maximum depth \(D\), with root depth zero. For bounds \(b=0,1,\ldots,D\), restart depth-first search while permitting a nonpreferred branch only at nodes whose depth is less than \(b\); below that region, follow only preferred branches. Apply sound propagation and prune inconsistent nodes. Suppress paths already covered by smaller bounds when duplicate-free enumeration is required. Stop at a solution, or return infeasible after bound \(b=D\) is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progressively allow discrepancies at greater depths. Once the bound reaches the finite tree depth, every branch position is permitted and coverage is complete.
assumptions_latex: The ordered search tree has maximum depth \(D<\infty\).
Propagation and pruning are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(b=D\), every unpruned root-to-leaf path is admissible.
review_flags: Depth-bounded discrepancy search has variant-dependent conventions requiring source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf. The meaning and inclusivity of the depth bound, duplicate-suppression rule, and relationship to published depth-bounded discrepancy search are variant-dependent and require a direct source locator.

children.title: Depth–Discrepancy Allocation
children.top_down_role: Structural allocation of deviation allowances across search depth.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth–Discrepancy Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial allocation of discrepancies among eligible branching depths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary root-to-leaf path of depth \(D\), let \(E\subseteq\{0,\ldots,D-1\}\) be the depths at which discrepancies are permitted. A path using exactly \(k\) discrepancies is represented by a subset \(S\subseteq E\) with \(|S|=k\), where the nonpreferred child is selected precisely at depths in \(S\). Consequently, the number of depth-allocation patterns is \(\binom{|E|}{k}\) for exact budget \(k\), and \(\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{|E|}{j}\) for an at-most budget \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrepancy pattern is a subset of eligible depths. Exact and cumulative budgets therefore induce binomial counts of possible depth allocations.
assumptions_latex: Every considered path has depth \(D\).
Branching is binary with one preferred child at each depth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact and cumulative discrepancy allocations have the stated binomial cardinalities.

notation.meaning: depths at which a path deviates

review_flags: The combinatorial statement is standard, but no directly supporting locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind for the depth-allocation encoding, and the binomial formulas are coherent under the stated fixed-depth binary model. No cited source or standard-field rationale supports inclusion of this formulation in the exact discrepancy-search container.

children.title: Bound-Induced Coverage Gaps
children.top_down_role: Search regions deferred or omitted under particular depth or discrepancy bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Induced Coverage Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paths excluded when fixed depth or discrepancy bounds are not eventually relaxed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be an unpruned root-to-leaf path with discrepancy count \(\delta(p)\) and deepest discrepancy depth \(h(p)\). A traversal restricted to at most \(k\) discrepancies and to discrepancies above depth bound \(b\) cannot visit \(p\) whenever \(\delta(p)>k\) or \(h(p)\geq b\). Hence any fixed pair \((k,b)\) leaves a coverage gap if the tree contains such a path; completeness requires a schedule whose admissible bounds eventually include every finite pair \((\delta(p),h(p))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed discrepancy and depth bounds omit paths exceeding either bound. Completeness requires the bounds eventually to admit every finite path profile.
assumptions_latex: The search tree is ordered and finite-depth.
A discrepancy at depth \(d\) is admissible only when \(d<b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A solution occurring only on an excluded path may be missed despite sound propagation.

notation.meaning: number of discrepancies on path p
deepest discrepancy depth on path p

review_flags: No source locator directly addresses the stated coverage boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is the correct role for this leaf, and the exclusion condition is internally consistent with discrepancies being allowed only at depths d<b. The completeness boundary has no supporting citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Credit-Bounded Search
children.top_down_role: Search regimes allocating finite exploration credit across nodes, branches, or subtrees.

knowledge_statements.title: Credit-Bounded Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-bounded subtree exploration using recursively allocated nonnegative credit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign the root credit \(C>0\). At an expanded node with residual credit \(c\), propagation produces children \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\); choose allocations \(c_i\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i\leq c-r\), where \(r>0\) is the charged expansion cost. Explore child \(v_i\) only if its allocated credit covers its next required charge. Stop a subtree when its credit is exhausted, output a discovered solution, and otherwise return its unexplored-subtree descriptor. Completeness requires later replenishment or a schedule with unbounded cumulative credit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Charge search operations against recursively divided credit. Exhausted subtrees suspend with descriptors; completeness requires eventual replenishment sufficient for every finite solution path.
assumptions_latex: Each expansion has positive charged cost \(r\).
Child credits are nonnegative and do not exceed residual parent credit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A run with initial credit \(C\) consumes at most \(C\) charged resource but need not be complete.
review_flags: Credit-based search has implementation-specific accounting and allocation rules.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the container, but credit-bounded search is implementation- and source-specific. The charging equation, suspension descriptors, and replenishment condition require an authoritative locator before the mathematical version can be trusted.

children.title: Failure-Bounded Search
children.top_down_role: Search regimes limiting exploration by accumulated failures.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Bounded Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation-guided depth-first search limited by a counted number of failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a failure budget \(F\in\mathbb{N}\), perform depth-first search with sound propagation and initialize \(f=0\). Whenever propagation proves the current node inconsistent, increment \(f\), backtrack, and continue while \(f\leq F\). Stop with a solution when a feasible complete assignment is reached. If another failure would make \(f>F\), suspend and return the remaining frontier together with budget-exhausted status. Only exhaustion of the entire frontier, rather than budget exhaustion, certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Count propagation failures during depth-first search and suspend when the budget is exceeded. Budget exhaustion is not an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: Propagation detects failure soundly.
The budget satisfies \(F\in\mathbb{N}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run encounters at most \(F+1\) failures before suspension and is generally incomplete for fixed \(F\).
review_flags: A direct source for the precise failure-counting convention is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits failure-bounded search. The record consistently permits F failures and suspends upon encountering the next one, but that off-by-one convention and the required residual-frontier behavior need direct source support.

children.title: Credit Allocation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural choices for distributing, inheriting, or reclaiming search credit.

knowledge_statements.title: Credit Allocation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions distinguishing conservative, exhaustive, and fair credit allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with distributable credit \(c\) and children indexed by \(I\), an allocation is a vector \((c_i)_{i\in I}\) with \(c_i\geq0\). It is conservative when \(\sum_{i\in I}c_i\leq c\), exhaustive when equality holds, and locally positive when \(c_i>0\) for every live child. Across repeated resumptions \(t=1,2,\ldots\), an allocation schedule is credit-fair when every persistently live child \(i\) satisfies \(\sum_t c_i^{(t)}=\infty\). Credit fairness prevents permanent starvation of any finite-cost continuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Credit may be conserved, fully distributed, or positive for all children. Across resumptions, divergent cumulative credit to every live child is the fairness condition.
assumptions_latex: The child index set \(I\) is finite at each node.
Credits are nonnegative real quantities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every continuation requiring finite total credit is eventually affordable under a credit-fair schedule.

notation.meaning: credit assigned to child i at resumption t

review_flags: The regimes are formalized generically because no canonical credit-search source was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is a plausible role for allocation and fairness requirements. However, the conservative, exhaustive, locally positive, and credit-fair regimes appear to be a generic formalization rather than a sourced canonical taxonomy; moreover, divergent assigned credit implies eventual affordability only under specified accumulation and charging semantics.

children.title: Failure-Budget Exhaustion
children.top_down_role: Coverage and termination consequences when an exploration failure budget is depleted.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Budget Exhaustion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic boundary between resource exhaustion and exhaustive proof of infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a failure-bounded traversal stop after consuming budget \(F\), and let \(U\) be its set of generated or regenerable unexplored nodes. If \(U\neq\varnothing\), budget exhaustion certifies only that the prescribed run limit was reached; it does not certify that the constraint problem is infeasible. Infeasibility may be returned only when \(U=\varnothing\) and every explored leaf was rejected by sound propagation or branching. Thus a nonempty residual frontier is a verifiable witness that search coverage is incomplete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reaching the failure limit is not proof of infeasibility. A nonempty residual frontier witnesses incomplete coverage; infeasibility requires exhaustive sound rejection.
assumptions_latex: Propagation and branching are sound.
The residual set \(U\) represents every unexplored continuation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U\neq\varnothing\), the only valid terminal status is budget exhausted or unknown, not infeasible.
review_flags: The logical boundary is standard but lacks a directly supporting CP-search locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is the correct content kind, and the distinction between budget exhaustion and exhaustive infeasibility is mathematically coherent under the lossless-frontier assumption. A CP-search source with a specific locator is still required.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Sliced Subtree Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair interleaving of resumable propagation-guided subtree traversals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the unexplored search frontier into resumable subtrees \(S_1,S_2,\ldots\). For rounds \(t=1,2,\ldots\), select a live subtree by a fair scheduler and run its propagation-guided search for at most \(q_t>0\) units of a specified resource, such as node expansions or time. Save its continuation state when the slice ends, delete it when exhausted, and stop upon finding a solution. Return infeasible only when no live subtree remains. Completeness holds when every live subtree receives unbounded cumulative effective work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interleave resumable subtree searches using finite slices. Fair scheduling and unbounded cumulative work per live subtree preserve completeness on finite search trees.
assumptions_latex: Subtree continuation states preserve all unexplored branches.
The scheduler is fair.
Each search operation has finite resource cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every solution reachable after finite work is eventually found; exhaustion of all subtrees certifies infeasibility.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports time-sliced subtree search.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits time-sliced subtree search. The statement gives a plausible fair resumable traversal, but no source identifies this algorithm or supports its effective-work fairness condition and completeness conclusion; the listed local inventory does not address it.

assumptions_latex: The propagated search tree is binary and has depth \(n\).
At each node the heuristic designates one child as preferred; taking the other child contributes one discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A discrepancy budget below the number of erroneous preferred choices on every solution path makes the search incomplete for that budget.

notation.meaning: discrepancy count of a root-to-node path

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard binary limited-discrepancy model with unit cost for each nonpreferred branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a root-to-leaf path \(P\), let \(\delta(P)\) be the number of nonpreferred branches on \(P\). Budgeted discrepancy search with budget \(K\) visits only paths satisfying \(\delta(P)\le K\). Hence, if every solution path \(P\) has \(\delta(P)>K\), that run finds no solution. In particular, construct a depth-\(n\) tree whose unique solution lies below the nonpreferred child of the root and then follows preferred children. Its solution path has \(\delta(P)=1\), so budget \(K=0\) excludes the entire solution subtree. Thus even one erroneous root preference defeats the zero-discrepancy run, irrespective of all later choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single wrong preferred branch at the root can place every solution outside a small discrepancy budget, even when all later heuristic choices are correct.
knowledge_statements.title: Root-Error Sensitivity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the binary unit-discrepancy construction is mathematically coherent. However, no citation is supplied for the limited-discrepancy search model or the claimed root-error sensitivity, so the candidate cannot be accepted.

assumptions_latex: Search is rerun independently for successive discrepancy bounds \(0,1,\ldots,K\).
No cross-run cache suppresses previously expanded nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A node first reachable with discrepancy \(d\le K\) may be expanded \(K-d+1\) times.

notation.meaning: number of nodes having path discrepancy exactly d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to independently restarted bounded-discrepancy runs without retained search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a node whose root path has discrepancy \(d\) is expanded in every independently restarted run with bound \(k\ge d\). Across bounds \(k=0,1,\ldots,K\), that node is therefore expanded at most \(K-d+1\) times and exactly that many times if no earlier termination or pruning removes it. If \(N_d\) nodes have discrepancy exactly \(d\), the cumulative expansion count is bounded by \[\sum_{d=0}^{K}(K-d+1)N_d.\] A single nonrestarting traversal that expands each eligible node once would instead use at most \(\sum_{d=0}^{K}N_d\) expansions, exposing the duplicate-revisitation overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restarting search at every discrepancy bound can re-expand a discrepancy-d node K-d+1 times, producing the stated weighted expansion total.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Revisitation Overhead

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits duplicate revisitation under independently restarted discrepancy bounds. The weighted count is conditional on the stated expansion and pruning assumptions, but no discrepancy-search source supports either the restart model or the bound.

children.title: Search Choice Heuristic Family
children.top_down_role: Static and adaptive choices that order branching objects and alternatives without changing the logical coverage of complete search.

assumptions_latex: The finite CSP has variables \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\).
A total priority order is fixed before search begins.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Variable selection is independent of domains, failures, and propagation outcomes observed during search.

notation.meaning: fixed priority permutation of variable indices
variables unassigned at search state s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines static ordering by a fixed permutation, while propagation may still alter domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite CSP and a permutation \(\pi=(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_n)\) fixed before search. At any nonterminal search state \(s\), after propagation, choose \[x_{\pi_j}\quad\text{where}\quad j=\min\{i:x_{\pi_i}\in U(s)\}.\] Branch on the chosen variable according to the separately specified value-ordering rule, propagate, and repeat until a solution, failure, or external stopping condition occurs. The permutation is not recomputed from current domain sizes, constraint degrees, conflicts, impacts, or activities; only assigned variables are skipped.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A static ordering always selects the earliest unassigned variable in one permutation fixed before search, regardless of information learned during search.
knowledge_statements.title: Static Variable Orderings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Static Variable Orderings, and the permutation-based selector is internally precise. No inspectable CP-search citation is provided for this characterization.

children.title: First-Fail Selection
children.top_down_role: Variable selection centered on exposing likely failure early in the search tree.

assumptions_latex: Propagation has reached a fixpoint at the current state \(s\).
At least one variable remains unassigned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected variable belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in U(s)}|D_s(x)|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-fail is formalized as choosing a currently most tightly domain-constrained variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The first-fail selection principle chooses a variable expected to expose inconsistency earliest. Under the domain-cardinality proxy, its admissible selections at state \(s\) are exactly \[F(s)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in U(s)}|D_s(x)|.\] Any selected variable \(x^*\) must satisfy \(x^*\in F(s)\). If some unassigned variable has an empty domain, propagation has already certified failure and no branching variable is selected. If several variables attain the minimum positive cardinality, first-fail alone leaves their relative order unspecified and requires a tie rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After propagation, first-fail chooses an unassigned variable with the smallest current domain; ties require a separate rule.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Fail Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits First-Fail Selection, and the minimum-current-domain formulation correctly leaves ties to a separate rule. Acceptance requires an authoritative CP source with a specific locator connecting first fail to this domain-cardinality proxy.

children.title: Minimum-Domain Ordering
children.top_down_role: Variable ordering based on the smallest current domain.

assumptions_latex: The current propagated state \(s\) is consistent.
The tie-breaking order \(\prec\) is total on the variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule returns the unique \(\prec\)-least member of the minimum-domain set.

notation.meaning: fixed or dynamically supplied tie order

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic minimum-domain selection obtained by adding an explicit total tie order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a consistent propagated state \(s\), compute \(m_s(x)=|D_s(x)|\) for every \(x\in U(s)\), set \[M(s)=\{x\in U(s):m_s(x)=\min_{y\in U(s)}m_s(y)\},\] and return the \(\prec\)-least variable in \(M(s)\). Branch using an independently specified value rule, propagate the resulting child, and recompute domain sizes before the next selection. Stop with failure if propagation produces an empty domain, with success when all constraints are satisfied by a complete assignment, or according to an external search limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-domain ordering recomputes propagated domain sizes at each node and deterministically selects the smallest-domain variable using an explicit tie order.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Domain Ordering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the deterministic minimum-domain leaf, and the state, domains, tie order, and stopping cases are adequately introduced. No supporting CP-heuristics citation is supplied.

children.title: Domain-Size Tie Regimes
children.top_down_role: Secondary ordering choices when multiple variables share the same domain size.

assumptions_latex: The propagated state \(s\) has a nonempty set \(U(s)\) of unassigned variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Domain cardinality determines a unique choice exactly when the minimum-domain set is a singleton.

notation.meaning: minimum-domain tie class at state s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes precisely when domain size alone does or does not determine the next variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the minimum-domain tie class by \[T_s=\left\{x\in U(s):|D_s(x)|=\min_{y\in U(s)}|D_s(y)|\right\}.\] The domain-size rule uniquely determines the branching variable if and only if \(|T_s|=1\). When \(|T_s|>1\), every member of \(T_s\) has the same primary score, so any unique selection necessarily uses information not contained in that score, such as a fixed index, constraint degree, weighted degree, activity, impact, or randomization. A deterministic implementation is fully specified only after its tie-breaking map selects one element of every possible non-singleton \(T_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain size uniquely selects a variable only when exactly one unassigned variable has minimum cardinality; otherwise a secondary rule is mathematically necessary.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Size Tie Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role exactly fits the tie-regime leaf, and the singleton characterization follows from the defined score. The record nevertheless has no cited source or inspectable locator for its CP-search interpretation.

children.title: First-Fail Proxy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where current domain size poorly reflects the likelihood or cost of failure.

assumptions_latex: A variable heuristic observes only the vector of current domain cardinalities and a fixed tie order.
Two propagated states share those observations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The heuristic cannot distinguish different constraint structures or downstream search costs in those states.

notation.meaning: observable domain-size vector at state s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An information boundary for pure domain-cardinality first-fail heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a deterministic selector whose only state-dependent input is \(q(s)=(|D_s(x)|)_{x\in U(s)}\), with a fixed tie order. For any propagated states \(s\) and \(t\) having identically named unassigned variables, if \(q(s)=q(t)\), then \(H(s)=H(t)\). This remains true even when the residual constraint relations in \(s\) and \(t\) differ and branching on the selected variable produces different subtree sizes. Therefore domain size is only a proxy for failure likelihood: it cannot encode constraint topology, value support distribution, or the cost of propagation beyond their effects on current cardinalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure first-fail cannot distinguish states with identical domain sizes, even when their residual constraints and resulting search costs differ substantially.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Fail Proxy Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the indistinguishability statement is precise for a selector whose only state-dependent input is the named domain-size vector. A source is needed to support presenting this formal information boundary as a first-fail limitation.

children.title: Degree Orderings
children.top_down_role: Variable orderings based on the number or structure of relevant neighboring constraints.

assumptions_latex: The CSP constraint graph is fixed before search.
Each variable has a finite static degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule selects an unassigned variable of maximum static degree, with explicit tie breaking.

notation.meaning: number of constraints incident to x, or neighbors under the declared graph convention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static maximum-degree ordering under a declared constraint-graph convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a constraint graph \(G\) and a total tie order \(\prec\). At a nonterminal propagated state \(s\), form \[M_G(s)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in U(s)}\deg_G(x),\] and select the \(\prec\)-least member of \(M_G(s)\). The degree values are computed from the original graph and are not reduced when neighboring variables become assigned or constraints become entailed. After branching and propagation, repeat over the remaining variables. For nonbinary constraints, the implementation must declare whether \(\deg_G(x)\) counts incident constraints or distinct neighbors in the primal graph, since these scores need not coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degree ordering chooses an unassigned variable with maximum degree in a fixed constraint graph, using a declared degree convention and tie rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Degree Orderings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Degree Orderings, and the record properly distinguishes incident-constraint degree from primal-graph neighbor degree. No direct CP source establishes the selected convention or static maximum-degree rule.

children.title: Domain–Degree Orderings
children.top_down_role: Variable orderings combining current domain size with constraint degree.

assumptions_latex: Every unassigned variable has a nonempty propagated domain.
Its degree score is nonnegative and is interpreted under a fixed graph convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected variable minimizes the domain-to-degree score under the stated zero-degree convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio form combining small domains with large constraint degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At propagated state \(s\), assign each \(x\in U(s)\) the score \[r_s(x)=\begin{cases}|D_s(x)|/d_s(x),&d_s(x)>0,\\+\infty,&d_s(x)=0.\end{cases}\] Select a variable in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in U(s)}r_s(x)\), resolving ties by a specified total order. Here \(d_s(x)\) may be a declared static or dynamic degree, but that choice must remain explicit. The score favors variables having simultaneously small current domains and many constraint connections. If every remaining variable has degree zero, the ratio gives only infinite ties and the fallback tie rule determines the choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain-degree ordering minimizes domain size divided by declared degree, favoring small domains and high connectivity while explicitly handling zero-degree variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain–Degree Orderings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the domain-degree leaf, and the zero-denominator convention is explicit. The precise ratio orientation, permitted degree variants, and zero-degree treatment are variant-sensitive and need a direct source with a specific locator.

children.title: Dynamic Degree Variants
children.top_down_role: Degree scores updated to reflect the residual constraint graph during search.

assumptions_latex: A propagated search state \(s\) determines which variables and constraints remain active.
The active-degree convention is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dynamic degree is recomputed after propagation and may change between parent and child states.

notation.meaning: residual active constraint graph at state s
degree of x in the residual graph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-graph variants that update degree after assignment and propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After propagation at state \(s\), construct the residual graph \(G_s\) using the declared convention: vertices are unassigned variables, and edges or incidences represent active, nonentailed constraints. Compute \(\deg_{G_s}(x)\) for every remaining variable and select a member of \[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in U(s)}\deg_{G_s}(x),\] using an explicit tie rule. Branch, propagate, rebuild or incrementally update the residual graph, and repeat. Unlike static degree, the score can decrease when variables are assigned, constraints become entailed, or propagation removes an incidence; correctness of the implementation requires these events to match the chosen active-graph definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic degree ordering repeatedly selects a maximum-degree variable in the residual active constraint graph, recomputing scores after branching and propagation.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Degree Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Dynamic Degree Variants, and the distinction from static degree is clear. The definition of active or nonentailed constraints is implementation-dependent and is unsupported by a cited CP source.

children.title: Sparse-Graph Ranking Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ranking behavior when degree information is weak, uniform, or structurally misleading.

assumptions_latex: The residual primal graph \(G_s\) is \(d\)-regular on the unassigned variables.
The selector uses only residual degree and a fixed tie order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degree supplies no state-dependent ranking: every unassigned variable is tied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-score indistinguishability on regular residual graphs, including sparse regular and isolated cases; sparsity alone does not imply a complete tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the residual graph \(G_s\) is \(d\)-regular, then \(\deg_{G_s}(x)=d\) for every \(x\in U(s)\), and therefore \[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in U(s)}\deg_{G_s}(x)=U(s).\] A degree-only selector consequently reduces to its tie rule and cannot rank variables by domain size, constraint tightness, conflict history, or propagation impact. The boundary includes the sparse edgeless case \(d=0\), which can arise after all remaining constraints are entailed or when the remaining variables are isolated. More generally, degree cannot distinguish variables in the same degree class, even if their incident constraint relations have different tightness or computational cost. Sparsity by itself does not imply that all variables are tied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a regular residual graph, including an edgeless sparse graph, all variables have equal degree, so degree ordering collapses to its tie rule; sparsity alone does not force this collapse.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Graph Ranking Boundaries

assumptions_latex: Every active constraint \(c\) has a positive weight \(w(c)\), initially fixed by convention.
A propagation failure identifies one or more responsible constraints whose weights are updated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selection minimizes current domain size divided by accumulated incident conflict weight.

notation.meaning: weighted degree of variable x at state s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-history domain-over-weighted-degree ordering with unit failure increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(w(c)=1\) for every constraint \(c\). At propagated state \(s\), compute \[\operatorname{wdeg}_s(x)=\sum_{c\in C_s(x)}w(c)\] and select an unassigned variable minimizing \(|D_s(x)|/\operatorname{wdeg}_s(x)\), assigning score \(+\infty\) when the denominator is zero and resolving ties explicitly. When propagation produces a failure attributed to constraint \(c\), update \(w(c)\leftarrow w(c)+1\); if several constraints receive blame, apply the declared attribution policy. Backtrack and recompute scores. Search stops on a solution, proof of failure, or external limit. The weights affect ordering only, not CSP feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict-weighted degree selects a small-domain variable incident to frequently failing constraints, increasing blamed constraint weights after propagation failures.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Weighted Degree Orderings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Conflict-Weighted Degree Orderings, and the record clearly separates heuristic weights from feasibility. Initialization, active-constraint membership, failure attribution, and multi-constraint blame are variant-sensitive, so a direct source is required before acceptance.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite-domain constraint satisfaction problem at a search node with propagated domains \(D(x)\).
A deterministic propagation operator \(\operatorname{prop}\) maps each trial assignment to either failure or residual domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected variable maximizes its estimated expected domain reduction.

notation.meaning: Aggregate logarithmic size of the current domains.
Observed reduction produced by probing a value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain impact search using propagation-induced domain reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every candidate variable \(x\) and value \(a\in D(x)\), probe \(x=a\), propagate, and set \(S_{x=a}=0\) if propagation fails; otherwise set \(S_{x=a}=\sum_y\log |D_{x=a}(y)|\). Maintain an empirical estimate \(\widehat I(x=a)\) of \(I(x=a)=S-S_{x=a}\) from probes and realized branches. Define \(\widehat I(x)=|D(x)|^{-1}\sum_{a\in D(x)}\widehat I(x=a)\). Select a variable in \(\operatorname*{argmax}_x\widehat I(x)\), break ties by a fixed rule, branch on it, and update the estimates after propagation. Stop when failure or a complete assignment is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probe assignments, estimate their propagated domain reduction, and branch on a variable having maximum average estimated impact.
knowledge_statements.title: Impact-Based Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the logarithmic reduction and averaging rule are not established as the canonical impact-based-search definition. A specific CP source is required to determine the correct impact normalization, aggregation, probing, and update conventions.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite-domain constraint problem searched by propagation and backtracking.
Each propagation event identifies variables whose domains changed or whose associated constraints participated in failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected variable has maximum current decayed propagation activity among eligible variables.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable activity driven by recent propagation or failure participation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(A_x=0\) for every variable \(x\). After each propagation episode, replace every score by \(A_x\leftarrow\rho A_x\), and for each variable credited with a domain reduction or failure participation apply \(A_x\leftarrow A_x+w_x\), where \(w_x>0\) is the prescribed event weight. At a branching node, select an unfixed variable in \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x:|D(x)|>1} A_x\), using a fixed secondary rule for ties. Branch, propagate, and repeat until failure or a complete assignment. Thus recent frequently active variables dominate old or inactive variables when \(\rho<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decay stored scores, reward variables involved in propagation or failure, and branch on the eligible variable with greatest activity.
knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Based Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but activity-based search has source-dependent event-credit, increment, rescaling, and decay conventions. No cited evidence supports this particular hybrid of domain-change and failure participation.

assumptions_latex: Each variable \(x\) has a finite current domain \(D(x)\).
Every domain is equipped with a fixed total order \(\preceq_x\) independent of the current search history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Values are tried in the restriction of the predetermined order \(\preceq_x\) to the current domain.

notation.meaning: Fixed total order for values of variable x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-independent value enumeration for finite-domain branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Before search, choose for each variable \(x\) a total order \(\preceq_x\) on its original domain. Whenever search selects an unfixed \(x\), enumerate its current values as \(a_1\preceq_x a_2\preceq_x\cdots\preceq_x a_k\), where \(D(x)=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\), and explore branches \(x=a_1,\ldots,x=a_k\) in that order. Domain deletions merely remove deleted values from this sequence; propagation outcomes, conflicts, activities, incumbents, and objective bounds do not alter the relative order of surviving values. Search terminates at failure, a complete assignment, or an externally specified limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix a total value order before search and always enumerate surviving values in that unchanged relative order.
knowledge_statements.title: Static Value Orderings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is precise and the algorithm role fits static value ordering, but the record supplies no inspectable citation with a section, page, or definition locator.

children.title: Promise Orderings
children.top_down_role: Value rankings based on estimated residual feasibility or future search potential.

assumptions_latex: At the current node, \(x\) is selected and \(D(x)\) is finite.
A scoring rule assigns each trial value a real-valued estimate of residual search opportunity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Values are explored in nonincreasing estimated promise.

notation.meaning: Estimated promise of assigning value a to x.
Propagated child state after assigning x=a.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic promise ordering parameterized by an explicit residual-opportunity estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(a\in D(x)\), form or estimate the propagated child \(P_{x=a}\) and compute \(p_x(a)\), with larger scores stipulated to mean greater predicted likelihood of extending to a solution. Order the values as \(a_1,\ldots,a_k\) so that \(p_x(a_1)\ge\cdots\ge p_x(a_k)\), resolving equal scores by a fixed rule. Explore \(x=a_i\) in this order, omitting any value whose probe immediately fails. The estimator may use residual domain sizes, solution-count approximations, or learned statistics, but its definition and orientation must be fixed before scores are compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score each value by predicted residual solution opportunity and explore values from greatest to least estimated promise.
knowledge_statements.title: Promise Orderings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but “promise” has multiple meanings in the CP literature. Evidence is needed for the selected residual-solution-opportunity orientation and the treatment of failed probes.

children.title: Min-Conflicts Orderings
children.top_down_role: Value rankings favoring alternatives associated with fewer anticipated conflicts.

knowledge_statements.title: Min-Conflicts Orderings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-conflicting value ordering within propagation-guided tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(a\in D(x)\), compute \(c_x(a)\) from a prescribed conflict estimator, such as the number or weighted sum of currently incompatible neighboring assignments, violated constraints, or values removed by propagation after \(x=a\). Arrange \(D(x)=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\) so that \(c_x(a_1)\le\cdots\le c_x(a_k)\), with deterministic tie-breaking, and explore the branches \(x=a_1,\ldots,x=a_k\) in that order. Any probed value producing immediate failure may be assigned score \(+\infty\) or removed. The rule orders branches but does not itself discard a finite-score value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate the conflicts caused by each candidate value and try the least-conflicting values first without pruning them solely by score.
assumptions_latex: At the current node, \(x\) is selected with finite domain \(D(x)\).
Each value can be assigned a nonnegative estimate of the constraints or assignments it would violate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Values are explored in nondecreasing estimated conflict count.

notation.meaning: Estimated number or weighted sum of conflicts caused by x=a.

children.title: Promise Estimation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sources and granularities of information used to estimate value promise.

assumptions_latex: For every candidate assignment \(x=a\), propagation yields either failure or residual domains \(D_{x=a}(y)\).
A selected estimator is interpreted monotonically: larger values mean greater predicted extendability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact, propagation-based, sampled, and learned estimates are comparable only after their scale and orientation are specified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative regimes for estimating a branch's residual solution opportunity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A promise estimator may be represented by \(\widehat p_x(a)=F(P_{x=a},H,\theta)\), where \(P_{x=a}\) is the propagated child, \(H\) is search history, and \(\theta\) contains fixed or learned parameters. Common regimes include the exact count \(p_x(a)=|\operatorname{Sol}(P_{x=a})|\); the domain-product surrogate \(\widehat p_x(a)=\prod_{y\in U_{x=a}}|D_{x=a}(y)|\); a sample mean \(m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m}Z_j(x,a)\); and a learned predictor \(F_\theta(P_{x=a},H)\). Failure receives promise \(0\). A regime must specify normalization, update timing, and whether probing costs are charged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Promise may be estimated exactly, from propagated domain volume, by sampling, or by a learned predictor, with explicit orientation and normalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Promise Estimation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role is suitable for estimation regimes, but no evidence supports this proposed taxonomy or establishes the domain-product, sampling, and learned quantities as mutually comparable promise estimators under the stated conventions.

children.title: Conflict-Estimate Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where local conflict estimates misrepresent downstream search difficulty.

assumptions_latex: A value-ordering rule uses an estimate \(\widehat c_x(a)\) of a true branch conflict quantity \(c_x(a)\).
Ordering decisions do not independently prove feasibility or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without an order-preserving error guarantee, estimated conflict order need not equal true conflict order and cannot justify pruning.

notation.meaning: True conflict quantity for branch x=a.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of using approximate conflict scores as branch-order evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two values \(a,b\in D(x)\), the estimated preference \(a\prec b\) is reliable only when \(\widehat c_x(a)<\widehat c_x(b)\) implies \(c_x(a)<c_x(b)\). If uniform errors satisfy \(|\widehat c_x(v)-c_x(v)|\le\varepsilon\), then \(\widehat c_x(a)+\varepsilon<\widehat c_x(b)-\varepsilon\) is sufficient for the true ordering. When this separation fails, even bounded errors may reverse the preference. Moreover, any conflict estimate based only on the current partial assignment can miss conflicts revealed by later propagation. Therefore the score may order values, but pruning requires an independent sound propagation or bounding certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate conflict scores safely determine order only with adequate error separation; without a sound certificate they cannot justify pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Estimate Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, and the stated uniform-error separation condition is mathematically coherent. A source is still required for the nontrivial claims about conflict-estimate reliability and the prohibition on score-only pruning.

children.title: Solution-Guided Values
children.top_down_role: Value choices biased toward assignments observed in reference solutions.

assumptions_latex: The current problem and a reference solution \(r\) share variables with compatible value domains.
The selected variable \(x\) has current finite domain \(D(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reference value is tried first exactly when it remains admissible.

notation.meaning: Reference value assigned to variable x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value preference induced by a compatible reference solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When branching on \(x\), if \(r(x)\in D(x)\), place \(r(x)\) first and order the remaining values \(D(x)\setminus\{r(x)\}\) by a fixed fallback rule. If \(r(x)\notin D(x)\) or \(r\) has no mapped value for \(x\), apply the fallback rule to all of \(D(x)\). Explore the resulting branches with ordinary propagation and backtracking. The reference preference changes only branch order: it neither asserts that \(r\) satisfies the current problem nor permits removal of a nonpreferred value. Output follows the surrounding satisfaction or optimization search convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Try the compatible reference solution's value first; otherwise use a fallback order, retaining all values allowed by propagation.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Guided Values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and local meaning are appropriate, but no cited source supports this reference-solution branching convention or its stated correctness boundary.

children.title: Incumbent-Guided Values
children.top_down_role: Value choices biased toward the current best optimization solution.

assumptions_latex: An optimization search has a feasible incumbent assignment \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\).
The current branching variable \(x\) has finite domain \(D(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent value is preferred when still present, but this preference does not alter correctness or pruning conditions.

notation.meaning: Value of x in the incumbent solution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization value ordering guided by the current feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Upon selection of variable \(x\), if \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}(x)\in D(x)\), explore the branch \(x=x^{\mathrm{inc}}(x)\) first and order all remaining values by a prescribed fallback rule. If the incumbent value has been removed, use the fallback rule on the entire domain. Whenever a better feasible solution becomes incumbent, subsequent branching decisions use its values; already created nodes need not be reordered unless the implementation explicitly does so. Incumbent guidance is solely an ordering device. Feasibility propagation and valid objective bounds, rather than disagreement with the incumbent, determine pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prefer the current incumbent's admissible value, update future preferences after improvement, and leave pruning to valid propagation and bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Guided Values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits incumbent-guided value ordering, but the update and node-reordering conventions are implementation-sensitive and lack a supporting citation.

children.title: Reference-Solution Transfer
children.top_down_role: Use of solutions from earlier runs, neighboring instances, or auxiliary searches.

assumptions_latex: A source assignment \(r_s\) and target model have a declared partial variable map \(\phi\).
For mapped variables, a declared value map \(\psi_x\) converts source values into target-domain values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transferred guidance is defined only for mapped values that belong to the current target domain.

notation.meaning: Partial map from target variables to source variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transporting value preferences between explicitly mapped model instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a target variable \(x\in\operatorname{dom}(\phi)\), compute \(g(x)=\psi_x(r_s(\phi(x)))\). If \(g(x)\in D_t(x)\), place \(g(x)\) first in the target value order; otherwise invoke a fixed fallback ordering. Variables outside \(\operatorname{dom}(\phi)\) also use the fallback. The maps must preserve value meaning, not merely names or indices. Transferred values are heuristic preferences only: every target constraint is propagated independently, and no target value is pruned because it disagrees with \(r_s\). The procedure outputs the ordering supplied to the target search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map source-solution values into semantically corresponding target domains, prefer valid images, and fall back whenever mapping or admissibility fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Reference-Solution Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the transfer leaf, but the mapping conditions and semantic-preservation requirement are application-dependent and unsupported by cited evidence.

children.title: Stale-Guidance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Search regimes where reference assignments cease to provide useful value guidance.

assumptions_latex: A reference assignment \(r\) supplies preferred values during search.
The current node may have domains or constraints different from those under which \(r\) was obtained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reference disagreement alone is never a sound infeasibility or dominance certificate.

notation.meaning: Preferred value from the reference assignment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for outdated or incompatible reference preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Guidance for \(x\) is stale whenever \(r(x)\notin D(x)\), the variable or value mapping has changed, or updated constraints make closeness to \(r\) unrelated to feasibility or objective quality. In these cases the search must ignore the unavailable preference and use a complete fallback ordering over \(D(x)\). Even when \(r(x)\in D(x)\), selecting it first conveys no certificate that the branch is feasible or improving. Pruning a branch solely because it differs from \(r\) can remove every feasible or optimal solution; only sound propagation, dominance, or bound arguments may prune it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outdated reference values may be absent or misleading; discard their preference and never prune solely because a branch differs from them.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Guidance Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the claim is internally coherent, but the stale-guidance conditions and pruning warning are nontrivial claims without an inspectable source.

assumptions_latex: The search minimizes an objective \(f\) over a finite-domain constraint model.
For each candidate assignment \(x=a\), a valid or heuristic child objective score can be computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Values are explored in nondecreasing predicted objective score, while pruning remains governed by valid bounds.

notation.meaning: Predicted objective quality after assigning x=a.
Valid lower bound for a minimization child.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization-oriented value ordering based on predicted child objective quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node selecting \(x\), assign every \(a\in D(x)\) a score \(q_x(a)\), for example a valid relaxation bound \(L(P_{x=a})\), the immediate objective contribution, or a stated prediction of the best completion. Sort \(D(x)=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\) so that \(q_x(a_1)\le\cdots\le q_x(a_k)\), resolve ties by a fixed rule, and explore branches in that order. For maximization, reverse the inequalities. A heuristic score controls ordering only; a child may be pruned against the incumbent only when its score is a valid bound with the required orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Try values predicted to yield the best objective first, reversing order for maximization and pruning only with valid bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Directed Value Orderings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits objective-directed value ordering. Evidence is needed because the record combines valid relaxation bounds, immediate objective contributions, and heuristic predictions, which have different semantics even though all may be used for ordering.

children.title: Phase Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of previously preferred assignment phases across later search episodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-selection rule that reuses the most recently recorded phase after backtracking or restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each search variable \(x\in X\) have current domain \(D(x)\) and an optional stored phase \(p(x)\). When branching on \(x\), select \(p(x)\) if \(p(x)\in D(x)\); otherwise select a fallback value \(h(x,D(x))\). After choosing value \(v\), set \(p(x)\leftarrow v\). Backtracking restores domains but not the phase map; a restart likewise retains the map unless the prescribed lifetime policy expires it. Stop when propagation proves failure or all variables are assigned, and output the resulting failure or solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a variable’s last recorded value whenever it remains feasible; otherwise use a fallback rule, then replace the recorded value with the new choice.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and every current domain \(D(x)\) is finite.
\(h(x,D(x))\in D(x)\) whenever \(D(x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v=p(x)\) when the stored phase is currently feasible, and \(v=h(x,D(x))\) otherwise.

notation.meaning: stored preferred value, or phase, of variable x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formalizes the standard phase-saving mechanism in propagation-guided search
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate kind for Phase Reuse, and the reuse rule is coherent. However, no inspectable citation supports the phase-retention semantics, lifetime behavior, or added whole-search termination claims.

children.title: Value Persistence
children.top_down_role: Retention of preferred values across backtracking, restart, or neighborhood changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Value Persistence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence invariant for a stored value preference across changes in search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Index search states by \(t\), and let \(p_t(x)\) be the stored preference for variable \(x\). If no preference-update or expiration event for \(x\) occurs between states \(t\) and \(t+1\), then \(p_{t+1}(x)=p_t(x)\), independently of domain restoration by backtracking or restart. The preference affects selection only when \(p_t(x)\in D_t(x)\); persistence does not assert that the stored value remains feasible or that it must be selected after it becomes infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recorded value survives ordinary backtracking and restarts until an explicit update or expiration, but it is usable only while currently feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(p_t\) is stored outside the reversible domain state.
No update or expiration event for \(x\) occurs during the transition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{t+1}(x)=p_t(x)\), while admissible reuse additionally requires \(p_t(x)\in D_t(x)\).

notation.meaning: preference stored for x at search state t
current domain of x at search state t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: states the persistence invariant implicit in phase-saving implementations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property fits Value Persistence and clearly distinguishes retention from feasibility. An authoritative source is required for the asserted persistence across both backtracking and restart.

children.title: Persistence Lifetime Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scopes over which stored value preferences remain active.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistence Lifetime Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of persistent preferences by the events that erase or replace them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each variable \(x\), define its preference lifetime as an interval \([u,e)\) of search events, beginning at update event \(u\) and ending at the first expiration event \(e\). A node-local regime sets \(e\) at backtracking past the recording node; a restart-local regime sets \(e\) at the next restart; an epoch-local regime sets \(e\) at the next scheduled epoch boundary; and a run-persistent regime sets \(e=+\infty\), subject only to replacement by a later update. A preference may be consulted exactly during its lifetime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preference regimes differ by expiration event: leaving a node, restarting, ending an epoch, or ending the complete solver run.
assumptions_latex: Search events are totally ordered.
Each update records both a variable and a preferred value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The preference recorded at \(u\) is retained precisely for events \(t\) satisfying \(u\le t<e\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: event-based taxonomy captures common finite and run-persistent cache lifetimes
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the lifetime-regime leaf, but the four named regimes and their exact expiration semantics appear to be a proposed classification without cited support.

children.title: Preference-Staleness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which retained value preferences impede diversification or adaptation.

knowledge_statements.title: Preference-Staleness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary determining when a persistent value preference must no longer control selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose preference \(p(x)
eq\bot\) was recorded at event \(u(x)\), has lifetime limit \(L(x)\), and is evaluated at event \(t\). It is stale when \(t-u(x)>L(x)\), when \(p(x)\notin D_t(x)\), or when an invalidation predicate \(I_t(x,p(x))\) holds. The selection rule may reuse the preference only if none of these conditions holds. On staleness it must ignore or erase the preference and invoke its fallback selector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preference becomes stale after its lifetime, upon infeasibility, or when a declared invalidation test holds; stale preferences cannot determine the next value.
assumptions_latex: \(L(x)\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
\(I_t\) is a declared Boolean invalidation predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reuse is permitted exactly when \(t-u(x)\le L(x)\), \(p(x)\in D_t(x)\), and \(\neg I_t(x,p(x))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: supplies a precise operational formalization of preference staleness
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits the terminal container, but the record presents a particular age, infeasibility, and invalidation policy as an exact boundary. Infeasibility may be temporary after backtracking, so cited semantics are needed to justify treating it as staleness or erasing the preference.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Tie Breaking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic composition of ordered heuristic scores for selecting one admissible search choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be the finite nonempty set of admissible search choices and let \(s_1,\ldots,s_k:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be ordered scores, all interpreted as quantities to minimize. Initialize \(C_0=C\), and for \(j=1,\ldots,k\) set \(C_j=\{c\in C_{j-1}:s_j(c)=\min_{d\in C_{j-1}}s_j(d)\}\). If \(C_k\) contains several choices, apply a fixed final ordering and return its least element. Thus score \(s_{j+1}\) is consulted only among choices tied under every preceding score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successively retain choices minimizing each ordered score; later scores resolve only earlier ties, and a fixed ordering resolves any final tie.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and nonempty.
Each score \(s_j\) is defined on every choice in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned choice lexicographically minimizes \((s_1(c),\ldots,s_k(c))\) over \(c\in C\).

notation.meaning: choices surviving the first j tie-breaking levels

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite lexicographic minimization is the canonical formal model of hierarchical tie breaking
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm correctly formalizes hierarchical tie breaking as lexicographic minimization, and the mathematical statement is precise. No source with a specific locator establishes this formulation in the stated CP search-control context.

children.title: Online Score Adaptation
children.top_down_role: Search-time revision of heuristic scores using newly observed search behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Online Score Adaptation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental update of heuristic scores from observations generated during the current search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate \(c\), initialize a score \(q_0(c)\in\mathbb{R}\) and count \(n_0(c)=0\). After the search produces bounded feedback \(r_t(c)\) for each observed candidate \(c\in O_t\), choose a learning rate \(\alpha_t(c)\in(0,1]\) and update \(q_{t+1}(c)=(1-\alpha_t(c))q_t(c)+\alpha_t(c)r_t(c)\) and \(n_{t+1}(c)=n_t(c)+1\). Scores and counts of unobserved candidates remain unchanged. At the next decision, rank admissible candidates by the current score under the declared minimization or maximization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After each search observation, blend its feedback into the candidate’s current score; leave unobserved candidates unchanged and rank future choices by updated scores.
assumptions_latex: Each feedback value \(r_t(c)\) is finite.
Each learning rate satisfies \(0<\alpha_t(c)\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only candidates in \(O_t\) change score at event \(t\), according to the displayed convex update.

notation.meaning: online score of candidate c at event t
new search feedback for candidate c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exponential incremental scoring is a standard online adaptation mechanism
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits Online Score Adaptation, but exponential blending is only one possible online adaptation mechanism. A CP heuristic source is needed to support this particular update as the intended local concept.

children.title: Score Aging
children.top_down_role: Reduction of influence assigned to older heuristic evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Score Aging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential decay of accumulated heuristic evidence before incorporating new search events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_t(c)\) be the score of candidate \(c\) before event \(t\), and fix an aging factor \(\rho\in[0,1]\). First replace every retained score by \(\widetilde q_t(c)=\rho q_t(c)\). If event \(t\) contributes increment \(r_t(c)\) to candidate \(c\), set \(q_{t+1}(c)=\widetilde q_t(c)+r_t(c)\); otherwise set \(q_{t+1}(c)=\widetilde q_t(c)\). Consequently, an increment recorded \(j\) events earlier has current weight \(\rho^j\). Candidate ranking uses the resulting aged scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply old scores by a fixed decay factor before adding current evidence, so the influence of an observation decreases geometrically with age.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le\rho\le1\).
All score increments are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An increment of age \(j\) contributes its original magnitude multiplied by \(\rho^j\).

notation.meaning: score increment supplied at event t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: geometric decay is the standard mathematical form of score aging
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits Score Aging and the geometric-decay calculation is internally consistent. The per-event global-decay convention and its CP heuristic interpretation lack an inspectable citation.

children.title: Adaptation Timescales
children.top_down_role: Short-horizon, long-horizon, or mixed-timescale score adjustment.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptation Timescales
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative memory horizons induced by constant-rate online score updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the constant-rate update \(q_{t+1}=(1-\alpha)q_t+\alpha r_t\), with \(0<\alpha\le1\), define the retention factor \(\rho=1-\alpha\). The effective sample-size timescale is \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}=(1+\rho)/(1-\rho)=(2-\alpha)/\alpha\). For \(0<\rho<1\), the e-folding memory time is \(\tau_e=-1/\log\rho\), because feedback of age \(j\) has relative weight \(\rho^j\). At \(\alpha=1\), set \(\tau_e=0\): only the newest observation is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant learning rate determines geometric memory: smaller rates yield longer effective and e-folding horizons, while rate one retains only the newest feedback.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\alpha\le1\).
The update rate is constant across events.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Past feedback has weight proportional to \((1-\alpha)^j\), with timescales \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}=(2-\alpha)/\alpha\) and \(\tau_e=-1/\log(1-\alpha)\) when \(\alpha<1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formulas follow the standard exponentially weighted moving-average convention
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits Adaptation Timescales, and the formulas are consistent with normalized geometric weights. The meaning of effective sample-size timescale and its steady-state weighting convention require an authoritative source and explicit locator.

children.title: Aging-Rate Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Responsiveness and stability consequences of different score-aging intensities.

knowledge_statements.title: Aging-Rate Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact responsiveness–noise tradeoff for exponential score aging under stationary independent feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_t=\mu+\varepsilon_t\), where the errors are independent with mean zero and variance \(\sigma^2\), and let \(q_{t+1}=\rho q_t+(1-\rho)r_t\) with \(0\le\rho<1\). In stationarity, \(\mathbb{E}[q_t]=\mu\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(q_t)=\sigma^2(1-\rho)/(1+\rho)\). Hence increasing \(\rho\) reduces score variance but gives an observation of age \(j\) the larger relative weight \(\rho^j\), lengthening response to changes. Decreasing \(\rho\) increases responsiveness while admitting more observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slower aging smooths stationary noise but retains obsolete evidence longer; faster aging responds sooner but produces noisier scores.
assumptions_latex: \((\varepsilon_t)\) are independent with \(\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_t]=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_t)=\sigma^2<\infty\).
\(0\le\rho<1\), and the recursion is stationary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}(q_t)=\sigma^2(1-\rho)/(1+\rho)\), while age-\(j\) influence is proportional to \(\rho^j\).

notation.meaning: retention factor; larger values mean slower aging

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact stationary variance and geometric-memory formulas are standard for exponential smoothing
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property fits Aging-Rate Tradeoffs, and the stationary variance formula is correct under the stated independent-noise recursion. It nevertheless lacks a source supporting both the stochastic result and its application to CP heuristic scores.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled selection among several search heuristics during a single solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\{h_1,\ldots,h_m\}\) be deterministic search-choice heuristics and partition the search into epochs \(e=1,2,\ldots\). Maintain for each heuristic a statistic \(Q_e(h)\) and usage count \(N_e(h)\). At the start of epoch \(e\), a portfolio policy \(\pi\) selects \(h_e=\pi(Q_e,N_e,e)\). Use \(h_e\) for every choice in that epoch, observe a declared reward \(R_e\), update the selected heuristic’s statistics, and continue until failure, a solution, or a prescribed resource limit is reached. Output the solver’s terminal result.
