knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide search into epochs, select one heuristic per epoch from maintained performance statistics, update its statistics afterward, and stop at the solver’s terminal condition.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite and nonempty.
The epoch boundaries, reward, and policy \(\pi\) are fixed before execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each search choice is generated by exactly one selected heuristic \(h_e\in H\), and its epoch reward updates the portfolio state.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: epoch-based policy selection formalizes a standard online heuristic portfolio
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is suitable for Heuristic Portfolios, but it defines a specific epoch-based adaptive portfolio rather than the general concept. A cited CP portfolio source is needed for the epoch, reward, and update semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Modeler Search Annotations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Declarative metadata that constrains or prioritizes solver search without changing feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constraint model \(M\) with feasible set \(F(M)\), a search annotation is metadata \(A=(V,\prec,h_V,h_D,r)\), where \(V\) is an ordered or priority-partitioned subset of variables, \(\prec\) is a tie-breaking priority, \(h_V\) and \(h_D\) are variable- and value-selection rules, and \(r\) is an optional restart policy. The annotated solver may alter its search order using \(A\), but annotation semantics require \(F(M,A)=F(M)\). Thus annotations control enumeration strategy rather than model feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search annotation declares variable priorities, selection rules, or restart policy while leaving the model’s feasible set unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The underlying solver is complete under both annotated and unannotated search.
Annotations do not add, remove, or relax model constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(M,A)=F(M)\), although the order in which search states are explored may differ.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: declarative search annotations conventionally affect control rather than feasible-set semantics
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits Modeler Search Annotations and consistently treats annotations as search control. Solver-language documentation is required because annotation fields and feasible-set preservation are language-dependent; completeness alone does not establish the semantic equality.

knowledge_statements.title: Early-Mistake Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential search penalty caused by committing first to a deceptively preferred root branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(n\ge1\), consider a binary depth-first search tree with root choice \(x\in\{0,1\}\). Under \(x=0\), the remaining \(n\) binary choices form a complete subtree whose inconsistency is detected only at depth \(n\); under \(x=1\), propagation immediately completes a solution. A heuristic preferring \(x=0\) therefore visits all \(2^n\) leaves of the failing subtree before reaching the solution branch, whereas preferring \(x=1\) reaches a solution without exploring that subtree. Thus one erroneous early preference can induce exponential additional search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A wrong root preference can force exhaustive traversal of a failing binary subtree, while the opposite preference reaches a solution immediately.
assumptions_latex: Depth-first search exhausts the first branch before trying its sibling.
No propagation detects failure inside the \(x=0\) branch before depth \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The wrong first choice incurs at least \(2^n\) failing leaf visits, while the correct first choice avoids them.

notation.meaning: depth of the deceptive failing subtree

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit adversarial search-tree construction directly establishes the stated failure mechanism
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is the correct kind, and the abstract tree construction yields the stated exponential leaf-count gap. A source or explicit CP model construction is needed to establish that this adversarial tree behavior represents the intended propagation-guided CP failure phenomenon.

knowledge_statements.title: Deceptive Propagation Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a propagation-based score to predict the downstream search cost of a branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite set of search states, let \(B(s)\) be the admissible branches at \(s\), let \(q_s(b)\) be a score maximized by the heuristic, and let \(T_s(b)\) be the size of the completed subtree below branch \(b\). The score is deceptive at \(s\) if there exist \(b_1,b_2\in B(s)\) such that \(q_s(b_1)>q_s(b_2)\) but \(T_s(b_1)>T_s(b_2)\). It is uniformly deceptive on \(U\subseteq S\) with factor \(\rho>1\) if the selected branch \(b^*(s)\in\arg\max_{b\in B(s)}q_s(b)\) satisfies \(T_s(b^*(s))\geq \rho\min_{b\in B(s)}T_s(b)\) for every \(s\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation score is deceptive when it prefers a branch whose completed search subtree is larger than that of a lower-scored alternative.
assumptions_latex: \(B(s)\) is finite and nonempty for every state under consideration.
\(T_s(b)\) is measured under a fixed continuation and tie-breaking policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_s(b_1)>q_s(b_2)\) need not imply \(T_s(b_1)\leq T_s(b_2)\).

notation.meaning: Propagation-based score of branch b at state s.
Completed subtree size after taking branch b at state s.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the proposed deceptive-score and uniform-factor definitions are local constructions with no cited source establishing these exact criteria.

children.title: Score Nonstationarity
children.top_down_role: Changes in the relevance or distribution of heuristic scores across search regions or time.

knowledge_statements.title: Score Nonstationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporal instability of scores for branches that remain admissible during search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For search states \(s_t\) and persistent candidate branches \(P_t=B(s_t)\cap B(s_{t+1})\), a score family \(q_t\) is \(\varepsilon\)-nonstationary at time \(t\) if \(\max_{b\in P_t}|q_{t+1}(b)-q_t(b)|>\varepsilon\). It is persistently \(\varepsilon\)-nonstationary along an infinite search trajectory if this inequality holds for infinitely many \(t\). When scores are scale-dependent, replace \(q_t\) by a fixed normalization \(\widehat q_t\); otherwise rescaling alone can create apparent nonstationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scores are nonstationary when a still-available branch repeatedly receives materially different scores as the search state evolves.
assumptions_latex: \(P_t\neq\varnothing\) whenever nonstationarity is evaluated.
\(\varepsilon>0\), and one fixed score normalization is used across times.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent score variation prevents eventual numerical stabilization of all persistent candidates.

notation.meaning: Branches admissible at two consecutive search states.
Score assigned to branch b at time t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local formalization is uncited. Moreover, infinitely many maxima over changing persistent sets need not mean one branch repeatedly changes, so the plain statement and conclusion are stronger than the formula without additional finiteness or persistence assumptions.

children.title: Heuristic Thrashing
children.top_down_role: Repeated switching among competing heuristic preferences without sustained search progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Thrashing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated switching among heuristic choices without commensurate search progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b_t\in B(s_t)\) be the branch selected at time \(t\), and let \(p:S\to\mathbb R_{\geq0}\) be a monotone progress measure. A trajectory exhibits \((K,\delta)\)-heuristic thrashing on times \(t_0, t_0+K\) if \(b_{t+1}\neq b_t\) for every consecutive pair, at least one previously selected branch class recurs, and \(p(s_{t_0+K})-p(s_{t_0})\leq\delta\). Unbounded thrashing occurs when such intervals exist for arbitrarily large \(K\) with a fixed finite \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic thrashes when it repeatedly switches among recurring choices while making only bounded progress over increasingly long intervals.
assumptions_latex: \(K\geq2\) and \(\delta\geq0\).
Branch recurrence is measured using one fixed equivalence relation on choices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Arbitrarily long switching intervals may occur without unbounded growth of the chosen progress measure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but this uncited operational definition is not reliable as written: branch equality is used for switching while recurrence is separately defined through an unspecified equivalence relation, and the interval notation is ambiguous.

children.title: Ranking-Reversal Regimes
children.top_down_role: Search conditions producing frequent reversals in variable or value rankings.

knowledge_statements.title: Ranking-Reversal Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability in the relative ordering of persistent candidate branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_t\) score branches at search state \(s_t\). A pair of branches \(b,c\in B(s_t)\cap B(s_u)\) undergoes a ranking reversal between \(t<u\) if \((q_t(b)-q_t(c))(q_u(b)-q_u(c))<0\). A trajectory is in a persistent ranking-reversal regime if some persistent pair, or pairs drawn from a fixed finite candidate class, undergo reversals at infinitely many pairs of times. Such a regime can change the heuristic maximizer even when the admissible candidate set remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ranking reversal occurs when two still-available branches exchange score order; persistent reversals can repeatedly change the selected branch.
assumptions_latex: Scores are comparable across the two states.
Tied scores are excluded from a strict reversal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A strict reversal changes the pairwise preference relation between \(b\) and \(c\).

notation.meaning: Score of branch b at search time t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict pairwise-reversal formula is sound, but the proposed persistent-regime definition leaves the persistent-pair and time-pair quantifiers ambiguous and has no authoritative locator.

children.title: Stabilization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of damping, aging, or persistence controls used to contain unstable ranking behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient margin condition for eventual invariance of a heuristic choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a fixed finite candidate set and suppose \(q_t(b)\to q_\infty(b)\) uniformly over \(b\in B\). If \(b^*\) is the unique maximizer of \(q_\infty\) and \(\gamma=q_\infty(b^*)-\max_{b\in B\setminus\{b^*\}}q_\infty(b)>0\), then there exists \(t_0\) such that \(b^*\) is the unique maximizer of \(q_t\) for every \(t\geq t_0\). Thus uniform score error below \(\gamma/2\) is a stabilization boundary; without a positive limiting margin, convergence alone does not ensure a fixed maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly convergent scores eventually select the same branch when the limiting best branch has a strictly positive margin.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is finite and does not change with time.
\(q_t\to q_\infty\) uniformly on \(B\).
The limiting maximizer is unique with margin \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists t_0\,\forall t\geq t_0:\ \arg\max_{b\in B}q_t(b)=\{b^*\}.\)

notation.meaning: Limiting gap between the best and second-best candidates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-set argmax-stability claim is mathematically standard and precise, but the record states a theorem rather than merely a condition. No authoritative section, theorem, or page locator is supplied to support the claim or its intended container treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Induced Duplication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate search caused by branching without quotienting or breaking model symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act on assignments and preserve both feasibility and the objective value of a constraint optimization problem. Two search nodes \(u,v\) are symmetry-equivalent when their partial assignments satisfy \(v=g\cdot u\) for some \(g\in G\). A search exhibits symmetry-induced duplication if it expands two distinct equivalent nodes before either is eliminated by symmetry handling. In the worst case, if a node has trivial stabilizer, its orbit contains \(|G|\) equivalent nodes; an invariant branching and propagation scheme may therefore reproduce the same residual subproblem up to \(|G|\) times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model symmetries create duplicate search whenever distinct nodes in the same symmetry orbit are expanded without symmetry breaking or quotienting.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts on the assignment space.
Every \(g\in G\) preserves constraints and objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number of equivalent copies of node \(u\) is \(|G\cdot u|=|G|/|\operatorname{Stab}_G(u)|\).

notation.meaning: Orbit of search node u under the symmetry group.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Orbit–stabilizer supports the orbit-size formula, but it does not by itself establish that a particular invariant branching and propagation scheme expands every orbit member or reproduces a residual subproblem up to that multiplicity. A CP-symmetry source and precise algorithmic hypotheses are needed.

children.title: Failure-Directed Search Record Calculus
children.top_down_role: Classical failure-directed retraction and reusable records of failed partial assignments, ordered before SAT-style learning architectures.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Sections 4.4–4.5, Nogood Recording and Non-Chronological Backtracking
Survey taxonomy of explanations and nogoods

knowledge_statements.title: Backjumping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonchronological retraction from a failed search state to a designated earlier decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite ordered decision sequence \(d_1, d_k\), a failed state, and a sound failure explanation identifying a nonempty index set \(J\subseteq\{1, k\}\). Set \(j=\max J\), retract decisions \(d_j, d_k\), retain the prefix \(d_1, d_{j-1}\), and forbid the failed alternative at level \(j\). Propagate the retained prefix and continue with another admissible alternative at level \(j\). If no alternative remains, derive a new failure explanation and repeat; if \(J=\varnothing\), report global inconsistency. The jump is nonchronological when \(j<k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backjumping retracts directly to the latest decision implicated by a sound failure explanation, skipping later decisions not needed for that failure.
assumptions_latex: The decision sequence is finite and totally ordered.
Each failure explanation is sound for the current constraint store.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm removes the implicated suffix while preserving the earlier prefix; \(j<k\) yields a nonchronological jump.

notation.meaning: Decision made at search level i.
Indices implicated by the failure explanation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the index sequence and index set are malformed as \(d_1,d_k\) and \(\{1,k\}\), and the explanation-directed procedure may describe a particular backjumping variant rather than generic backjumping. A primary locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Directed Backjumping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backjumping whose destination is computed from accumulated conflict sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate with each decision variable \(x_i\) a conflict set \(C_i\) of earlier decision indices. Upon failure at level \(k\), form a sound conflict set \(C\subseteq\{1, k\}\). If \(C=\varnothing\), report inconsistency; otherwise set \(j=\max C\), retract all decisions after level \(j\), and record at level \(j\) the reduced explanation \(C\setminus\{j\}\), combined with any explanation already stored there. Reject the value or branch implicated at level \(j\), propagate, and continue. Repeating this rule directs each jump to the deepest decision occurring in the current conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict-directed backjumping jumps to the deepest decision in a sound conflict and transfers the remaining conflict information to that level.
assumptions_latex: Conflict sets contain only earlier or current decision indices.
Every recorded conflict is a sound explanation of failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For nonempty \(C\), the backjump destination is \(j=\max C\), and levels greater than \(j\) are skipped.

notation.meaning: Current set of decision levels jointly explaining failure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but \(C\subseteq\{1,k\}\) incorrectly denotes only two levels rather than the intended range. Conflict-set transfer and combination rules vary across formulations and require a primary source locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure-directed retraction that preserves later assignments independent of the retracted decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an ordered partial assignment \(A\) and, for each assigned variable, elimination explanations for rejected values. When every value of variable \(x\) is eliminated, combine the corresponding explanations into a conflict set \(C\). Choose the most recent assignment \(y=a\) occurring in \(C\), retract \(y=a\), and retain every later assignment whose justification does not depend on \(y=a\). Delete or recompute explanations invalidated by the retraction, record an explanation eliminating \(a\) for \(y\), propagate, and continue. If the combined conflict is empty, report inconsistency; a complete consistent assignment is returned as a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic backtracking retracts a culprit assignment while retaining later assignments whose explanations do not depend on it.
assumptions_latex: Domains and the variable set are finite.
Every value elimination has a sound explanation.
Invalidated explanations are removed or recomputed after retraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Assignments independent of the retracted decision remain in \(A\), while the failed value is eliminated by a recorded explanation.

notation.meaning: Combined conflict explaining a domain wipeout.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Dynamic backtracking is correctly treated as an algorithm, but the precise conflict construction, culprit selection, retention criterion, and explanation-update rules require verification against a primary formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Order Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retraction governed by explicit dependency order rather than decision chronology alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain active decisions \(D\) and a directed acyclic dependency relation \(\prec\), where \(d_i\prec d_j\) means that the validity or justification of \(d_j\) depends on \(d_i\). Given a sound conflict \(C\subseteq D\), choose a culprit \(c\in C\), retract \(c\) and every active decision reachable from \(c\) in \(\prec\), but retain decisions incomparable with and independent of \(c\). Remove invalidated dependency edges and explanations, forbid the failed alternative for \(c\), propagate, and resume search from any linear extension of the remaining partial order. An empty conflict certifies inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial-order backtracking retracts a conflicting decision and its dependents while retaining decisions independent under an explicit dependency order.
assumptions_latex: \((D,\prec)\) is a finite directed acyclic dependency structure.
Conflict and dependency explanations are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only \(c\) and its dependency descendants must be retracted; independent active decisions may be retained.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but partial-order backtracking has multiple formulations. Soundness of retracting exactly a culprit and its dependency descendants, retaining all independent decisions, and resuming from any linear extension depends on operational details not supplied here.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment Nogoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nogoods represented as forbidden conjunctions of variable-value assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite set of variables with domains \(D_x\). An assignment nogood is a finite set \(N=\{x_1=a_1, x_m=a_m\}\), with distinct \(x_i\in X\) and \(a_i\in D_{x_i}\), such that no feasible total assignment extends all members of \(N\). Operationally it is the constraint \(\neg\bigwedge_{i=1}^m(x_i=a_i)\), equivalently \(\bigvee_{i=1}^m(x_i\neq a_i)\). A partial assignment violates \(N\) exactly when it contains every assignment in \(N\); if all but one member hold, the remaining member is forbidden.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assignment nogood forbids a finite combination of variable-value assignments that cannot occur together in any feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: Each variable \(x\in X\) has a specified domain \(D_x\).
The nogood is sound for the original constraints or the current valid search context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\) is equivalent to the disjunction \(\bigvee_{i=1}^m(x_i\neq a_i)\).

notation.meaning: Forbidden set of simultaneous variable-value assignments.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role and logical equivalence are standard, but \(N=\{x_1=a_1,x_m=a_m\}\) omits the intended intermediate members. The distinction between globally valid nogoods and context-dependent nogoods also needs an authoritative locator and precise scope.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Constraint Nogoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nogoods expressed over general branching constraints rather than only value assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be the base constraint system and let \(\ell_1, \ell_m\) be branching constraints, each interpreted as a predicate on complete assignments. A branching-constraint nogood is a finite set \(N=\{\ell_1, \ell_m\}\) satisfying \(F\models
eg(\ell_1\land\cdots\land\ell_m)\). It is represented by the valid constraint \(
eg igwedge_{i=1}^m\ell_i\), equivalently \( igvee_{i=1}^m
eg\ell_i\). The representation includes assignment nogoods as the special case \(\ell_i\equiv(x_i=a_i)\), while permitting bounds, disequalities, or other branch predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching-constraint nogood forbids an infeasible conjunction of branch predicates, generalizing nogoods made solely from variable assignments.
assumptions_latex: All branch predicates are interpreted over one common assignment space.
\(F\) logically entails that their conjunction is impossible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models\bigvee_{i=1}^m\neg\ell_i\).

notation.meaning: A branching constraint or branch predicate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role is plausible, but \(\ell_1,\ell_m\) and \(N=\{\ell_1,\ell_m\}\) omit the intended indexed sequence. The exact term and generalized branch-predicate formulation require a relevant authoritative source.

children.title: Generalized Nogoods
children.top_down_role: Nogood representations extending beyond simple forbidden complete assignment tuples.

assumptions_latex: A finite-domain constraint satisfaction problem has variable set \(V\), domains \((D_x)_{x\in V}\), and solution set \(F\subseteq\prod_{x\in V}D_x\).
Each predicate \(p_i\) has a specified scope and is evaluable on complete assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recording \(N\) permits every complete assignment satisfying all predicates in \(N\) to be rejected without removing any feasible assignment.

notation.meaning: Finite family of predicates forming the nogood

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic definition allowing arbitrary finite-scope predicates as nogood atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A generalized nogood is a finite family \(N=\{p_1,\ldots,p_m\}\) of predicates such that their simultaneous satisfaction is inconsistent with feasibility:
\[
F\cap\{a: p_i(a)=\mathrm{true}\text{ for every }i=1,\ldots,m\}=\varnothing.
\]
A partial assignment \(s\) violates \(N\) when every \(p_i\) is already entailed by \(s\). Equivalently, the learned constraint associated with \(N\) is
\[
\neg\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m}p_i,
\]
which is valid for every member of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized nogood is a finite conjunction of predicates that no feasible complete assignment can satisfy simultaneously; its negation is therefore a valid learned constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Nogoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic formulation is coherent and fits the definition container, but no inspectable CP source supports this particular generalized-nogood terminology or the partial-assignment violation convention.

children.title: Signed Nogoods
children.top_down_role: Nogood representations distinguishing positive from negative assignment information.

assumptions_latex: Every variable \(x\) has a finite domain \(D_x\).
The solution set is \(F\subseteq\prod_x D_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The signed nogood is equivalent to the valid constraint \(\bigvee_{i=1}^{m}(x_i\notin S_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain set-membership form of signed nogoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A signed literal is a domain-membership assertion \([x\in S]\), where \(x\) is a variable and \(\varnothing\ne S\subseteq D_x\); its complement is \([x\notin S]\). A signed nogood is a finite set
\[
N=\{[x_1\in S_1],\ldots,[x_m\in S_m]\}
\]
satisfying
\[
F\cap\{a:a(x_i)\in S_i\text{ for all }i\}=\varnothing.
\]
Thus no feasible assignment may make all its signed literals true, and the associated learned constraint is \(\bigvee_{i=1}^{m}[x_i\notin S_i]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A signed nogood forbids the simultaneous truth of finitely many domain-membership literals and is represented by the disjunction of their complements.
knowledge_statements.title: Signed Nogoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-membership formulation is internally consistent and definition-shaped, but signed-literal conventions vary and no authoritative source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Signed Generalization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representational overlap between generalized conditions and signed literals.

assumptions_latex: A valid signed nogood is \(N=\{[x_i\in S_i]:i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
For each \(i\), choose \(T_i\) with \(S_i\subseteq T_i\subseteq D_{x_i}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(S_i\) by \(T_i\) is sound exactly when \(F\cap\{a:a(x_i)\in T_i\ \forall i\}=\varnothing\); shrinking signed sets is always sound but weakens the nogood.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact soundness criterion for weakening signed literals by enlarging their value sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(N'=\{[x_i\in T_i]:i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Because each \(T_i\) contains \(S_i\), the conjunction represented by \(N'\) covers at least the assignments covered by \(N\), so \(N'\) is a stronger exclusion. This signed generalization is sound if and only if
\[
F\cap\{a:a(x_i)\in T_i\text{ for every }i\}=\varnothing.
\]
By contrast, replacing any \(S_i\) by a subset or deleting values from it preserves soundness automatically, but yields a weaker exclusion. Literal deletion also requires the displayed infeasibility test for the remaining conjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging signed value sets strengthens a nogood and requires an infeasibility check; shrinking them is automatically sound but weakens propagation.
knowledge_statements.title: Signed Generalization Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The enlargement and shrinking claims follow the stated semantics and fit a condition container, but the intended published signed-generalization regime and terminology cannot be verified without a source.

children.title: Representation-Strength Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on compactness, reuse, or propagation strength for generalized or signed records.

assumptions_latex: Representations use only the original Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\).
A clausal representation must have exactly the same satisfying assignments as the represented constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Native generalized nogoods can be exponentially more succinct than clausal nogoods over the original variables.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Succinctness boundary for clauses without auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
P_n=\left\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\equiv1\pmod 2\right\}.
\]
The relation \(P_n\) has a single native parity-constraint representation. Any conjunctive normal form over only \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) whose models are exactly \(P_n\) requires \(2^{n-1}\) clauses: every even-parity assignment must be excluded, and no clause excluding two distinct even assignments can remain valid on all odd assignments. Hence bounded-width or polynomially many original-variable clauses cannot represent this generalized nogood family exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Odd parity has a one-constraint native representation but requires exponentially many clauses when auxiliary variables are forbidden, marking a strict succinctness boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Strength Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The original-variable parity example is an appropriate representation-strength boundary, but its exact 2^(n-1)-clause lower bound is a nontrivial claim requiring an authoritative locator.

children.title: Clausal Nogoods
children.top_down_role: Nogoods represented through clause-compatible literal structures.

assumptions_latex: The variables are Boolean.
A literal is either \(x\) or \(\neg x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The clause \(C_N\) excludes exactly the simultaneous assignment recorded by \(N\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of simultaneously forbidden literals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean clausal form of a recorded nogood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A clausal nogood is a finite set of Boolean literals \(N=\{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m\}\) whose conjunction is infeasible. Its clausal representation is
\[
C_N=\neg\ell_1\vee\cdots\vee\neg\ell_m.
\]
For every total Boolean assignment \(a\), \(a\) violates \(C_N\) if and only if \(a\models\ell_i\) for every \(i\). If the conjunction \(\bigwedge_i\ell_i\) has no feasible extension, then \(C_N\) is valid for all feasible assignments and can be recorded as a learned clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clausal nogood negates a forbidden conjunction of Boolean literals, producing a clause violated exactly when all recorded literals hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Clausal Nogoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Boolean clause–nogood correspondence is mathematically standard, precise, and appropriate as a definition, but the record supplies neither a citation nor a specific locator.

children.title: Nonclausal Nogoods
children.top_down_role: Nogoods retained in native structures not restricted to clause form.

assumptions_latex: A constraint satisfaction problem has feasible set \(F\).
The native constraint language contains a relation \(R\) not required to be a clause.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint \(R(z)\) is a sound recorded nogood precisely when every feasible assignment satisfies it.

notation.meaning: Tuple of variables in the constraint scope
Native relation used as a learned constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic definition covering learned constraints outside disjunctive clause form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonclausal nogood is a learned native constraint \(R(z)\) whose relation is not represented as a single disjunction of literals and which excludes a search region proved infeasible. Soundness requires
\[
F\subseteq\{a:R(a|_z)=\mathrm{true}\}.
\]
Its forbidden region is therefore \(\{a:R(a|_z)=\mathrm{false}\}\), which must contain no feasible complete assignment. Examples of admissible forms include cardinality, linear, table, and parity constraints, provided the solver supplies semantics and propagation for the chosen native relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonclausal nogood is any valid learned native constraint, such as a cardinality or table constraint, that excludes only infeasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonclausal Nogoods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity condition is coherent, but treating every valid learned native constraint as a nonclausal nogood is terminology-dependent and needs authoritative CP support.

children.title: Clausalization Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Compactness, propagation, and integration consequences of translating native nogoods into clauses.

assumptions_latex: A Boolean formula \(\varphi\) is represented by a syntax circuit with \(s\) connective occurrences.
Fresh Boolean variables may name internal circuit nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Clausalization can be linear and projection-equivalent with auxiliaries, while forbidding auxiliaries can cause exponential growth and different propagation behavior.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size and propagation tradeoff of auxiliary-variable clausalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Tseitin-style encoding introduces one auxiliary variable for each internal node and produces a conjunctive normal form \(T_\varphi(x,y)\) of size \(O(s)\) such that
\[
\varphi(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y\,T_\varphi(x,y).
\]
Thus clausalization preserves the solutions projected onto \(x\), but it enlarges the search state and unit propagation acts through the selected encoding. Requiring an equivalent conjunctive normal form over \(x\) alone may require exponentially many clauses. Consequently, representation size and propagation strength must be assessed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary variables permit linear-size clausalization preserving projected solutions, but alter propagation and search state; original-variable clausalization may be exponentially large.
knowledge_statements.title: Clausalization Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation tradeoff fits the container, but the linear-size Tseitin claim, projection equivalence, exponential original-variable boundary, and propagation qualification require an inspectable SAT source.

children.title: Native-Form Integration Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Solver-interface limits affecting storage or use of nonclausal nogoods.

assumptions_latex: A native learned constraint \(R(z)\) is valid for every feasible assignment.
The solver exposes a propagator \(P_R\) for \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Native-form integration is sound under contracting and solution-preserving propagation, but explanation-based learning additionally requires sound explanations for every propagated deletion and failure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between semantic validity, propagation support, and explainability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Native integration requires \(P_R(D)\subseteq D\) and solution preservation:
\[
\{a\in D:R(a|_z)\}\;=\;\{a\in P_R(D):R(a|_z)\}.
\]
A detected failure is admissible only when the left-hand set is empty. In a solver requiring clausal or signed explanations, every deletion \(x\ne v\) made by \(P_R\) must also be accompanied by an accepted explanation \(E\) satisfying
\[
R\wedge E\models x\ne v.
\]
Without such explanations, the native constraint may be used for sound pruning but cannot safely participate in the solver's explanation-dependent conflict analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A native nogood needs a sound contracting propagator; participation in explanation-based conflict learning additionally requires valid explanations for every deletion and failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Native-Form Integration Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is appropriately a condition record, but the propagation equality treats domain stores as assignment sets without defining that interpretation, and the explanation contract is solver-dependent; a source is needed to fix the exact formal version.

assumptions_latex: Every learned nogood is valid for all feasible assignments.
The search procedure is otherwise a sound finite-domain backtracking search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime preserves completeness and prevents recurrence of every retained forbidden conjunction, although the database may grow without a finite a priori bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent recording without size, relevance, or deletion limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\mathcal N=\varnothing\). Whenever propagation or conflict analysis derives a valid nogood \(N\), update
\[
\mathcal N\leftarrow\mathcal N\cup\{N\},
\]
retain every member for the remainder of search, and propagate the original constraints together with all constraints represented by \(\mathcal N\). Stop when a feasible complete assignment is found, when exhaustive search proves infeasibility, or when an externally specified enumeration objective is met. The output is the search result together with the accumulated database \(\mathcal N\). No learned nogood is rejected or deleted because of size, age, or current relevance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unrestricted recording permanently stores and propagates every sound learned nogood, preserving completeness but allowing an unbounded database.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrestricted Nogood Recording

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches unrestricted persistent recording, but its completeness and recurrence-prevention claims need an authoritative CP search reference with a specific locator.

assumptions_latex: A positive integer size limit \(k\) is fixed.
The size \(|N|\) is the number of atomic predicates in nogood \(N\).
Every admitted nogood is valid for all feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy stores only nogoods of size at most \(k\); omitting larger valid nogoods affects pruning but not search soundness or completeness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admission policy bounded by the number of nogood atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\mathcal N=\varnothing\). On deriving a valid nogood \(N\), apply
\[
\mathcal N\leftarrow
\begin{cases}
\mathcal N\cup\{N\},&|N|\le k,\\
\mathcal N,&|N|>k.
\end{cases}
\]
Propagate every admitted nogood during subsequent search. Terminate under the underlying solver's ordinary solution, infeasibility, or enumeration stopping rule, and return that result with \(\mathcal N\). Because rejected nogoods are logical consequences rather than required original constraints, their omission cannot create a false solution when final solutions are checked against the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Size-bounded recording admits a valid nogood only when its atom count is at most a fixed threshold, trading pruning power for database control.
knowledge_statements.title: Size-Bounded Nogood Recording

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The admission rule is a clear size-bounded algorithm, but the completeness claim depends on the underlying search and final-solution checking assumptions and lacks an authoritative locator.

assumptions_latex: A current partial assignment \(s\) and a nonnegative threshold \(k\) are given.
Each recorded nogood is a finite conjunction of literals.
All recorded nogoods are valid for every feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only nogoods with at most \(k\) currently undecided literals remain active; deactivation changes pruning strength but not correctness.

notation.meaning: Number of literals in the nogood undecided by the current assignment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One explicit undecided-literal relevance policy; published conventions vary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nogood \(N\), define
\[
r_s(N)=|\{\ell\in N:s\text{ neither entails nor refutes }\ell\}|.
\]
At each search state, activate
\[
\mathcal A_s=\{N:r_s(N)\le k\}
\]
and run nogood propagation only on \(\mathcal A_s\). A newly learned valid nogood is stored, after which its activity is determined by the same rule. Recompute or incrementally update activity after assignment and backtracking. Stop according to the underlying complete search procedure and return its result; inactive nogoods remain logical consequences and may be reactivated when their relevance changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This relevance-bounded policy propagates only nogoods having at most a fixed number of currently undecided literals, while retaining correctness of the underlying search.
knowledge_statements.title: Relevance-Bounded Learning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed active-set algorithm is internally defined, but it may not match the established relevance-bounded learning measure; the exact metric and reactivation policy require an authoritative definition.

children.title: Subsumption Control
children.top_down_role: Management of nogoods made unnecessary by stronger covering records.

assumptions_latex: Nogoods \(N_1\) and \(N_2\) are conjunctions of literals under identical literal semantics.
Both nogoods are valid for all feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(N_1\subseteq N_2\), retaining \(N_2\) adds no forbidden assignment or unit consequence beyond those supplied by \(N_1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion subsumption for conjunctive literal nogoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Nogood \(N_1\) subsumes \(N_2\) when \(N_1\subseteq N_2\). Every assignment satisfying all literals of \(N_2\) then satisfies all literals of \(N_1\), so the forbidden region of \(N_2\) is contained in that of \(N_1\). Equivalently, for the corresponding clauses,
\[
C_{N_1}=\bigvee_{\ell\in N_1}\neg\ell
\quad\text{and}\quad
C_{N_2}=\bigvee_{\ell\in N_2}\neg\ell,
\qquad C_{N_1}\models C_{N_2}.
\]
Therefore a database may reject or delete \(N_2\) whenever \(N_1\) is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nogood subsumes any nogood containing all its literals; the larger nogood is redundant and may be omitted while the smaller remains stored.
knowledge_statements.title: Subsumption Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Set-inclusion subsumption and clause entailment are coherent and fit the property container, but the stronger claim about adding no unit consequence requires a SAT/CP source and explicit propagation semantics.

children.title: Redundancy Control
children.top_down_role: Management of duplicate or otherwise unnecessary learned records beyond direct subsumption.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic preservation criterion for adding or deleting recorded nogoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the current constraint store and \(R\) the recorded nogoods, each interpreted as a constraint. A candidate nogood \(N\) is redundant when \(F\land\bigwedge R\models N\). Rejecting such an \(N\) preserves the feasible assignments. Likewise, a stored nogood \(M\in R\) may be deleted whenever \(F\land\bigwedge(R\setminus\{M\})\models M\), because then \[\operatorname{Sol}\!\left(F\land\bigwedge R\right)=\operatorname{Sol}\!\left(F\land\bigwedge(R\setminus\{M\})\right).\] Syntactic tests such as subsumption are sufficient but not necessary implementations of this semantic criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nogood may be rejected or deleted when the remaining constraints imply it; this preserves exactly the feasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and all members of \(R\) have a common assignment semantics.
Entailment is evaluated relative to the permanent constraint store \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land\bigwedge(R\setminus\{M\})\models M\Longrightarrow \operatorname{Sol}(F\land\bigwedge R)=\operatorname{Sol}(F\land\bigwedge(R\setminus\{M\}))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: logical entailment immediately gives solution-set preservation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic entailment criterion and solution-set preservation claim are mathematically sound and fit the leaf, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Online Redundancy Screening
children.top_down_role: Redundancy checks performed during recording, propagation, or database maintenance.

knowledge_statements.title: Online Redundancy Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental screening performed when each candidate nogood is generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a constraint store \(F\), retained nogoods \(R\), and a stream \((N_t)_{t\geq1}\) of candidate nogoods. Initialize \(R_0=R\). At time \(t\), test a sound redundancy predicate \(Q(F,R_{t-1},N_t)\). If it returns true, set \(R_t=R_{t-1}\); otherwise set \(R_t=R_{t-1}\cup\{N_t\}\) and install \(N_t\) for propagation. A sound predicate must satisfy \[Q(F,R,N)=\mathsf{true}\Longrightarrow F\land\bigwedge R\models N.\] On termination, output the retained set and the unchanged feasible solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test each generated nogood immediately; discard it only when a sound test establishes that the current store already implies it.
assumptions_latex: Each candidate \(N_t\) is valid for the original constraint model.
The predicate \(Q\) has no false positive redundancy decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(F\land\bigwedge R_t)=\operatorname{Sol}(F\land\bigwedge R\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^{t}N_i)\) for every \(t\).

notation.meaning: candidate nogood generated at time t
nogoods retained after screening time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incremental application of a sound entailment screen preserves solutions inductively
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The online algorithm and its inductive preservation invariant are coherent, but the record has no inspectable citation supporting this screening regime.

children.title: Screening-Cost Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where detecting removable records costs more than their continued retention.

knowledge_statements.title: Screening-Cost Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case boundary for exact semantic screening of Boolean clausal nogoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean CNF \(F\) and a candidate clause \(C\), exact redundancy screening asks whether \(F\models C\). This holds exactly when \(F\land\neg C\) is unsatisfiable. Consequently, exact clause-redundancy screening is coNP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions: membership follows from a falsifying assignment certificate for non-entailment, and hardness includes testing whether a CNF \(F\) entails the empty clause. By contrast, determining whether some stored clause syntactically subsumes \(C\) can be implemented in time linear in the total inspected literal occurrences using suitable set representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact semantic clause screening is coNP-complete, whereas syntactic subsumption screening can be linear in the inspected clause data.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite Boolean CNF formula.
\(C\) is a Boolean clause, with the empty clause permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models C\Longleftrightarrow F\land\neg C\text{ is unsatisfiable}\), and deciding this relation is coNP-complete.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: CNF entailment reduces exactly to unsatisfiability
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entailment-to-unsatisfiability equivalence and coNP-completeness claim are standard, but the complexity result and subsumption-cost comparison require an authoritative source with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation–Backjumping Overlap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for redundant immediate pruning after a conflict-directed backjump.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a learned clause \(L\) have backjump level \(b\), and let \(A_b\) be the literals retained after removing decisions above \(b\). Let \(\mathcal P_F(A_b)\) denote propagation to a fixpoint using the pre-existing store \(F\), without \(L\). If \(L\) is asserting at level \(b\) with asserting literal \(\ell\), propagation and backjumping overlap precisely in their immediate effect when \[\ell\in\mathcal P_F(A_b).\] In that case installing \(L\) performs no additional immediate domain reduction at the backjump state, although \(L\) may still prune later search states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlap occurs when ordinary propagation after the backjump already derives the learned clause’s asserting literal, so the clause adds no immediate pruning.
assumptions_latex: Propagation under \(F\) reaches a deterministic fixpoint.
The learned clause \(L\) is asserting after backjumping to level \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell\in\mathcal P_F(A_b)\Longrightarrow \mathcal P_{F\land L}(A_b)=\mathcal P_F(A_b)\).

notation.meaning: assignment retained at backjump level b
fixpoint propagation operator for store F
asserting literal of the learned clause

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equality follows when the only new asserting consequence is already in the propagation closure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sufficient condition for no additional immediate pruning is plausible, but the word “precisely” depends on the exact propagation and overlap definitions. A source is needed to establish the claimed equivalence in this local sense.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Ordering Dependency Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of search-dependent explanation arcs to remain invariant under dynamic ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Search-dependent explanation arcs need not survive a change of decision order. For Boolean variables constrained by \(x=y\), deciding \(x=0\) first permits the propagation explanation \(x=0\Rightarrow y=0\), producing an arc from \(x\) to \(y\). Deciding \(y=0\) first instead permits \(y=0\Rightarrow x=0\), producing the reverse arc. Thus the directed dependency graph extracted from recorded propagation events is not generally an invariant of the constraint model. Any backjump or learning rule using arc orientation must therefore use the graph associated with the actual search history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic decision ordering can reverse explanation dependencies, so a history-derived directed dependency graph cannot safely be treated as model-invariant.
assumptions_latex: Propagation enforces the equality constraint \(x=y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{x\text{-first}}\neq G_{y\text{-first}}\) in general, even for the same constraint model.

notation.meaning: explanation dependency graph when x is decided first
explanation dependency graph when y is decided first

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the two-variable equality example directly exhibits order-dependent arc reversal
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality example correctly exhibits history-dependent reversal of explanation arcs and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but no inspectable source is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Nogood Memory Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case number of distinct Boolean clausal nogoods retained without deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) Boolean variables, a non-tautological clause contains, for each variable, either its positive literal, its negative literal, or neither, but not both. Hence there are exactly \(3^n\) such clauses when the empty clause is included, and \(3^n-1\) nonempty ones. A learning procedure that records distinct nonempty clauses and never deletes any therefore uses at most \(3^n-1\) clause records, but this bound is exponential and cannot be replaced by a polynomial bound without additional restrictions on learning, clause width, or deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without deletion, distinct Boolean clause records can grow exponentially: up to three choices per variable, excluding the empty clause if it is not stored.
assumptions_latex: There are exactly \(n\) Boolean variables.
Only distinct, non-tautological, nonempty clauses are retained.
No learned clause is deleted.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct enumeration by positive, negative, or absent status for each variable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The count of distinct non-tautological clauses is correct. However, the assertion that no polynomial worst-case bound is possible requires a realizable learning-growth construction or cited lower-bound result, not merely the counting upper bound.

children.title: Explanation-Based Constraint Learning
children.top_down_role: Reason-producing propagation and conflict analysis within CP; general SAT/CDCL theory and formal proof systems remain in their owning chapters.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entailment certificate explaining why the current propagated state is inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the permanent constraint store and \(A\) the currently active decision and propagation literals. A failure explanation is a finite set \(E\subseteq A\) satisfying \[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\bot.\] Equivalently, the conjunction of \(F\) and the literals in \(E\) is unsatisfiable. The learned nogood \(\neg\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\), or its clausal form \(\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e\), is therefore valid for every solution of \(F\). Inclusion-minimality of \(E\) is desirable but is not required for certificate validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A failure explanation is a subset of active literals whose conjunction with the model is inconsistent; negating that conjunction yields a valid nogood.
assumptions_latex: All literals in \(A\) are active in the failed search state.
Entailment is interpreted in the model's constraint semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\bot\Longrightarrow F\models\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: logical conflict explanations are unsatisfiable antecedent sets whose negations are entailed nogoods
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entailment certificate and resulting valid nogood are precise, and certificate is an appropriate content kind, but the record lacks an inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entailment certificate for one literal inferred by a propagator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the permanent constraint store, \(A\) the literals true before a propagation event, and \(\ell\notin A\) the inferred literal. A propagation explanation for \(\ell\) is a finite set \(E\subseteq A\) such that \[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\ell.\] It certifies the implication \(\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\Rightarrow\ell\), equivalently the valid clause \(\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e\lor\ell\). The explanation is sound independently of whether it is inclusion-minimal; minimization affects strength and processing cost, not validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation explanation is a set of previously true literals that, together with the model, entails the newly inferred literal.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(E\) was true before \(\ell\) was propagated.
The constraint semantics used for entailment matches the propagator's semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\ell\Longrightarrow F\models\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e\lor\ell\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: implication explanations are entailment certificates for propagated literals

children.title: Eager Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations produced or retained when the associated propagation event occurs.

knowledge_statements.title: Eager Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explanation materialization at the time each propagation occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a propagating constraint solver with store \(F\). Whenever a propagator infers a literal \(\ell\) from the current active literals \(A\), immediately compute and store a set \(E_\ell\subseteq A\) satisfying \(F\land\bigwedge E_\ell\models\ell\), together with the inference record for \(\ell\). If propagation derives a conflict, traverse the stored explanations to construct a failure explanation or learned nogood. Stop according to the host search procedure and output its solution, infeasibility result, or bound together with any retained learned constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute and store every propagation explanation immediately, making later conflict analysis independent of reconstructing past propagator states.
assumptions_latex: Each propagator can produce a sound explanation when it performs an inference.
Stored antecedent literals remain identifiable during later conflict analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall\ell\text{ propagated},\;F\land\bigwedge E_\ell\models\ell\).

notation.meaning: active literals immediately before an inference
stored eager explanation for inferred literal l

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: eager explanation timing materializes a sound antecedent set at inference time
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The procedure accurately describes eager explanation materialization and algorithm is a suitable role for the operational statement, but no inspectable source supports the timing regime.

children.title: Lazy Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations reconstructed or requested only when later analysis needs them.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deferred explanation construction from a replayable propagation record.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a propagating solver with store \(F\). When a propagator infers \(\ell\), store a compact recipe \(r_\ell\) identifying the propagator and sufficient antecedent-state information, but do not materialize an explanation. If conflict analysis later requests \(\ell\)'s antecedents, invoke a reconstruction map \(\mathcal R(r_\ell)=E_\ell\) and require \(F\land\bigwedge E_\ell\models\ell\). Cache \(E_\ell\) optionally, continue conflict analysis, and terminate according to the host search procedure. Soundness requires every requested recipe to remain reconstructible after backtracking and state mutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Record a replayable recipe at propagation time and construct the actual explanation only if later conflict analysis requests it.
assumptions_latex: Every retained recipe contains enough immutable information for sound reconstruction.
Reconstruction is available whenever conflict analysis requests an antecedent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R(r_\ell)=E_\ell\Longrightarrow F\land\bigwedge E_\ell\models\ell\).

notation.meaning: deferred explanation recipe for inferred literal l

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: lazy timing defers materialization while preserving an entailment-producing reconstruction recipe
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deferred reconstruction algorithm is internally coherent and states the necessary availability assumption, but it lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Hybrid Explanation Timing
children.top_down_role: Selective combinations of eager production and deferred reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Explanation Timing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-inference choice between eager materialization and lazy reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a propagating solver, store \(F\), and a timing policy \(h\). For each inferred literal \(\ell\), evaluate \(h(\ell,A,p)\), where \(A\) is the antecedent state and \(p\) the responsible propagator. If the result is eager, store an explanation \(E_\ell\subseteq A\) with \(F\land\bigwedge E_\ell\models\ell\). If it is lazy, store a recipe \(r_\ell\) whose reconstruction later returns such an \(E_\ell\). During conflict analysis, use stored eager explanations and reconstruct requested lazy ones. Output follows the host search stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy chooses eager storage or a lazy reconstruction recipe for each inference; every explanation eventually used must certify the inference.
assumptions_latex: The eager explanation generator is sound.
Every lazy recipe selected by \(h\) remains reconstructible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall\ell\text{ used in analysis},\;F\land\bigwedge E_\ell\models\ell\), regardless of the timing selected by \(h\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hybrid timing composes eager materialization and sound deferred reconstruction on a per-inference basis
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The per-inference composition of eager and lazy timing is coherent and fits an algorithmic leaf, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Reconstruction-Availability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where deferred explanations become costly, unavailable, or weaker than retained explanations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction-Availability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary determining whether deferred explanations can be reconstructed soundly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\) be the information retained for a deferred inference of \(\ell\), and let \(\sigma\) denote the antecedent state at inference time. Sound reconstruction from \(r\) alone is impossible if there exist states \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2\) with the same record, \(r(\sigma_1)=r(\sigma_2)\), such that \(F\land\sigma_1\models\ell\) but \(F\land\sigma_2\not\models\ell\). Therefore a lazy regime must retain enough immutable information to distinguish all states relevant to entailment, or preserve a replayable snapshot; a propagator identifier without adequate antecedent-state data is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lazy reconstruction fails when one retained record represents two past states that disagree on whether the propagated literal follows.
assumptions_latex: Reconstruction receives only the retained record \(r\) and immutable model \(F\).
The same reconstructed explanation would be returned for equal records.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(\sigma_1)=r(\sigma_2)\land F\land\sigma_1\models\ell\land F\land\sigma_2\not\models\ell\Longrightarrow\text{no sound total reconstruction from }r\text{ alone exists}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: indistinguishable records cannot support different entailment-correct reconstructions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indistinguishable-record argument fits the reconstruction failure boundary, but the impossibility statement requires a cited formal treatment or a source establishing the relevant reconstruction-information condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Constraint Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical explanations emitted by a sound propagator for a global constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a global constraint, let \(A\) be a finite set of currently true literals, and let \(p\) be a propagated literal. The set \(A\) is an explanation of the propagation when \[C\land\bigwedge_{a\in A}a\models p.\] It is an explanation of failure when \[C\land\bigwedge_{a\in A}a\models\bot.\] Thus the explanation records sufficient logical premises, rather than the internal filtering steps of the global-constraint propagator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global-constraint explanation is a set of current literals that, together with the constraint, logically entails a propagation or inconsistency.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) has fixed semantics over the variables represented by the literals.
Every literal in \(A\) is true in the current search state.
The propagator is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\land\bigwedge_{a\in A}a\models p\quad\text{or}\quad C\land\bigwedge_{a\in A}a\models\bot
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard logical definition of a propagation or failure explanation
No supplied locator specifically supports explanations for global-constraint propagation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent, variables are introduced, the content kind fits the leaf, and all TeX commands in statement_latex are delimited. However, no cited source or inspectable locator supports the CP-specific interpretation of propagation and failure explanations for global constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion-based computation of a subset-minimal explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a sound explanation \(A\) for consequence \(p\) under constraint theory \(T\). Initialize \(E\leftarrow A\). For each \(a\in E\), query whether \[T\land\bigwedge_{e\in E\setminus\{a\}}e\models p.\] If the entailment holds, replace \(E\) by \(E\setminus\{a\}\); otherwise retain \(a\). After every remaining literal has been tested against the current set, output \(E\). The result is subset-minimal: no single remaining literal can be deleted while preserving the explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly delete any premise whose removal preserves entailment. The output is subset-minimal, though not necessarily minimum-cardinality.
assumptions_latex: \(T\land\bigwedge_{a\in A}a\models p\).
Each entailment query is exact.
Deleted literals are never reintroduced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models p\quad\land\quad\forall e\in E:\ T\land\bigwedge_{f\in E\setminus\{e\}}f\not\models p
review_flags: A source distinguishing subset-minimal from minimum-cardinality explanations is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deletion procedure and its subset-minimal, rather than minimum-cardinality, conclusion are internally consistent, and algorithm is the correct content kind. A source with a specific locator is required for the procedure, exact-query assumptions, and minimality distinction.

children.title: Reusable Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanation structures retained for use across multiple related propagation or conflict events.

knowledge_statements.title: Reusable Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cached explanations equipped with an explicit validity guard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a theory \(T\), a reusable explanation is a triple \((G,E,p)\), where \(G\) is a guard, \(E\) is a finite set of premise literals, and \(p\) is the explained consequence, satisfying \[T\models G\rightarrow\left(\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\rightarrow p\right).\] The explanation may be reused in any search state \(s\) in which \(G\) and every member of \(E\) are true and the interpretation of \(T\), the variables, and the literals is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached explanation is reusable whenever its guard and premises hold and the theory and literal meanings have not changed.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and the literal interpretation remain invariant between generation and reuse.
The reuse state satisfies \(G\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\models G\rightarrow\left(\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\rightarrow p\right)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: guarded logical entailment provides a precise reusable-explanation model
Terminology and reuse conditions require a dedicated explanation-learning source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The guarded implication is a coherent definition and fits the reusable-explanations leaf, but the record supplies no evidence that this triple, terminology, and invariance conditions match the intended explanation-learning literature.

children.title: Piecewise Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanation structures assembled from independently maintained explanatory components.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A consequence represented by different explanations on guarded state regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a constraint theory and let \(p\) be a consequence. A piecewise explanation is a finite family \(\{(G_i,E_i)\}_{i=1}^m\) such that, for every \(i\), \[T\models G_i\rightarrow\left(\bigwedge_{e\in E_i}e\rightarrow p\right).\] On a state satisfying \(G_i\), the corresponding set \(E_i\) may explain \(p\). If the guards cover a target region \(R\), meaning \(T\models R\rightarrow\bigvee_{i=1}^mG_i\), the family supplies an explanation throughout \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A piecewise explanation assigns distinct sufficient premise sets to guarded regions and covers a target region when at least one guard always applies there.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is finite.
Each guard and premise literal has a fixed interpretation under \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall i:\ T\models G_i\rightarrow\left(\bigwedge_{e\in E_i}e\rightarrow p\right)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: guarded case representation formalizes piecewise explanation reuse
The intended literature-specific meaning of piecewise explanation needs confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The guarded finite-family representation is internally precise and representation is a suitable content kind. Because no citation is supplied, it is uncertain whether this constructed meaning of piecewise explanations matches the exact literature-specific sense of the immutable leaf.

children.title: Explanation Composition
children.top_down_role: Structural combination of explanatory components into conflict-analysis inputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transitive composition of explanation implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a theory, let \(E_1,E_2\) be finite literal sets, and let \(p,q\) be literals. If \[T\land\bigwedge_{e\in E_1}e\models p\qquad\text{and}\qquad T\land p\land\bigwedge_{e\in E_2}e\models q,\] then eliminating the intermediate consequence gives \[T\land\bigwedge_{e\in E_1\cup E_2}e\models q.\] Hence antecedent explanations can be substituted recursively to obtain an explanation expressed in earlier decisions or retained premises.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If one premise set explains an intermediate literal and that literal helps explain another consequence, their union explains the final consequence.
assumptions_latex: \(T\land\bigwedge_{e\in E_1}e\models p\).
\(T\land p\land\bigwedge_{e\in E_2}e\models q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\land\bigwedge_{e\in E_1\cup E_2}e\models q
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: composition follows the standard implicational semantics of explanations
A CP-specific source for compositional explanation generation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entailment-composition claim is mathematically sound, plain text agrees with the formula, and property fits the terminal container. It nevertheless lacks a CP-specific citation and locator supporting explanation substitution or composition in this setting.

children.title: Reuse-Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Context changes that restrict safe or useful reuse of stored explanatory components.

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions beyond which a cached explanation is not soundly reusable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached implication \(G\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\rightarrow p\) is soundly reusable only while the generating theory, literal meanings, and guard remain valid. If generation actually used an additional condition \(h\), with \[T\models h\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\rightarrow p\quad\text{but}\quad T\not\models\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\rightarrow p,\] then reusing \(E\) in a state where \(h\) is false is unsound. The missing condition must be retained as a premise or incorporated into \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse becomes unsound when a hidden generation condition, theory component, or literal interpretation changes without being represented in the cached guard.
assumptions_latex: The cached explanation was derived using condition \(h\).
A reuse state can satisfy every literal in \(E\) while falsifying \(h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\not\models\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\rightarrow p
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: omitted assumptions give the canonical logical boundary for reuse
A dedicated source is needed for CP-specific invalidation events.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The omitted-condition example correctly describes a logical failure boundary, and failure_boundary is the appropriate content kind. A dedicated source is still needed to establish the intended CP reuse-validity conditions and invalidation events.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Strength–Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto comparison of explanation pruning power and computational burden.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate explanations \(E\), let \(S(E)\) measure expected search reduction from learning with \(E\), and let \(K(E)\) measure generation, minimization, storage, and propagation cost. Explanation \(E_1\) dominates \(E_2\) when \[S(E_1)\ge S(E_2),\qquad K(E_1)\le K(E_2),\] with at least one strict inequality. A rational selection rule retains only nondominated candidates, or maximizes a specified scalar utility such as \(S(E)-\lambda K(E)\) for \(\lambda\ge0\); logical size alone does not determine computational value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explanation selection balances anticipated pruning against production and use costs; dominated candidates can be discarded under the chosen measures.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(K\) are evaluated under a fixed search policy and workload.
\(K(E)\ge0\) for every candidate \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_1\succ E_2\iff S(E_1)\ge S(E_2)\land K(E_1)\le K(E_2)\land\bigl(S(E_1)>S(E_2)\lor K(E_1)<K(E_2)\bigr)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Pareto dominance precisely expresses the strength–cost tradeoff
Measures of explanation strength and cost vary across systems and require a specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto definition is internally consistent and principle fits a tradeoff leaf. The proposed strength and cost measures are abstract and system-dependent, and no cited source establishes that this formalization is the intended explanation-quality tradeoff.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Set Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward traversal from failure to a decision-level conflict set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an inconsistent trail \(M\) with a failure explanation \(F\), and an antecedent explanation \(A(l)\) for every propagated literal \(l\). Initialize \(C\leftarrow F\). While \(C\) contains a selected propagated literal \(l\), replace it by its antecedents: \[C\leftarrow(C\setminus\{l\})\cup A(l).\] Stop when the chosen cut criterion holds, such as containing only decision literals. Output \(C\); its conjunction is infeasible under the constraint theory \(T\), so \(\neg\bigwedge_{c\in C}c\) is a learnable nogood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a failure explanation, repeatedly replace propagated literals by their antecedents until the desired conflict cut is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(T\land\bigwedge_{f\in F}f\models\bot\).
For each replaced \(l\), \(T\land\bigwedge_{a\in A(l)}a\models l\).
Antecedent edges point to earlier trail positions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\models\neg\bigwedge_{c\in C}c
review_flags: No supplied locator covers explanation-based conflict-set analysis.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The antecedent-expansion procedure is coherent under the stated earlier-trail assumption, its learned nogood follows from the maintained conflict explanation, and algorithm fits the leaf. No inspectable source supports this particular explanation-based conflict-set calculus or its stopping cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolution-Style Conflict Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-resolution elimination along an implication trail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent explanations and the current conflict as clauses. Initialize the learned clause \(L\) to the conflict clause. If \(x\) is a trail literal occurring in \(L\) and its antecedent clause has form \(R\lor x\), while \(L=L'\lor\neg x\), update \[L\leftarrow L'\lor R.\] Repeat using antecedents in reverse trail order until a stopping criterion, commonly one current-level literal, is met. Output \(L\), which remains entailed by the theory because every update is a sound resolution step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve the conflict clause with antecedent clauses in reverse trail order until the selected cut, often a single current-level literal, is reached.
assumptions_latex: Every antecedent clause and the initial conflict clause are entailed by \(T\).
Each pivot appears with opposite polarity in the two resolved clauses.
