Trail antecedents precede their propagated literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\models L
review_flags: A CP or lazy-clause-generation source is required for the precise calculus.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pivot polarities and resolution update are consistent, the entailment invariant is correctly stated, and algorithm is the correct role. A CP or lazy-clause-generation citation with a precise locator is required for the reverse-trail procedure and stopping criterion.

knowledge_statements.title: Asserting-Nogood Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Learned nogoods that force propagation after backjumping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) be a learned nogood, so \(T\models\neg\bigwedge_{l\in N}l\), and let \(b\) be a candidate backjump level. The nogood is asserting at \(b\) when exactly one literal \(u\in N\) is assigned above \(b\), while every literal in \(N\setminus\{u\}\) remains true after truncating the trail to level \(b\). At that level, unit propagation on \(N\) forces \(\neg u\). Different conflict cuts or literal encodings therefore induce families of asserting nogoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An asserting nogood has one literal left to prevent after backjumping, so it immediately forces that literal's negation.
assumptions_latex: \(T\models\neg\bigwedge_{l\in N}l\).
Exactly one member \(u\) of \(N\) is assigned above level \(b\).
Every member of \(N\setminus\{u\}\) is true at level \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\land\bigwedge_{l\in N\setminus\{u\}}l\models\neg u
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard asserting-clause condition translated to nogoods
A source is needed for asserting-nogood variants in CP.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly captures immediate propagation after truncation to the backjump level, and definition fits the leaf. The asserted family interpretation and its translation from asserting clauses to CP nogoods have no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Learning-Guided Backjumping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonchronological backtracking determined by a learned asserting nogood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a trail with decision levels and a learned asserting nogood \(N\). Let \(u\) be its unique literal at the highest level and define \(b\) as the greatest level among literals in \(N\setminus\{u\}\), taking \(b=0\) when that set has no positive-level literal. Delete trail assignments above \(b\), retain \(N\), and propagate \(\neg u\). If \(N\) is asserting, this propagation is immediate and prevents reconstruction of the analyzed conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backjump to the highest level among the learned nogood's nonasserting literals, retain the nogood, and propagate the asserting literal's negation.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is entailed by the constraint theory.
\(N\) is asserting with unique highest-level literal \(u\).
Decision levels on the trail are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b=\max\bigl(\{\operatorname{lev}(l):l\in N\setminus\{u\}\}\cup\{0\}\bigr)\quad\land\quad T\land\bigwedge_{l\in N\setminus\{u\}}l\models\neg u
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard nonchronological backjump rule for an asserting learned constraint
No supplied locator specifically supports learning-guided CP backjumping.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Given an asserting nogood and a well-defined trail, the stated second-highest-level backjump rule is coherent and algorithm fits the container. No cited locator supports the precise CP learning-guided backjump procedure or its stated conflict-prevention behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Conflict Learning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict learning from infeasibility relative to an incumbent objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of \(f(x)\) over feasible set \(X\) with incumbent value \(U\). Search under the cutoff \(B_U(x): f(x)<U\). If literals \(E\) imply that no improving feasible solution exists, \[X\land B_U\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\bot,\] then the guarded nogood \(B_U\rightarrow\neg\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\) may be learned. It remains valid after tightening the incumbent to \(U'\le U\), because \(B_{U'}\) implies \(B_U\), but it cannot generally be reused after relaxing the cutoff unless the bound guard is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An improving-solution conflict yields a bound-guarded nogood; tightening preserves it, while relaxing the incumbent may invalidate unguarded reuse.
assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(f\) over \(X\).
\(U\) is a valid incumbent objective value.
\(X\land B_U\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\bot\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\models B_U\rightarrow\neg\bigwedge_{e\in E}e
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: objective-cutoff infeasibility yields a guarded learned nogood
A source is required for optimization-specific conflict learning and incumbent-bound reuse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound-guarded implication and monotonic validity under incumbent tightening are mathematically coherent, and principle is an acceptable role for this validity rule. An optimization-specific conflict-learning source is required to support the cutoff semantics, learning rule, and reuse boundary.

assumptions_latex: A finite-domain constraint problem has current decision literals whose conjunction is denoted by \(A\).
Every propagation or failure used for learning has a sound explanation over recorded literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every learned constraint is entailed by the original constraint set and excludes the explained failure while preserving all solutions.

notation.meaning: conjunction of currently active decision or propagation literals
an explained consequence literal, with \(q=\bot\) for failure

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound explanation-based learning is standard in constraint programming, but no supplied locator addresses it directly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational form for finite-domain constraint search with sound explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given active literals \(A\), propagate until a propagator derives \(q\) or detects failure \(q=\bot\). Require an explanation \(E\subseteq A\) satisfying \(C\models (\bigwedge E)\rightarrow q\), where \(C\) is the original constraint set. On failure, analyze the implication graph formed by explanations, derive a constraint \(L\) with \(C\models L\) that is falsified by the current assignment, add \(L\) permanently, backtrack to a level where \(L\) is not falsified, and resume propagation. Terminate with a solution, unsatisfiability, or an external resource limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explain each propagation or failure, analyze conflicting explanations, learn an entailed constraint, backtrack, and continue without eliminating any feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-Based Constraint Learning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf and is broadly standard, but no cited source supports the explanation, learning, backtracking, and termination specification.

assumptions_latex: The solver maintains a constraint store \(C\) and a current partial assignment \(A\).
Each learned constraint can be checked as a logical consequence of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding any generated constraint \(G\) with \(C\models G\) preserves the solution set and may prevent recurrence of the generalized failure.

notation.meaning: learned constraint in the solver's native constraint language

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: consequence-preserving constraint learning is standard, but the intended general-constraint architecture lacks a supplied source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Learning constraints need not be clauses when the solver supports sound native constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a failed search state, construct a constraint \(G\) in an admitted constraint language, possibly stronger than a single nogood clause, such that \(C\models G\) and the current partial assignment \(A\) violates \(G\). Insert \(G\) into the persistent store and propagate it after backtracking. Soundness requires only entailment by \(C\); completeness additionally requires that branching and propagation continue fairly whenever no resource limit intervenes. The learned constraint may summarize several explanations, exploit global-constraint structure, or remove values beyond the immediately conflicting assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Learn any solver-supported constraint entailed by the model and violated by the failed state; clauses are only one possible learned form.
knowledge_statements.title: General-Constraint Learning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits general-constraint learning, but the native-constraint architecture and the stated fairness-based completeness condition require a direct source.

assumptions_latex: Each variable \(x\) has a finite ordered domain \(D_x=\{v_1<\cdots<v_m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality and order literals represent every finite-domain restriction and admit clauses enforcing their intended semantics.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct and order encodings of finite-domain variables are standard, but no relevant supplied locator is available
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct and order Boolean representations for finite ordered domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent \(x=v_i\) by \(e_{x,i}\) and \(x\le v_i\) by \(o_{x,i}\). The direct encoding imposes \(\bigvee_{i=1}^{m}e_{x,i}\) and pairwise or cardinality constraints ensuring exactly one equality literal is true. The order encoding imposes \(o_{x,i}\rightarrow o_{x,i+1}\) for \(1\le i<m\), with boundary conventions \(o_{x,0}=\bot\) and \(o_{x,m}=\top\). Equality is recoverable as \(e_{x,i}\leftrightarrow(o_{x,i}\wedge\neg o_{x,i-1})\), so bounds, removals, and assignments can be exchanged as Boolean consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode finite-domain assignments by equality literals or monotone order literals, with clauses enforcing exactly-one and threshold consistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Literal Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but the direct/order encoding claims and semantic clauses have no inspectable supporting citation.

assumptions_latex: Every propagator is sound for its associated constraint.
All domain changes are expressible by registered Boolean literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The architecture exposes each CP inference as a SAT implication and each CP failure as a SAT conflict clause.

notation.meaning: active input literals explaining a propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lazy-clause-generation architecture with explanation-producing CP propagators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize SAT and CP states from the same root literals. Whenever the SAT trail changes, update the CP domains and run affected propagators to a fixpoint. For each derived literal \(q\), the responsible propagator returns \(E\) such that its constraint entails \((\bigwedge E)\rightarrow q\); enqueue \(q\) with reason clause \((\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e)\vee q\). For failure it returns \(E\) entailing \(\neg\bigwedge E\). SAT conflict analysis learns a clause and selects the backtrack level; both layers then restore the corresponding synchronized state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CP propagators return clausal reasons for deductions and failures, enabling the SAT engine to analyze conflicts and control backtracking.

children.title: SAT-Engine Responsibilities
children.top_down_role: Conflict analysis, clause-oriented propagation, or learned-record services owned by the SAT engine.

assumptions_latex: The CP layer reports only literals and clauses valid under the shared encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SAT engine maintains the authoritative trail, learns entailed clauses, and selects logically valid backtrack points.

notation.meaning: ordered SAT assignment trail partitioned by decision levels

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: these responsibilities follow the standard CDCL component of lazy clause generation, but a direct source is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical responsibilities of the CDCL component in a synchronized SAT-CP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SAT engine owns the trail \(T\), decision levels, Boolean unit propagation, branching decisions, reason clauses, and clause database. Given a conflict clause \(K\) falsified by \(T\), it resolves \(K\) with recorded reasons until a learned asserting clause \(K'\) is obtained, where the chosen analysis scheme determines the stopping condition. It computes the backjump level from \(K'\), retracts the trail to that level, installs \(K'\), and enqueues its asserting literal. It may also restart and delete redundant learned clauses without changing satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SAT engine owns decisions, the Boolean trail, unit propagation, conflict analysis, learned clauses, backjumping, restarts, and clause management.
knowledge_statements.title: SAT-Engine Responsibilities

assumptions_latex: Each CP propagator is sound and can explain every deduction communicated to SAT.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The CP layer maintains domain consistency with the SAT trail and supplies sound, literal-based reasons for every exported inference.

notation.meaning: current domain store induced by the synchronized trail
constraint handled by a CP propagator

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: these are standard CP-layer duties in lazy clause generation, but no direct source locator was supplied
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain and propagation responsibilities of the CP component in lazy clause generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The CP layer maps incoming trail literals to domain restrictions, maintains the reversible domain store \(D\), schedules propagators, and computes a propagation fixpoint. If a propagator for \(c\) derives a representable restriction \(q\), it emits \(q\) with antecedents \(E\) satisfying \(c\models(\bigwedge E)\rightarrow q\). If a domain becomes empty or a propagator detects inconsistency, it emits antecedents satisfying \(c\models\neg\bigwedge E\). On SAT backtracking, the layer restores every domain and propagator state to the matching decision level before further propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The CP layer updates reversible domains, schedules propagators, exports explained deductions or conflicts, and restores state when SAT backtracks.

children.title: Synchronization Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Consistency, latency, or state-ownership problems at the integration boundary.

assumptions_latex: SAT and CP exchange encoded literals while maintaining separate reversible states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Violating semantic agreement, explanation validity, message ordering, or rollback alignment can make the combined solver unsound or incomplete.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: synchronization invariants are logically necessary, but concrete failure cases need a directly supporting architecture source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp correctness boundaries for a stateful SAT-CP propagation interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Correctness is not guaranteed if any of the following occurs: a literal has different meanings in the two layers; a reason contains an antecedent absent from the relevant trail prefix; a propagation is installed after its supporting state was retracted; or backtracking from \((T_d,D_d)\) restores only one layer. An invalid reason may yield a learned clause not entailed by the model, causing unsound pruning. A missed propagation or stale CP restriction may respectively destroy propagation completeness or exclude a genuine solution.

children.title: Decomposition-Based Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanation support obtained through decomposed constraints or auxiliary encodings.

assumptions_latex: A constraint \(c\) is replaced by a decomposition \(F_c\) over original and auxiliary literals.
The decomposition is satisfiability-equivalent to \(c\) after existentially quantifying auxiliaries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unit-propagation reasons from \(F_c\) are sound explanations for \(c\), although their inference strength depends on the decomposition.

notation.meaning: decomposed clause or primitive-constraint system for \(c\)

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explanation through an equivalent decomposition is standard, but supplied decomposition sources concern mathematical programming rather than LCG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explanations obtained by propagating an encoded decomposition of a global constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(X)\leftrightarrow\exists Y\,F_c(X,Y)\), where \(F_c\) is a conjunction of clauses or explanation-capable primitive constraints. If propagation in \(F_c\) derives \(q\) from active literals \(E\), record the implication chain and eliminate intermediate auxiliary literals by resolution, obtaining a clause \((\bigvee_{e\in E'}\neg e)\vee q\) with \(E'\subseteq E\) and \(c\models(\bigwedge E')\rightarrow q\). For a conflict, resolve to a clause over active literals that is entailed by \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decompose a global constraint into explainable primitives, then resolve their implication chain into a sound reason for each deduction or conflict.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every exported deduction \(q\), the native propagator returns active literals \(E\) such that \(c\models(\bigwedge E)\rightarrow q\). The corresponding reason clause is \(R=(\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e)\vee q\). It is verifiable by checking that all literals in \(E\) precede \(q\) on the trail and that the propagator's certified inference rule establishes \(c\models R\). For failure, the certificate is \(R=\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e\), with \(c\models R\) and every member of \(E\) active.

children.title: Explanation Granularity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Differences in explanatory precision, size, and propagation visibility across the two regimes.

assumptions_latex: Two sound explanations \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) justify the same propagated literal \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explanation selection trades generation cost and clause size against backjumping power and future propagation; soundness alone does not determine the best granularity.

notation.meaning: alternative antecedent sets for the same consequence

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explanation-size and strength tradeoffs are recognized in LCG, but the comparative claim requires a dedicated source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of coarse and fine antecedent sets for sound explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any sound antecedent set \(E\), define \(R(E)=(\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e)\vee q\). If \(E_1\subseteq E_2\), then \(R(E_1)\models R(E_2)\), so the smaller-antecedent explanation is logically stronger. However, finding a small or maximally general \(E_1\) may require additional propagator work, and its literals may occur at decision levels that yield a different learned clause or backjump level. Thus explanation quality must be assessed jointly by construction cost, reason size, decision-level profile, and resulting learned-clause utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fewer antecedents give a stronger reason, but finding them may cost more and need not produce the most useful learned clause or backjump.
knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Granularity Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical entailment comparison is correct and the principle fits the leaf, but the operational tradeoffs concerning cost, backjumping, and learned-clause utility need a dedicated source.

children.title: Encoding-Overhead Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Memory or propagation costs that limit decomposition-based explanation support.

assumptions_latex: A constraint over \(n\) variables is translated into Boolean literals and clauses before or during search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An encoding whose materialized size exceeds available resources, or whose propagation is asymptotically weaker than native propagation, marks a practical boundary for decomposition-based learning.

notation.meaning: number of generated Boolean literals and clauses

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: encoding size and propagation strength are standard implementation boundaries, but no exact family or bound is supplied by the source hints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource and inference-strength limits of materialized Boolean decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S(n)\) count the literals and clauses materialized by an encoding on instances of size \(n\). Full materialization is infeasible whenever \(S(n)>M\), where \(M\) is the solver's storage budget; repeated scanning is likewise infeasible when the cumulative propagation work exceeds the search budget. Even when \(S(n)\le M\), the encoding crosses a propagation boundary if Boolean unit propagation fails to derive a domain consequence that the intended native consistency algorithm derives at the same search state. Lazy generation can defer size cost but cannot remove a superpolynomial worst-case requirement inherent to the chosen representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean decomposition becomes unsuitable when its size or propagation work exceeds resources, or when unit propagation is materially weaker than native filtering.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Overhead Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the record gives no concrete encoding family or complexity model, and its broad superpolynomial worst-case assertion requires a specific theorem and source.

children.title: Retention Policies
children.top_down_role: Criteria for preserving learned constraints across database-reduction events.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the fixed constraint model and every learned constraint \(c\in L_t\) satisfies \(F\models c\).
Each learned constraint has a finite score \(s_t(c)\) and a Boolean protection flag \(p_t(c)\).
The database capacity at management time \(t\) is \(B_t\in\mathbb{N}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_t=P_t\cup\operatorname{Top}_{B_t-|P_t|}(L_t\setminus P_t,s_t)\), provided \(|P_t|\le B_t\).

notation.meaning: learned-constraint database at management time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generic bounded retention rule for entailed learned constraints, with mandatory protection and score-based selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a database-management event \(t\), form the protected set \(P_t=\{c\in L_t:p_t(c)=1\}\). If \(|P_t|\le B_t\), retain every member of \(P_t\), then fill the remaining \(B_t-|P_t|\) positions with unprotected constraints having greatest score, using a fixed deterministic tie rule. Thus \[R_t=P_t\cup\operatorname{Top}_{B_t-|P_t|}(L_t\setminus P_t,s_t).\] Output \(R_t\) as the next learned database. Since every discarded constraint is entailed by \(F\), retention affects propagation and search effort but not the feasible set defined by \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep every protected learned constraint, then retain the highest-scoring unprotected constraints up to capacity; deleting other entailed constraints changes search performance but not feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Retention Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Retention Policies leaf, and the bounded top-score rule is internally coherent. However, no citation supports this particular protection, capacity, and score-based retention policy or its intended CP learned-constraint interpretation.

children.title: Deletion Policies
children.top_down_role: Criteria for removing learned constraints from active storage.

assumptions_latex: Every \(c\in L_t\) is logically entailed by the fixed model \(F\).
The protected set \(P_t\subseteq L_t\) is excluded from deletion.
A deletion quota \(q_t\) satisfies \(0\le q_t\le |L_t\setminus P_t|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{t+1}=L_t\setminus\operatorname{Bottom}_{q_t}(L_t\setminus P_t,s_t)\) and \(F\land\bigwedge L_{t+1}\equiv F\).

notation.meaning: constraints immune to the current deletion event
deletion score, where smaller values have lower priority

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-based deletion of redundant learned constraints while preserving protected records and model equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At deletion event \(t\), rank the eligible set \(L_t\setminus P_t\) by nondecreasing score \(s_t\), with a fixed tie rule. Delete exactly the first \(q_t\) records: \[D_t=\operatorname{Bottom}_{q_t}(L_t\setminus P_t,s_t),\qquad L_{t+1}=L_t\setminus D_t.\] The output database is \(L_{t+1}\). Because \(F\models c\) for every \(c\in D_t\), deletion preserves logical equivalence \[F\land\bigwedge_{c\in L_{t+1}}c\equiv F.\] This conclusion does not apply to original constraints or to records whose validity depends on assumptions no longer present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete the prescribed number of lowest-scoring eligible constraints. Sound deletion preserves the original model because every deleted learned constraint is redundant and globally entailed.
knowledge_statements.title: Deletion Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Deletion Policies leaf, and equivalence follows under the stated global-entailment assumption. No source supports the specific bottom-score deletion rule, protected-set semantics, or stated validity boundary.

children.title: Protected Constraint Classes
children.top_down_role: Learned-constraint categories exempted from ordinary deletion decisions.

assumptions_latex: \(L_t\) is a finite learned database.
Each record has predicates for lock status, permanent status, and current reason use.
Protection is evaluated before any deletion selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_t=\{c\in L_t:\ell_t(c)\lor m(c)\lor r_t(c)\}\) and every admissible deletion set satisfies \(D_t\cap P_t=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: predicate that c is locked by current propagation state
predicate that c is permanently retained by policy
predicate that c is an active explanation or reason

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimal protection predicate for constraints that deletion must not remove at the current search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the protected class at management time \(t\) by \[P_t=\{c\in L_t:\ell_t(c)\lor m(c)\lor r_t(c)\}.\] Here \(\ell_t(c)\) means that a live propagated consequence stores \(c\) as its reason, \(m(c)\) means that policy marks \(c\) permanent, and \(r_t(c)\) means that the current conflict or explanation construction is using \(c\). A deletion operation is admissible only if its deletion set \(D_t\) satisfies \(D_t\subseteq L_t\setminus P_t\), equivalently \(D_t\cap P_t=\varnothing\). Additional solver-specific classes may enlarge \(P_t\), but may not invalidate this exclusion condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Protect locked, permanent, and currently used explanation constraints. Any deletion set must be disjoint from this protected class.
knowledge_statements.title: Protected Constraint Classes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits this leaf, but the asserted mandatory protection of locked, permanent, and currently used explanation constraints is solver-dependent. A domain-specific source is required to establish these classes and distinguish the overlapping lock and reason-use predicates.

children.title: Database-Churn Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Search regimes where frequent removal or reacquisition destabilizes learned-constraint management.

assumptions_latex: Database management occurs at discrete events \(t=0,1,2,\ldots\).
At event \(t\), at most \(a_t\) records are admitted and at most \(d_t\) are deleted.
Uniform bounds \(a_t\le A\) and \(d_t\le D\) hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl||L_{t+1}|-|L_t|\bigr|\le\max\{A,D\}\) and \(|L_T|\le |L_0|+TA\).

notation.meaning: learned database after management event t
numbers admitted and deleted at event t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic per-event bounds on learned-database turnover and resulting size growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lifecycle policy satisfies an \((A,D)\)-churn boundary when every management event obeys \[|L_{t+1}\setminus L_t|=a_t\le A,\qquad |L_t\setminus L_{t+1}|=d_t\le D.\] Consequently, \(|L_{t+1}|=|L_t|+a_t-d_t\), so \[\bigl||L_{t+1}|-|L_t|\bigr|\le\max\{A,D\},\qquad |L_T|\le |L_0|+TA.\] If a hard capacity \(B\) is also required, every event must choose deletions satisfying \(d_t\ge\max\{0,|L_t|+a_t-B\}\). These conditions bound record turnover; they do not bound the computational cost of propagating individual constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cap admissions and deletions per management event. The caps bound database-size changes and, with enough deletion, enforce a hard capacity.
knowledge_statements.title: Database-Churn Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is suitable for a churn boundary, and the displayed size bounds follow from the stated set-difference definitions. No cited source supports this particular per-event admission/deletion formalization as a learned-constraint database policy.

children.title: Activity Policies
children.top_down_role: Learned-constraint management driven by recorded use during propagation or conflict analysis.

assumptions_latex: Conflict events are indexed by \(t\in\mathbb{N}\).
For each learned constraint \(c\), the indicator \(u_t(c)\) records whether it participated in event \(t\).
Parameters satisfy \(0<\rho\le1\) and \(b>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_{t+1}(c)=\rho a_t(c)+b u_t(c)\), with larger \(a_t(c)\) denoting greater recent activity.

notation.meaning: activity score of learned constraint c after event t
participation indicator for c at event t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponentially decayed conflict-participation activity for ranking learned constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(a_0(c)=0\) when a learned constraint \(c\) is created. After conflict event \(t\), set \(u_t(c)=1\) if \(c\) participated in the conflict analysis or explanation, and set \(u_t(c)=0\) otherwise. Update every live score by \[a_{t+1}(c)=\rho a_t(c)+b u_t(c).\] At a management event, rank constraints by decreasing \(a_t(c)\); larger values represent more frequent recent participation. If scores are rescaled by a common positive factor to avoid overflow, their ranking is unchanged. Output the updated scores together with the induced ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bump constraints used in conflict analysis and exponentially decay all activity scores. Higher scores indicate more frequent recent use.
knowledge_statements.title: Activity Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Activity Policies, and the recurrence is mathematically well-defined. A source is needed because this exact decay-and-bump update, the meaning of participation, and updating every live constraint are implementation-specific choices rather than a uniquely standard policy.

children.title: Relevance Policies
children.top_down_role: Learned-constraint management driven by current applicability to the residual search state.

assumptions_latex: Each learned constraint \(c\) has a finite set of literals or atomic antecedents \(A(c)\).
The current search state partitions these atoms into decision-level blocks.
Smaller structural width is treated as greater relevance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_t(c)=1/(1+\lambda_t(c))\), where \(\lambda_t(c)=|\{\operatorname{lev}_t(x):x\in A(c)\}|\).

notation.meaning: atoms or antecedents occurring in learned constraint c
current decision level of atom x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A decision-level diversity metric used as structural relevance for learned constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a learned constraint \(c\) at state \(t\), define its level-block count by \[\lambda_t(c)=\left|\{\operatorname{lev}_t(x):x\in A(c)\}\right|.\] Define relevance as \[r_t(c)=\frac{1}{1+\lambda_t(c)}.\] A policy ranks constraints by decreasing \(r_t(c)\), equivalently by increasing \(\lambda_t(c)\), so constraints connecting fewer decision-level blocks are preferred. Ties require a fixed secondary rule, such as activity or creation time. The metric is state dependent whenever decision-level annotations change, and it is defined only when every antecedent in \(A(c)\) has an assigned level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure relevance by the number of decision-level blocks represented in a learned constraint; fewer blocks receive higher relevance, with a fixed rule resolving ties.
knowledge_statements.title: Relevance Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is a particular score representation or scoring rule, not merely a condition. More importantly, the decision-level block metric is closely associated with clause-learning variants and its extension to arbitrary CP learned constraints and atomic antecedents requires a specific source.

children.title: Aging Policies
children.top_down_role: Learned-constraint management that discounts evidence as records become older.

assumptions_latex: Management events are indexed by \(t\in\mathbb{N}\).
Each learned constraint \(c\) has creation time \(\tau(c)\) and last-use time \(u_t(c)\le t\).
The decay factor satisfies \(0<\gamma<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_t(c)=\gamma^{t-u_t(c)}\), so nonuse for \(k\) further events multiplies the score by \(\gamma^k\).

notation.meaning: most recent event at which c was used

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recency-based exponential aging of learned constraints between recorded uses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(c\) is created, set \(u_{	au(c)}(c)=\tau(c)\). At each later event \(t\), replace \(u_t(c)\) by \(t\) if \(c\) participates in propagation or explanation; otherwise retain its previous value. Compute \[g_t(c)=\gamma^{t-u_t(c)}.\] Rank constraints by decreasing \(g_t(c)\), optionally after protected constraints have been removed from consideration. If \(c\) remains unused for \(k\) additional events, then \(g_{t+k}(c)=\gamma^k g_t(c)\). Output the updated last-use times and aging scores; a deletion threshold may then be applied separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Record each constraint's last use and decay its score exponentially during nonuse. Recently used constraints rank above otherwise comparable older constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Aging Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Aging Policies, and the exponential recency calculation is internally consistent. No citation establishes this exact last-use definition, event clock, use criterion, or decay rule for learned constraints.

children.title: Signal-Combination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Priority schemes combining activity, relevance, or age during retention decisions.

assumptions_latex: Each constraint has raw signals \(x_{j,t}(c)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\).
Each normalization map \(N_{j,t}\) has codomain \([0,1]\) and a fixed convention for constant signals.
Weights satisfy \(w_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_{j=1}^m w_j=1\).

notation.meaning: raw value of scoring signal j for c
normalization of signal j at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex combination of normalized activity, relevance, age, or other learned-constraint signals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each live learned constraint \(c\), normalize every raw signal to \(z_{j,t}(c)=N_{j,t}(x_{j,t}(c))\in[0,1]\), orienting all normalized signals so that larger values mean stronger retention priority. Define \[S_t(c)=\sum_{j=1}^{m}w_jz_{j,t}(c),\qquad w_j\ge0,\qquad\sum_{j=1}^{m}w_j=1.\] Then \(S_t(c)\in[0,1]\). Rank constraints by decreasing \(S_t\), using a fixed tie rule. Normalization parameters, orientations, weights, and the convention for a constant signal must be fixed for each management epoch; otherwise scores from that epoch are not comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize all retention signals to a common orientation and range, then combine them with nonnegative weights summing to one.
knowledge_statements.title: Signal-Combination Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Signal-Combination Regimes, and the convex-combination range claim is correct under the stated assumptions. A source is still required for presenting this normalization and weighted aggregation scheme as a learned-constraint scoring regime.

children.title: Metric-Drift Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where management signals cease to track the future utility of learned constraints.

assumptions_latex: At epochs \(t\) and \(t+1\), a raw metric is normalized using parameters \(\theta_t\) and \(\theta_{t+1}\).
Retention compares scores against a fixed threshold \(q\in(0,1)\).
The normalization map is \(N_{\theta}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(N_{\theta_t}(x(c))\ge q>N_{\theta_{t+1}}(x(c))\), the same record changes retention class solely because the metric scale drifted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of threshold decisions when score normalization changes across management epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a learned record \(c\) whose raw metric \(x(c)\) does not change between two management epochs. If normalization parameters drift so that \[N_{\theta_t}(x(c))\ge q>N_{\theta_{t+1}}(x(c)),\] then a threshold policy retains \(c\) at epoch \(t\) and rejects it at epoch \(t+1\) despite unchanged raw evidence. Thus cross-epoch threshold decisions are stable only if normalization is fixed, scores are recomputed under common parameters, or the drift cannot move any live score across \(q\). Rank preservation alone is insufficient for absolute-threshold stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing normalization can move an unchanged constraint across a retention threshold. Stable threshold decisions require fixed or consistently recomputed metric scales.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Drift Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind exactly fits the leaf, and the threshold-crossing example is logically correct. No source is supplied for the claimed lifecycle-policy boundary or for the broader stability characterization.

children.title: Restart-Scoped Retention
children.top_down_role: Learned constraints or heuristic state preserved across sequential restart episodes.

assumptions_latex: A restart changes search state but leaves the base model \(F\) unchanged.
Every globally retained constraint \(c\) satisfies \(F\models c\).
State-dependent learned constraints carry an explicit validity predicate for the new restart epoch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L^{k+1}_0=G_k\cup\{c\in E_k:V_{k+1}(c)=1\}\), where \(G_k=\{c\in L^k:F\models c\}\).

notation.meaning: learned database produced during restart epoch k
globally entailed records from epoch k
validity predicate for record c in epoch k+1

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of globally valid and explicitly revalidated learned constraints across search restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the end of restart epoch \(k\), partition the learned database into \(G_k=\{c\in L^k:F\models c\}\) and the remaining state-dependent set \(E_k=L^k\setminus G_k\). After restarting, initialize \[L^{k+1}_0=G_k\cup\{c\in E_k:V_{k+1}(c)=1\}.\] Discard every \(c\in E_k\) for which validity is false or unavailable. Apply capacity and scoring policies only after this validity filter. The output \(L^{k+1}_0\) may safely accompany the unchanged base model; unconditional transfer is not justified when the base model or active assumptions differ across epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across a restart, keep globally entailed constraints and revalidate state-dependent ones. Discard records lacking validity under the new epoch's assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart-Scoped Retention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Restart-Scoped Retention, but the global-versus-state-dependent partition and the predicate used to revalidate state-dependent records depend on the solver's learning semantics. A source must specify those semantics and justify transfer across restart epochs.

children.title: Parallel Constraint Sharing
children.top_down_role: Transfer of learned constraints among concurrently running search workers.

assumptions_latex: Workers \(i=1,\ldots,p\) solve the same base model \(F\).
A worker exports only learned constraints carrying a checkable validity scope and metadata.
Communication may be asynchronous and may deliver duplicate records.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_j\leftarrow L_j\cup\{c:\operatorname{admit}_j(c,m)=1\}\), and admission requires \(F\models c\) or a locally satisfied validity scope.

notation.meaning: exported learned constraint and its metadata

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous export, validation, and admission of learned constraints among workers solving a common model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When worker \(i\) learns \(c\), it may export the record \((c,m)\), where \(m\) contains validity scope and scoring metadata. Receiving worker \(j\) rejects malformed or duplicate records, checks that \(F\models c\) or that every assumption in the recorded scope is active locally, and evaluates \(\operatorname{admit}_j(c,m)\). If the predicate is true, update \[L_j\leftarrow L_j\cup\{c\};\] otherwise leave \(L_j\) unchanged. Imported constraints enter the local propagation and lifecycle mechanisms under receiver-local scores. Message order must not affect logical soundness, although it may affect search trajectory and runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers asynchronously export learned constraints with validity metadata. A receiver validates, deduplicates, and locally admits each record before using it for propagation.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Constraint Sharing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Parallel Constraint Sharing. The proposed asynchronous validation, deduplication, admission, and receiver-local scoring protocol is plausible but implementation-specific and has no supporting citation; the meaning and checkability of validity scopes also require a source.

children.title: Shared-Record Admission
children.top_down_role: Selection criteria for accepting externally produced learned constraints.

assumptions_latex: A received record contains constraint \(c\), validity scope \(H\), size \(\sigma(c)\), and quality value \(q(c)\).
The receiver has active assumptions \(A_j\), capacity limit \(B_j\), and admission thresholds \(S_j,Q_j\).
The receiver can verify the record's entailment claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{admit}_j(c)=1\) exactly when validity, novelty, size, quality, and capacity predicates all hold.

notation.meaning: assumptions under which c is valid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conjunctive receiver-side gate for validity, novelty, quality, size, and available capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define receiver \(j\)'s admission predicate by \[\operatorname{admit}_j(c)=\mathbf{1}\!\left[H\subseteq A_j\ \land\ F\land\bigwedge H\models c\ \land\ c\notin L_j\ \land\ \sigma(c)\le S_j\ \land\ q(c)\ge Q_j\ \land\ |L_j|<B_j\right].\] Admit the shared record exactly when this value is \(1\); otherwise reject or defer it. The entailment test establishes local soundness, novelty prevents exact duplicates, and the remaining predicates implement resource and utility gates. A fingerprint may test novelty only when collisions are resolved by an exact equality check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admit a shared record only if its scope is active, entailment is verified, it is new, it meets quality and size thresholds, and capacity remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Record Admission

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Shared-Record Admission, but no source supports this exact conjunction of validity, novelty, size, quality, and capacity gates. The base model F is used in the entailment test without being explicitly introduced in the assumptions or notation, and the semantics of H as assumptions versus constraints need authoritative clarification.

children.title: Cross-Worker Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model, state, or representation differences that constrain safe sharing between workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Worker Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound admission condition for learned constraints exchanged between heterogeneous CP workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let worker \(w\) solve base constraints \(F_w\), and let \(C\) be learned by worker \(u\) using assumptions \(A_u\). Worker \(v\) may retain \(C\) only if \(F_v\models C\). A sufficient check is that every inference producing \(C\) is sound and \(F_v\models A_u\). Literals encoding source-local decisions, temporary bounds, worker-specific auxiliary variables, or retracted constraints must therefore be discharged, translated semantics-preservingly, or retained as explicit antecedents. Otherwise importing \(C\) can remove a solution of \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worker may import a learned constraint only when its own permanent model entails it; source-local assumptions must be discharged, translated, or represented explicitly.
assumptions_latex: \(F_u\) and \(F_v\) have well-defined solution semantics.
The translation between shared variables preserves truth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_v\models C\) is required for sound cross-worker retention.

notation.meaning: Permanent constraint conjunction of worker w
Assumptions used by the source derivation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but no citation is supplied. The claimed sufficient check also needs a precise premise connecting the derivation of C to A_u and constraints valid for worker v; inference soundness and F_v entails A_u alone do not establish F_v entails C.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-Generation Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-sensitive lower bound for constructing explicit propagation explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a search run performs \(T\) explained propagations or failures and emits explanation \(E_t\) containing \(\ell_t\) literal occurrences at event \(t\). In any explicit representation requiring each occurrence to be written, explanation generation takes time \(\Omega(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell_t)\) and produces the same asymptotic output volume. Hence explanations of size \(\Theta(n)\) at \(\Theta(T)\) events impose \(\Omega(Tn)\) work even when the underlying propagator detects each event in constant amortized time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit explanation construction costs at least its output size, so large explanations can dominate otherwise inexpensive propagation.
assumptions_latex: Explanations are materialized explicitly as literal lists.
Writing one literal occurrence has unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generation cost is \(\Omega(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell_t)\).

notation.meaning: Number of literal occurrences in the explanation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the bottleneck leaf and the output-size argument is plausible under the stated unit-cost representation, but no inspectable source supports the computational model or bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak or Nonreusable Nogoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary where a sound nogood excludes negligible search volume or depends on local state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) with permanent constraint \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\ge 1\), the conflicting assignment \(x_1=\cdots=x_n=0\) yields the sound nogood \(x_1\lor\cdots\lor x_n\). Among all \(2^n\) complete assignments it excludes only that single assignment, a fraction \(2^{-n}\). Moreover, a nogood containing restart-local decision identifiers or temporary-bound literals is not reusable after those meanings disappear unless it is translated into literals over the permanent model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound nogood may exclude only one leaf, while nogoods mentioning temporary or local state cannot safely be reused without translation.
assumptions_latex: Variables \(x_i\) are Boolean.
Nogood strength is measured by excluded complete assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed nogood excludes fraction \(2^{-n}\), and locally scoped nogoods need not be reusable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, and the Boolean example is internally correct. An authoritative source is still required for the broader claim about restart-local literals and reusable learned nogoods.

knowledge_statements.title: Learned-Database Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case growth without deletion, subsumption, or duplicate suppression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a learning solver begin with \(M_0\) learned constraints and add one distinct constraint \(C_t\) after each of \(T\) conflicts, deleting none. Then \(M_T=M_0+T\), and explicit storage is \(\Omega(\sum_{t=1}^{T}|C_t|)\). If every search node scans all retained constraints and each scan costs at least one operation, propagation overhead per node is \(\Omega(M_0+T)\). Thus unrestricted learning permits linear database growth and cumulative quadratic scan work over \(T\) subsequent nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without deletion or deduplication, one learned constraint per conflict gives linear storage growth and can cause quadratic cumulative scanning work.
assumptions_latex: Each conflict adds a distinct explicitly stored constraint.
No learned constraint is deleted or subsumed.
Propagation scans every retained learned constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_T=M_0+T\), with storage \(\Omega(\sum_t|C_t|)\) and scan cost \(\Omega(M_0+T)\) per node.

notation.meaning: Number of retained learned constraints after t conflicts
Explicit representation size of the constraint

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits. The growth and scanning bounds follow from the unusually strong stated assumptions, but no source supports this learned-database model or its relevance to the claimed failure phenomenon.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe or Incomplete Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for explanations used to learn implication clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For permanent constraints \(F\), a propagation explanation \(E\) for literal \(p\) is safe only if \(F\land E\models p\); then \(F\models(\neg E\lor p)\). Omitting a necessary antecedent can violate this condition. For example, if \(F\) contains \((a\land b)\rightarrow p\), then \(E=a\land b\) is valid, whereas \(E'=a\) is incomplete: the assignment \(a=1,b=0,p=0\) satisfies \(F\) but falsifies the learned clause \(\neg a\lor p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explanation must entail its propagation under permanent constraints; dropping a necessary antecedent can produce a learned clause that removes valid solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(a\), \(b\), and \(p\) are Boolean literals.
Learned clauses are retained beyond the current search state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(F\land E\not\models p\), learning \(\neg E\lor p\) is unsafe.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and the counterexample is mathematically consistent, but the record supplies no authoritative locator for the explanation-soundness condition used in constraint learning.

children.title: Randomized Restart Search
children.top_down_role: Diversification and cutoff policies for randomized complete search, including state retention, runtime regimes, and completeness boundaries.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Optimal Speedup of Las Vegas Algorithms
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Optimal Speedup of Las Vegas Algorithms

knowledge_statements.title: Random Tie Breaking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform random selection among equally scored branching alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite set \(B\) of admissible branches and a deterministic score \(s:B\to\mathbb{R}\), compute \(s^*=\min_{b\in B}s(b)\) and the tie set \(T=\{b\in B:s(b)=s^*\}\). Draw \(b\) uniformly from \(T\), branch on \(b\), and repeat after propagation at each nonterminal node. Stop upon proving infeasibility or optimality, finding an accepted solution, or meeting an external resource limit. If \(|T|=1\), the rule coincides with deterministic selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each node, identify all best-scoring branches and choose uniformly among them; randomness has no effect when the best branch is unique.
assumptions_latex: The admissible branch set \(B\) is finite and nonempty.
The score \(s\) is defined for every admissible branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(b\in T\) is selected with probability \(1/|T|\).

notation.meaning: Admissible branches at the current node

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits and the rule is well specified, but uniform selection among tied minimum-score branches is one particular randomized tie-breaking variant and has no cited support.

children.title: Randomized Variable Ordering
children.top_down_role: Random perturbation or sampling applied to variable-selection priorities.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Variable Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized selection of the next branching variable while retaining deterministic value choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a propagated nonterminal state, let \(U\) be the finite set of branchable variables and let \(q:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be a heuristic score. Form a probability distribution \(P\) on \(U\), for example \(P(x)\propto\exp(-q(x)/\tau)\) with \(\tau>0\). Sample \(x\sim P\), apply the fixed value-ordering rule to create branches for \(x\), and recurse. Stop under the solver's ordinary solution, proof, or resource-limit criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample the next variable from a heuristic-weighted distribution, then branch using a fixed value-ordering rule.
assumptions_latex: The branchable-variable set \(U\) is finite and nonempty.
Every variable in \(U\) has finite score \(q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next variable is distributed according to \(P\), while value ordering remains fixed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the softmax distribution is a specific randomized-variable-ordering construction rather than an intrinsic definition of the topic, and no source establishes this variant.

children.title: Randomized Value Ordering
children.top_down_role: Random perturbation or sampling applied to value-selection priorities.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Value Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized ordering of branches after deterministic variable selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a propagated nonterminal state, select variable \(x\) by a fixed variable heuristic. Let \(V(x)\) be its finite candidate-value set and \(r_x:V(x)\to\mathbb{R}\) a value score. Draw an ordering without replacement using positive weights \(w(v)=\exp(-r_x(v)/\tau)\), \(\tau>0\), and explore the resulting value branches in that order. Repeat at descendants until the solver's solution, proof, or resource-limit stopping condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the variable deterministically, then sample a weighted permutation of its candidate values and explore branches in that order.
assumptions_latex: \(V(x)\) is finite and nonempty.
Every candidate value has finite score.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Variable choice is fixed, while the value-branch order is a random weighted permutation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but 'ordering without replacement using positive weights' does not uniquely define a weighted-permutation distribution, and no source identifies the intended sequential sampling rule.

children.title: Coupled Ordering Randomization
children.top_down_role: Joint control of randomness across variable choices and value choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Ordering Randomization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jointly samples a variable and its associated branch ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a propagated nonterminal state, let \(B=\{(x,\pi):x\in U,\ \pi\in\Pi_x\}\), where \(U\) is the set of branchable variables and \(\Pi_x\) contains admissible orderings of branches for \(x\). Given joint score \(h:B\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(\tau>0\), sample \((x,\pi)\) with probability proportional to \(\exp(-h(x,\pi)/\tau)\), then explore branches of \(x\) in order \(\pi\). Repeat until the ordinary solver stopping condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample the variable and its branch order jointly, allowing dependencies that independent variable and value randomization cannot express.
assumptions_latex: The joint alternative set \(B\) is finite and nonempty.
The joint score \(h\) is finite on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected pair has distribution \(P(x,\pi)\propto\exp(-h(x,\pi)/\tau)\).

notation.meaning: Admissible branch orderings for variable x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits and the finite Gibbs distribution is defined, but this particular joint randomization scheme has no supporting citation and should not be treated as canonical without one.

children.title: Randomization-Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Levels of perturbation ranging from randomized ties to broad ordering reshuffles.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomization-Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temperature limits for score-weighted randomized branch ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite alternative set \(B\), scores \(s:B\to\mathbb{R}\), and temperature \(\tau>0\), define \(P_\tau(b)=\exp(-s(b)/\tau)/\sum_{c\in B}\exp(-s(c)/\tau)\). As \(\tau\downarrow0\), probability concentrates uniformly on the minimizers of \(s\); as \(\tau\to\infty\), \(P_\tau\) converges to the uniform distribution on \(B\). Thus small, intermediate, and large temperatures respectively yield near-deterministic, score-sensitive randomized, and near-uniform ordering regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temperature continuously controls selection from nearly deterministic best-score choice to nearly uniform random choice.
assumptions_latex: The alternative set \(B\) is finite and nonempty.
Every score \(s(b)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\tau\) concentrates on score minimizers as \(\tau\downarrow0\) and becomes uniform as \(\tau\to\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits and both finite-set temperature limits are mathematically correct, but the record has no citation connecting this Gibbs model and its regime interpretation to randomized CP branch ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Heuristic Perturbation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive stochastic perturbation of deterministic branching scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each branching state, let \(B\) be the finite admissible branch set with deterministic scores \(s(b)\). Independently draw noise variables \(\xi_b\) from a specified distribution, choose \(b^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{b\in B}\{s(b)+\sigma\xi_b\}\), and resolve any remaining tie by a fixed rule. Branch on \(b^*\), propagate, and repeat until the solver's ordinary stopping criterion holds. The parameter \(\sigma\ge0\) controls perturbation magnitude, with \(\sigma=0\) recovering the base heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add random noise to each branch score and select the perturbed best branch; zero noise recovers the deterministic heuristic.
assumptions_latex: The admissible branch set \(B\) is finite and nonempty.
Noise variables and scale \(\sigma\) are specified before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^*\) minimizes the perturbed score \(s(b)+\sigma\xi_b\).

notation.meaning: Base heuristic score of branch b

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits and the additive perturbation rule is precise, but the noise law is left generic and no authoritative source supports this as the intended CP heuristic-perturbation method.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Cutoff Restarts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated randomized runs using one constant resource cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a positive cutoff \(C\). For restart \(r=1,2,\ldots\), initialize search from the root with a fresh random seed, run until a solution or proof is obtained or exactly \(C\) units of the chosen resource are consumed, and restart after cutoff exhaustion. If each run independently succeeds within \(C\) units with probability \(p_C\), then success by restart \(R\) has probability \(1-(1-p_C)^R\). The scheme is probabilistically complete only when \(p_C>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeat independent randomized searches with the same cutoff; success probability approaches one exactly when a run has positive within-cutoff success probability.
assumptions_latex: The cutoff resource is fixed and measurable.
Restart outcomes are independent with common success probability \(p_C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\text{success by }R)=1-(1-p_C)^R\), converging to \(1\) iff \(p_C>0\).

notation.meaning: Probability that one run succeeds before cutoff
Number of completed or initiated runs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits. The probability formula is correct under independent identically distributed runs, but no source supports the restart scheme or the stated probabilistic-completeness characterization.

assumptions_latex: The restart base cutoff satisfies \(c>0\).
The growth factor satisfies \(\rho>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(k\)-th run receives cutoff \(C_k=\lceil c\rho^k\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic geometrically increasing failure or node cutoffs for randomized complete search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A geometric restart schedule with base cutoff \(c>0\) and growth factor \(\rho>1\) assigns run \(k\in\mathbb N_0\) the cutoff \[C_k=\lceil c\rho^k\rceil.\] If run \(k\) has not terminated before consuming \(C_k\) units of the chosen resource, it is stopped and run \(k+1\) begins with a fresh randomization and the next cutoff. A solution, proof of infeasibility, or proof of optimality terminates the schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each restarted run receives a cutoff obtained by multiplying the preceding scale by a fixed factor greater than one.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Restarts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Geometric Restarts leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no citation supports the CP restart interpretation or the local ceiling convention. An authoritative restart-scheduling source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is required.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Optimal Speedup of Las Vegas Algorithms
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Optimal Speedup of Las Vegas Algorithms

assumptions_latex: The base cutoff satisfies \(c>0\).
Successive runs are independently randomized instances of the same Las Vegas search procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cutoffs \(C_i=cu_i\) revisit every power-of-two scale while reaching arbitrarily large scales.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Luby-style power-of-two universal schedule for Las Vegas search runtimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(u_1=1\). For \(i\ge 2\), choose the unique \(k\ge 1\) satisfying \(2^{k-1}\le i<2^k\), and set \[u_i=\begin{cases}2^{k-1},&i=2^k-1,\\u_{i-2^{k-1}+1},&i<2^k-1.\end{cases}\] Thus \((u_i)_{i\ge1}=(1,1,2,1,1,2,4,\ldots)\). A universal restart schedule assigns run \(i\) cutoff \(C_i=cu_i\), restarting after cutoff exhaustion and terminating upon a conclusive search result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Luby sequence repeatedly revisits smaller power-of-two cutoffs while introducing progressively larger cutoffs, without selecting a runtime distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Universal Restart Sequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Universal Restart Sequences, and the displayed recurrence generates the stated Luby-style prefix. No source is cited, however, so the recurrence, indexing convention, and characterization as universal cannot be reviewed against primary evidence.

children.title: Dynamic Restarts
children.top_down_role: Restart cutoffs adapted from evolving search statistics or runtime conditions.

assumptions_latex: Each completed run yields a finite search history \(H_k\).
The update map returns a positive finite cutoff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next cutoff is \(C_{k+1}=U(C_k,H_k)\), so the schedule adapts to observed search behavior.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online cutoff adaptation using statistics collected during completed or interrupted CP runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial cutoff \(C_0>0\), run the randomized search until it terminates conclusively or exhausts \(C_k\). After an inconclusive run, collect its observable history \(H_k\), compute \[C_{k+1}=U(C_k,H_k)>0,\] reinitialize the designated transient search state, and start run \(k+1\). The update map \(U\) may use only information available by the restart time. Output the first solution or conclusive infeasibility or optimality certificate returned by a run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic restart policy computes each new cutoff from the cutoff and observable history of the preceding search run.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Restarts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is appropriate for Dynamic Restarts, and its variables and online-information restriction are explicit. The abstract update rule is not tied to a cited CP restart method, so evidence is needed to establish that this formulation matches the intended terminal container.

children.title: Event-Driven Restarts
children.top_down_role: Restarts triggered by designated search events rather than a fixed cutoff alone.

assumptions_latex: The event predicate is evaluated from the current observable history.
A conclusive search result takes precedence over restarting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A restart occurs at the first time \(t\) for which \(E(H_t)=1\).

notation.meaning: search history observed through time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restarts initiated by an observable search event rather than solely by a predetermined cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a randomized search run and monitor its history \(H_t\) after each eligible search event. For a Boolean event predicate \(E\), define \[\tau=\inf\{t\ge0:E(H_t)=1\}.\] Continue the run while \(E(H_t)=0\). If the search concludes before \(\tau\), return its result; otherwise restart at \(\tau\), retain only policy-designated state, reinitialize transient state, and repeat the same monitoring rule on the next run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An event-driven policy restarts at the first eligible search event whose observable history satisfies a specified Boolean predicate.
knowledge_statements.title: Event-Driven Restarts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Event-Driven Restarts and the statement distinguishes conclusive termination from restart triggering. A specific source is required for the event-driven restart model, including its eligible-event time domain and retained-state behavior.

children.title: Restart Trigger Signals
children.top_down_role: Conflict, propagation, progress, or stagnation signals used to initiate adaptive restarts.

assumptions_latex: Signal values are computable from information exposed by the running solver.
The trigger map has codomain \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restart decision at time \(t\) is the predicate \(T(s_t)=1\).

notation.meaning: vector of observable trigger signals at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable statistics used by adaptive restart predicates in propagation-guided search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) be a measurable signal space and let \(s_t\in\mathcal S\) contain statistics observable at search time \(t\), such as conflicts, failures, propagation counts, or moving averages. A restart trigger is a map \(T:\mathcal S\to\{0,1\}\). The policy requests a restart exactly when \[T(s_t)=1.\] Signal computation must not depend on information unavailable at time \(t\), and a conclusive solver result overrides the request.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart trigger signals are online solver statistics mapped by a Boolean rule to a restart or continue decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Trigger Signals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits Restart Trigger Signals, and the Boolean trigger map is internally consistent. No cited source supports the proposed signal class, measurability framing, examples, or precedence convention in propagation-guided CP search.

children.title: Trigger-Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where noisy or delayed trigger signals cause premature or ineffective restarts.

assumptions_latex: The restart trigger is a threshold rule \(T(s_t)=\mathbf 1\{s_t\ge\theta\}\).
The signal admits perturbations of magnitude at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Trigger decisions are perturbation-stable when \(|s_t-\theta|>\varepsilon\) and may be unstable when \(|s_t-\theta|\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation boundary for a scalar threshold restart trigger.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(T(s_t)=\mathbf 1\{s_t\ge\theta\}\) and an observed value \(\widetilde s_t=s_t+e_t\) with \(|e_t|\le\varepsilon\). If \(|s_t-\theta|>\varepsilon\), then \(T(\widetilde s_t)=T(s_t)\) for every admissible perturbation. If \(|s_t-\theta|\le\varepsilon\), an admissible perturbation can cross the threshold, so the restart decision need not be stable. Thus the closed band \([\theta-\varepsilon,\theta+\varepsilon]\) is the trigger-stability boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A threshold trigger is robust outside an epsilon-wide boundary band and can change decision inside that band under admissible perturbations.
knowledge_statements.title: Trigger-Stability Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the endpoint claim is not correct for the asymmetric rule T(s)=1{s>=theta}: at s=theta+epsilon, every perturbation with |e|<=epsilon leaves the trigger true. The exact unstable region and boundary convention therefore require mathematical correction and an authoritative source before a reliable replacement can be selected.

assumptions_latex: Every retained nogood is logically entailed by the original constraints and permanent valid assumptions.
A restart changes search decisions but not the underlying constraint semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding retained nogoods preserves the solution set while permitting stronger propagation after restart.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic validity of retaining learned nogoods across restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) denote the permanent constraint conjunction and \(N\) the retained nogoods. If \(F\models n\) for every \(n\in N\), then \[\operatorname{Sol}\!\left(F\land\bigwedge_{n\in N}n\right)=\operatorname{Sol}(F).\] Consequently, retaining \(N\) across a restart cannot remove a feasible solution. The retained nogoods may participate in propagation and conflict analysis in later runs, provided any nogood depending on a temporary assumption is discarded when that assumption ceases to hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logically entailed nogoods may survive restarts without changing feasibility, but clauses depending on removed temporary assumptions must be discarded.
knowledge_statements.title: Learned-Nogood Retention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits Learned-Nogood Retention, and the entailment condition correctly states the intended semantic safeguard. No cited CP source supports cross-restart nogood retention, propagation reuse, or the treatment of temporary assumptions.

children.title: Incumbent Retention
children.top_down_role: Covers preservation of the best known feasible solution across restarts.

assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(f(x)\) over feasible set \(X\).
The retained incumbent \(x^I\) remains feasible for the unchanged model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained value \(U=f(x^I)\) is a valid global upper bound after restart.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention of a feasible incumbent in minimization across randomized restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{f(x):x\in X\}\), suppose a pre-restart run found \(x^I\in X\). Retain \(x^I\) and \(U=f(x^I)\). Because restarting changes the explored search state rather than \(X\) or \(f\), \[\min_{x\in X}f(x)\le U.\] Hence \(U\) remains a valid global upper bound, and any later node whose valid lower bound is at least \(U\) may be pruned without losing a strictly improving solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent remains feasible after a search restart and supplies a valid upper bound for pruning in minimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Retention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits Incumbent Retention, and the minimization direction, feasibility assumption, upper-bound conclusion, and pruning qualification are consistent. A specific source is still required for incumbent retention across restarts and its use in pruning.

children.title: Objective-Bound Retention
children.top_down_role: Covers preservation of valid objective bounds across restarts.

assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(f(x)\) over an unchanged feasible set \(X\).
The retained bound \(U\) is certified by a feasible point or another valid global argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint \(f(x)<U\) preserves every solution strictly improving the retained bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention of a valid objective cutoff for exact minimization after restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a valid upper bound for \(z^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). After restart, retaining the objective cutoff means searching over \[X_U=\{x\in X:f(x)<U\}.\] Every feasible point strictly improving \(U\) belongs to \(X_U\), while no point with objective at least \(U\) can improve it. If ties must be enumerated, replace the strict cutoff by \(f(x)\le U\). The retained bound is invalidated if the model or objective changes incompatibly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid objective bound can be retained as a cutoff after restart, preserving all strictly improving feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Bound Retention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits Objective-Bound Retention, and the statement explicitly distinguishes strict improvement from tie enumeration. No source supports the cross-restart retention rule or the strict-cutoff convention for the intended exact-optimization setting.

children.title: Cross-Restart Retention Consistency
children.top_down_role: Covers compatibility between retained incumbents, retained bounds, revised search state, plus changed restart conditions.

assumptions_latex: Each restart epoch solves the same optimization model and objective.
Every retained incumbent, bound, or nogood carries the assumptions under which it was derived.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retained state is consistent exactly when every retained item remains valid under the next epoch's permanent assumptions.

notation.meaning: permanent assumptions in restart epoch k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for objective-related state transferred between restart epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) be the permanent model assumptions in epoch \(k\), and let \(R_k\) contain retained objective state. Cross-restart retention is consistent when \[\forall r\in R_k,\qquad \operatorname{Valid}(r\mid A_{k+1})=1.\] In particular, a retained incumbent must satisfy the next epoch's constraints, and a retained objective bound must remain justified for its objective and optimization direction. Any item failing this predicate must be recomputed or removed before it influences propagation or pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retained objective state is consistent only when every carried incumbent and bound remains valid under the next restart epoch's model assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Restart Retention Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is appropriate for Cross-Restart Retention Consistency. The abstract validity predicate gives a coherent necessary policy condition, but the claimed exact characterization and its application to retained objective state lack cited support and a source-grounded definition of validity.

children.title: Heuristic-Score Retention
children.top_down_role: Covers persistence, aging, or reset policies for accumulated heuristic scores.

assumptions_latex: The scoring rule permits initialization from an existing score vector.
Variable and value identities are preserved across the restart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retention initializes the next epoch with \(h^{k+1}_0=h^k_{\mathrm{end}}\) for preserved score components.

notation.meaning: heuristic score vector during restart epoch k
terminal score vector of epoch k
initial score vector of epoch k+1

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of branching heuristic scores between randomized restart epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h^k_{\mathrm{end}}\) be the terminal branching-score vector from restart epoch \(k\). Full heuristic-score retention initializes the next epoch by \[h^{k+1}_0=h^k_{\mathrm{end}}.\] Partial retention applies this equality only to designated components and initializes all others by the base policy.
