The transfer changes search ordering but not the feasible set, provided scores are used only to choose among admissible branching decisions and never as logical grounds for pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heuristic-score retention starts the next restart with selected branching scores learned during the preceding epoch.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic-Score Retention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role is compatible with Heuristic-Score Retention, and the statement separates search ordering from logical pruning. A CP-specific source is required for the score-transfer equation, partial-retention policy, and assumptions under which score identities persist across restarts.

children.title: Phase Retention
children.top_down_role: Covers persistence of preferred value phases or assignment directions.

assumptions_latex: Each decision variable has a finite domain.
Retained phases are used only as value-ordering preferences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next epoch prefers \(p_k(x)\) for variable \(x\) whenever \(p_k(x)\) remains in its current domain.

notation.meaning: retained preferred value for variable x after epoch k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phase-saving policy for value preferences across CP restart epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each decision variable \(x\in V\), let \(p_k(x)\) be its retained phase, such as its most recent assigned value in epoch \(k\). In epoch \(k+1\), when branching on \(x\), prefer \(p_k(x)\) if \(p_k(x)\in D(x)\); otherwise use the base value-ordering rule. Phase retention affects only branch ordering. Because propagation still rejects inconsistent assignments and all admissible alternatives remain searchable, the retained preference does not itself remove solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase retention reuses a variable's previous preferred value when still admissible, affecting branch order but not logical feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Phase Retention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits Phase Retention, and the domain-membership safeguard and ordering-only scope are explicit. No authoritative source is cited for phase saving across CP restarts or for the completeness conditions implicit in keeping all admissible alternatives searchable.

children.title: Cross-Restart Retention Policies
children.top_down_role: Covers coordinated retention regimes for heuristic state carried into a new search episode.

assumptions_latex: The constraint model and all sound learned constraints are fixed across restarts.
The heuristic state space is \(\mathcal H\), and \(R_k\subseteq\mathcal H\) denotes the components retained after run \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy produces the next heuristic state \(h_{k+1}=U_k(h_k,\sigma_k,R_k)\) while reinitializing every component outside \(R_k\).

notation.meaning: heuristic state used during run k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic policy covering score, phase, and other heuristic-state retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the heuristic state \(h_k\) and run statistics \(\sigma_k\), choose a retention set \(R_k\) and construct \(h_{k+1}=U_k(h_k,\sigma_k,R_k)\). The operator \(U_k\) must copy or transform precisely the components in \(R_k\), initialize every component in \(\mathcal H\setminus R_k\) from a prescribed distribution or default value, and leave the constraint model unchanged. Run \(k+1\) starts from the root search node using \(h_{k+1}\). A stopping rule returns the first solution, a proved optimum, or a proved infeasibility result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After each run, the policy retains selected heuristic components, resets the remainder, and starts root search again without changing the constraint model.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Restart Retention Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source or inspectable locator supports this retention-policy contract. Moreover, R_k is declared as a subset of the heuristic state space but is used as a set of state components; the underlying component index set and the type of U_k require clarification.

assumptions_latex: The solver state decomposes as \(S=(M,L,O,H,D)\): model, learned constraints, objective state, heuristic state, and current search decisions.
A declared retention set \(K\subseteq\{L,O,H\}\) contains only state valid for the unchanged model \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reinitialization yields \(S'=(M,L',O',H',\varnothing)\), with retained components copied according to \(K\) and all others reset.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-level reinitialization with an explicit separation between transient and retained state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a restart, discard the decision stack by setting \(D'=\varnothing\) and restore every variable domain to its root domain under \(M\) and the retained sound constraints. For each component \(X\in\{L,O,H\}\), set \(X'=X\) or apply its specified retention transform when \(X\in K\); otherwise set \(X'\) to its designated initial value. Propagate \(M\cup L'\) at the root before making a new decision. Output \(S'=(M,L',O',H',\varnothing)\), unless root propagation proves infeasibility or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart clears decisions and restores root domains, selectively retains valid learned, objective, or heuristic information, then performs root propagation.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-State Reinitialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The state decomposition, permitted retention transforms, root-domain restoration, and claimed root optimality detection are solver-specific assertions with no supporting citation or locator.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Section 4.7, when and why restarts help

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Optimal Speedup of Las Vegas Algorithms
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Optimal Speedup of Las Vegas Algorithms

assumptions_latex: A randomized complete search procedure is run on a fixed instance.
Its runtime \(T\) takes values in \(\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure is Las Vegas when \(\Pr(T<\infty)=1\) and every reported answer is correct.

notation.meaning: random runtime until a certified terminal answer
random seed or internal random choices

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime model for randomized exact constraint search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(x;\omega)\) be a randomized search algorithm on instance \(x\), and let \(T_x(\omega)\) be the number of search steps before it returns a terminal answer with a verifiable certificate. The algorithm is Las Vegas on \(x\) if every answer returned for every seed is correct and \(\Pr_\omega(T_x<\infty)=1\). Its runtime distribution may depend on \(x\), and its expected runtime is \(\mathbb E_\omega[T_x]\), which may be infinite despite almost-sure termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Las Vegas search algorithm never returns an incorrect answer and terminates with probability one, although its expected runtime can be infinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Las Vegas Search Model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically plausible, but no authoritative source is supplied. A source must also confirm the unusually strong every-seed correctness condition and the requirement that every terminal answer have a verifiable certificate.

assumptions_latex: Independent runs have a common runtime \(T\) with known distribution.
A fixed cutoff \(\tau>0\) is applied to every run, and \(p_\tau=\Pr(T\leq\tau)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The expected time to success is \(R(\tau)=\mathbb E[\min(T,\tau)]/p_\tau\), and an optimal fixed cutoff minimizes this quantity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent identically distributed runs with a known runtime law and zero restart overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Execute independent copies of the search, aborting each unsuccessful copy after \(\tau\) time units. The number of attempts through the successful attempt is geometric with parameter \(p_\tau\). With zero restart overhead, the expected total search time is \[R(\tau)=\frac{\mathbb E[\min(T,\tau)]}{\Pr(T\leq\tau)}.\] Consequently, among fixed-cutoff policies, any \(\tau^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\tau:p_\tau>0}R(\tau)\) is optimal. If each restart costs \(c\geq0\), replace the numerator by \(\mathbb E[\min(T,\tau)]+c(1-p_\tau)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For independent runs with known runtime distribution, the best fixed cutoff minimizes expected truncated run cost divided by the probability of finishing before that cutoff.
knowledge_statements.title: Known-Distribution Cutoff Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact expectation formula and restart-overhead convention have no citation. The record also needs source-backed confirmation that complexity_bound, rather than theorem or property, is the appropriate role for this exact finite expectation identity.

assumptions_latex: Independent runs share an unknown runtime distribution.
The base budget is \(b>0\), and each run uses a fresh random seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The schedule tests every dyadic cutoff \(2^j b\) infinitely often and succeeds almost surely whenever some finite cutoff has positive success probability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal dyadic restart scheduling when the runtime distribution is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the sequence \((u_k)_{k\geq1}=(1,1,2,1,1,2,4,\ldots)\), defined by concatenating, for each \(m\geq0\), the preceding block followed by \(2^m\). On attempt \(k\), run a fresh independent search for at most \(\tau_k=bu_k\) time units; return upon certified completion and otherwise restart. Because each value \(2^j\) recurs infinitely often, if \(\Pr(T\leq2^j b)>0\) for some \(j\), the probability that all corresponding attempts fail is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universal dyadic schedule repeatedly tries every power-of-two cutoff and therefore succeeds almost surely whenever one finite cutoff has positive success probability.
knowledge_statements.title: Distribution-Free Restart Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the stated universal dyadic sequence, its block construction, or its distribution-free completeness interpretation. The mathematical claim is plausible but cannot be accepted without a specific locator.

assumptions_latex: The runtime \(T\geq0\) satisfies \(\Pr(T>t)=t^{-\alpha}L(t)\) for sufficiently large \(t\), where \(\alpha>0\).
The function \(L\) is slowly varying.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(q>0\), \(\mathbb E[T^q]<\infty\) when \(q<\alpha\) and \(\mathbb E[T^q]=\infty\) when \(q>\alpha\); finite cutoffs can yield finite restarted expectation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularly varying runtime tails; the moment boundary case is intentionally excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A runtime distribution has a regularly varying heavy tail of index \(\alpha\) when \(\Pr(T>t)=t^{-\alpha}L(t)\) and \(L(ct)/L(t)\to1\) for every \(c>0\). Then moments below the index are finite and moments above it are infinite: \(\mathbb E[T^q]<\infty\) for \(0<q<\alpha\), while \(\mathbb E[T^q]=\infty\) for \(q>\alpha\). Nevertheless, any cutoff \(\tau\) with \(\Pr(T\leq\tau)>0\) gives restarted expectation \(\mathbb E[\min(T,\tau)]/\Pr(T\leq\tau)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularly varying runtimes may have infinite high-order moments, while restarting at any cutoff with positive completion probability yields finite expected completion time.
knowledge_statements.title: Heavy-Tailed Runtime Behavior

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regular-variation moment dichotomy and restarted-expectation claim are nontrivial and uncited. The deliberate omission of the boundary q=alpha is appropriate, but a specific authoritative locator is required.

assumptions_latex: Run \(k\) uses an independent seed and cutoff \(\tau_k\).
There exist \(\tau<\infty\) and \(p>0\) such that \(\Pr(T\leq\tau)\geq p\).
The set \(\{k:\tau_k\geq\tau\}\) is infinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restarted search terminates correctly with probability one.

notation.meaning: runtime of an independently seeded run
uniform completion probability by budget tau

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic completeness under infinitely many sufficiently long independent runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every terminal answer produced by the underlying search is correct. Let \(I=\{k:\tau_k\geq\tau\}\) be infinite, and assume each run indexed by \(I\), conditional on the preceding history, completes within \(\tau\) with probability at least \(p>0\). Then after \(m\) such runs the probability of no completion is at most \((1-p)^m\), which tends to zero. Hence the restarted procedure returns a correct terminal answer almost surely. Unbounded cutoffs are sufficient when the underlying runtime is finite almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completeness is preserved when infinitely many independent runs receive a budget having uniformly positive completion probability and all reported answers remain sound.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart-Preserved Completeness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional uniform-success theorem is coherent, but no source or locator supports it. The concluding assertion about unbounded cutoffs also requires explicit source confirmation under the stated runtime model.

assumptions_latex: Every successful trajectory requires at least \(L>0\) search steps from the root.
Every restart cutoff satisfies \(\tau_k<L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restarted search has success probability \(0\), even when an uninterrupted run would finish after \(L\) steps.

notation.meaning: minimum length of any successful trajectory

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp deterministic obstruction caused by uniformly premature cutoffs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a search instance for which no certificate can be reached in fewer than \(L\) steps, while some uninterrupted run reaches a certificate exactly at step \(L\). If the restart policy enforces \(\sup_k\tau_k<L\), every run is aborted before any certificate is reachable. Thus the total runtime is infinite and the success probability is zero, regardless of the number of restarts. This is restart thrashing: repeated root work consumes resources without allowing any run to cross the necessary search depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every cutoff is shorter than the minimum successful trajectory, restarts repeat shallow work forever and destroy completeness.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature-Restart Thrashing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No failure-boundary source is supplied. The assumptions require each cutoff to be below L, while the statement uses the stronger condition sup_k tau_k<L and additionally assumes existence of a run completing exactly at L; these formulations must be reconciled after sourcing.

assumptions_latex: The search trajectory is deterministic conditional on the model, initial state, and seed.
Every restart restores the same initial state and reuses the same seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All runs follow the same trajectory, so after \(m\) restarts the success probability remains \(p\in\{0,1\}\), rather than \(1-(1-p)^m\).

notation.meaning: success indicator for the repeated trajectory

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate restart correlation produced by identical seeds and retained initial state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the run outcome be the deterministic map \(Y=f(M,S_0,\omega)\in\{0,1\}\). If every restart uses the identical triple \((M,S_0,\omega)\), then \(Y_k=Y_1\) for every \(k\). Consequently, repeated restarts neither discover a new branch ordering nor amplify the chance of success: \(\Pr(\max_{1\leq k\leq m}Y_k=1)=\Pr(Y_1=1)\). The independent-run expression \(1-(1-p)^m\) is therefore invalid unless seeds or other trajectory-determining state actually diversify the runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restarting with the same seed and state reproduces one trajectory, so additional runs provide no independent chance of success.
knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Diversification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the diversification-failure model. The notation describes p as a success indicator, while the text uses it as a probability; with a fixed deterministic triple it is in {0,1}, whereas a once-randomized repeated triple may have an arbitrary marginal success probability.

assumptions_latex: Independent runtimes satisfy \(T=1\) with probability \(1-\varepsilon\) and \(T=M\) with probability \(\varepsilon\), where \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and \(M>1\).
Restart overhead is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cutoff \(1\) has expectation \(1/(1-\varepsilon)\), whereas any cutoff at least \(M\) has expectation \(1+\varepsilon(M-1)\), giving an unbounded ratio as \(M\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point runtime law demonstrating arbitrarily costly oversized cutoffs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the two-point runtime law \(\Pr(T=1)=1-\varepsilon\) and \(\Pr(T=M)=\varepsilon\), restarting after one unit succeeds geometrically and has expected total time \(R(1)=1/(1-\varepsilon)\). A cutoff \(\tau\geq M\) never restarts and has expectation \(R(\tau)=\mathbb E[T]=1+\varepsilon(M-1)\). For fixed \(\varepsilon\), the ratio \(R(\tau)/R(1)=(1-\varepsilon)(1+\varepsilon(M-1))\) diverges as \(M\to\infty\). Thus a cutoff at the wrong runtime scale can eliminate the restart advantage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-point runtime distribution shows that an oversized cutoff can be arbitrarily worse than restarting immediately after the common short runtime.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutoff-Scale Mismatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-point calculation is internally consistent and fits the cutoff-mismatch leaf, but the counterexample and its interpretation have no cited source or inspectable locator.

assumptions_latex: A retained heuristic state \(h^-\) deterministically selects a failing search basin within cutoff \(\tau\).
Fresh initialization selects a successful basin within \(\tau\) with probability \(p>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retaining \(h^-\) forever gives success probability \(0\), while fresh independent initialization gives success probability \(1-(1-p)^m\) after \(m\) runs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract basin model isolating harm from persistently retained misleading heuristic state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition root search trajectories into a successful basin \(B^+\), which reaches a certificate by time \(\tau\), and a failing basin \(B^-\), which does not. Suppose retained state \(h^-\) selects \(B^-\) with probability one, whereas a fresh state independently selects \(B^+\) with probability \(p>0\). Permanent retention of \(h^-\) makes every restarted run fail. Reinitialization instead succeeds within \(m\) runs with probability \(1-(1-p)^m\), tending to one. Retention is therefore harmful when stale state suppresses diversification without contributing sound inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistently retaining a misleading heuristic state can force every restart into one failing basin, while fresh states would eventually reach a successful basin.
knowledge_statements.title: Retained-State Pollution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract pollution model is uncited. The formula 1-(1-p)^m additionally requires independent fresh basin selections, which is stated in the main text but not included among the formal assumptions.

assumptions_latex: Each run starts from the root with an independently sampled configuration \(\omega_k\).
A run succeeds within budget \(\tau\) with common probability \(p>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After \(m\) runs, success probability is \(1-(1-p)^m\), and the expected number of runs through success is \(1/p\).

notation.meaning: independent configuration or seed for run k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent fixed-budget multistart without cross-run learning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k=1,2,\ldots,m\), independently sample \(\omega_k\), initialize a root search using \(\omega_k\), and execute it for at most \(\tau\) time units. Return immediately upon a certified terminal answer; otherwise discard all run-specific search and heuristic state before the next attempt. If no run succeeds, return failure-to-complete within the allocated portfolio budget. Under independent identical success events with probability \(p\), the probability of at least one success is \(1-(1-p)^m\), and an unlimited sequence uses a geometric number of runs with mean \(1/p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent multistart repeatedly samples a fresh search configuration, runs it for a fixed budget, and amplifies success probability geometrically across attempts.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Multistart Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and geometric amplification formulas are mathematically standard under independent identical run outcomes, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Diversified Search Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel portfolio for finite-domain constraint satisfaction or optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a constraint model \(M\), choose configurations \(A_1,\ldots,A_p\) that differ in branching, value ordering, random seed, restart schedule, or propagation strength. Run configuration \(A_i\) for an assigned resource budget \(b_i\), concurrently or by time slicing, with \(\sum_{i=1}^{p}b_i\leq B\). Each configuration explores only nodes permitted by \(M\). For satisfaction, stop when any configuration returns a feasible assignment; for minimization, return the feasible assignment having smallest objective value among all configurations when budget \(B\) is exhausted. If every configuration reports exhaustive failure, return infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run differently configured sound searches under a common budget and return the first feasible solution, best discovered objective value, or exhaustive infeasibility result.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}\) and \(b_i\geq0\).
Each \(A_i\) is sound for model \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathrm{out}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):x\text{ was found by some }A_i\}\) in the optimization case.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the portfolio leaf, but no source supports the resource-allocation model, configuration semantics, or exhaustive-infeasibility rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Learning Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Portfolio search with sound information exchanged among workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize workers \(A_1,\ldots,A_p\) on a common model \(M\) and a shared store \(S\). Whenever worker \(A_i\) derives an artifact \(a\), publish it only if \(a\) is valid for every worker's model, meaning that adding \(a\) cannot remove any globally feasible solution. Workers periodically import compatible artifacts from \(S\), propagate them, and continue search. In minimization, a feasible solution of value \(U\) may atomically replace the shared incumbent when it improves \(U\); imported objective cutoffs then use the new value. Return the best shared incumbent, or infeasible only after exhaustive sound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Portfolio workers exchange globally valid nogoods, bounds, or incumbents while preserving soundness and using shared improvements to reduce later search.
assumptions_latex: Every shared artifact \(a\) is entailed by the common model \(M\) or is a valid incumbent bound.
All incumbent updates are atomic and monotone for minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(M\land a)=\operatorname{Sol}(M)\) for learned artifacts, while the shared upper bound never increases.

notation.meaning: Shared nogood, bound, or other learned artifact.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the shared-learning leaf, but the treatment of entailed artifacts, incumbent bounds, and objective cutoffs requires an authoritative protocol-specific source.

children.title: Constraint Optimization Search
children.top_down_role: Exact and anytime search for objective-bearing constraint models, centered on branch-and-bound and its CP-specific propagation interface.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Finite constrained optimization and abstract branch and bound

knowledge_statements.title: Initial Incumbent Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal initialization for a finite minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a minimization model with feasible set \(F\), objective \(f\), and initialization budget \(B_0\), set the incumbent value to \(U=+\infty\). Run one or more sound feasibility heuristics until the budget is exhausted. Whenever a generated assignment \(x\) is verified to belong to \(F\) and \(f(x)<U\), set \((x^{I},U)\leftarrow(x,f(x))\). Output \((x^{I},U)\) if a feasible assignment was found; otherwise output the sentinel \((\bot,+\infty)\). Subsequent bounding search may use only the verified finite value \(U\) as a primal bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search briefly for a verified feasible solution, retain the best one found, and otherwise initialize the minimization bound at positive infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the feasible set and \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\).
Candidate feasibility and objective values can be verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{I}\in F\) and \(U=f(x^{I})\), or \((x^{I},U)=(\bot,+\infty)\).

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Incumbent Replacement Policies
children.top_down_role: Covers criteria governing replacement of the active incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Replacement Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone incumbent update rule for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain either no incumbent, represented by \((x^{I},U)=(\bot,+\infty)\), or a verified feasible incumbent satisfying \(U=f(x^{I})\). For each candidate \(y\), first verify that \(y\in F\) and evaluate \(f(y)\). If \(f(y)<U\), replace the incumbent by \((y,f(y))\). If \(f(y)=U\), optionally replace \(x^{I}\) by \(y\) exactly when a predetermined tie-breaking order \(\prec\) ranks \(y\) before \(x^{I}\); this replacement leaves \(U\) unchanged. Otherwise retain the current incumbent. Thus successive finite incumbent values form a nonincreasing sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a minimization incumbent with every verified strict improvement and optionally replace it by an equal-value solution preferred by a fixed tie-breaking order.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the feasible set and \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\).
Every admitted candidate \(y\) has verified feasibility and objective value.
The tie-breaking relation \(\prec\) is fixed before comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_{t+1}\leq U_t\), and every finite \(U_t\) is attained by a feasible incumbent.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Solution-Pool Management
children.top_down_role: Covers retention, diversity, capacity, plus lifecycle concerns for stored solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Pool Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-limited storage of verified feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a capacity \(K\geq1\), an equivalence relation \(\sim\) on feasible assignments, and a deterministic total priority order \(\preceq_t\) that may depend on objective value, diversity, and discovery time. At update time \(t\), verify a candidate \(y\); discard it if infeasible. Otherwise form the distinct candidate set from the old pool and \(y\) by retaining one representative per \(\sim\)-class, then retain its first \(K\) elements under \(\preceq_t\). The resulting pool \(P_t\) contains only verified feasible, pairwise nonequivalent assignments and satisfies \(|P_t|\leq K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verify incoming solutions, remove configured duplicates, and retain at most K feasible representatives according to a deterministic objective-and-diversity priority.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}\).
Candidate feasibility and equivalence under \(\sim\) are decidable.
\(\preceq_t\) is a deterministic total order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_t\subseteq F\), \(|P_t|\leq K\), and distinct members of \(P_t\) are not equivalent under \(\sim\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits solution-pool management, but its equivalence classes and time-dependent objective/diversity priority define a particular configurable policy for which no source is supplied.

children.title: Pool-to-Incumbent Promotion
children.top_down_role: Covers interfaces through which a stored solution becomes the active incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Pool-to-Incumbent Promotion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Promotion predicate for a minimization solution pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a nonempty pool of verified feasible solutions and let the current incumbent value be \(U\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). Select \(y\) from \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)\), resolving ties by a fixed order. Promote \(y\) to incumbent precisely when \(f(y)<U\). After promotion set \((x^{I},U)\leftarrow(y,f(y))\); otherwise leave the incumbent unchanged. If \(P\) is empty, promotion is undefined and no update occurs. This predicate ensures that promotion preserves feasibility and strictly improves every finite incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Promote the pool’s best verified solution exactly when it strictly improves the current minimization incumbent; an empty pool causes no update.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq F\) is finite.
Every value \(f(x)\) for \(x\in P\) is verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Promote}(y)\iff y\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)\land f(y)<U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and fits pool-to-incumbent promotion, but no source supports this exact strict-improvement promotion policy.

knowledge_statements.title: Cutoff Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-improvement cutoff for minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization problem with assignment space \(X\), feasible set \(F\subseteq X\), objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and incumbent value \(U\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). When \(U\) is finite and attained by a verified feasible incumbent, the strict-improvement cutoff constraint is \(f(x)<U\), and the surviving feasible set is \(F_U=\{x\in F:f(x)<U\}\). If \(f(F)\subseteq\mathbb{Z}\), then \(U\in\mathbb{Z}\) and the equivalent closed cutoff is \(f(x)\leq U-1\). With no incumbent, represented by \(U=+\infty\), the cutoff imposes no restriction. The non-strict cutoff \(f(x)\leq U\) is used instead when equal-valued solutions must remain eligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization cutoff retains solutions strictly better than a finite incumbent, equivalently those of value at most U−1 for an integer-valued objective; without an incumbent it imposes no restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is the feasible set and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is minimized.
\(U\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), and every finite \(U\) is attained by a verified feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_U=\{x\in F:f(x)<U\}\); if \(f(F)\subseteq\mathbb{Z}\) and \(U<+\infty\), then \(F_U=\{x\in F:f(x)\leq U-1\}\).

notation.meaning: Incumbent upper bound, or positive infinity when no incumbent exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Constraint Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound propagation after imposing an incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node with current domain store \(D\), constraints \(C\), objective \(f\), and finite incumbent \(U\), add the cutoff \(f(x)<U\) and apply a sound propagator \(P\) repeatedly to a fixpoint \(D^{*}\). Soundness requires that every assignment in \(D\) satisfying both \(C\) and the cutoff remains represented by \(D^{*}\). If \(D^{*}\) is empty, the node has no improving feasible completion and may be pruned. Otherwise the reduced domains, including the objective domain, are used for branching and further bound computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate the incumbent cutoff with all constraints, preserving every improving completion and pruning the node when propagation empties a domain.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is contracting, monotone, and solution preserving.
\(U\) is a verified incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(C\land f<U,D)\subseteq D^{*}\subseteq D\); if \(D^{*}=\varnothing\), no improving completion exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The propagation principle fits the leaf, but no CP propagation source is supplied, and the conclusion compares a solution set directly with domain stores without defining the representation relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Based Node Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-fathoming certificate for finite minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) denote the feasible completions of search node \(N\), let \(U\) be a verified incumbent value, and let \(L(N)\) be a certified lower bound satisfying \(L(N)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_N\). If \(L(N)\geq U\), then no completion of \(N\) can strictly improve the incumbent, so \(N\) may be pruned. The certificate consists of the incumbent solution attaining \(U\), together with verifiable data establishing the lower-bound inequality. If \(F_N\) is empty, infeasibility independently certifies pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prune a minimization node when its certified lower bound reaches the verified incumbent, because no completion can improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(U=f(x^{I})\) for a verified feasible incumbent \(x^{I}\).
\(L(N)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(N)\geq U\Longrightarrow \nexists x\in F_N\text{ with }f(x)<U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Node States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational states of a minimization search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A search node \(N\) is active while its propagated subproblem remains nonempty, is not bound-pruned, and still requires branching. It is infeasible when propagation or another certificate establishes \(F_N=\varnothing\). It is bound-pruned when a valid lower bound satisfies \(L(N)\geq U\). It is solved when all remaining decisions are fixed and its assignment has been checked, causing either incumbent consideration or infeasibility. It is expanded after sound child subproblems whose feasible completions cover \(F_N\) have been generated. The terminal states are infeasible, bound-pruned, solved, and expanded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node is active until it is certified infeasible, pruned by its bound, solved as a complete assignment, or expanded into covering children.
assumptions_latex: \(F_N\) denotes the feasible completions of node \(N\).
\(L(N)\) is a valid lower bound and \(U\) a verified incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{state}(N)\in\{\mathrm{active},\mathrm{infeasible},\mathrm{bound\mbox{-}pruned},\mathrm{solved},\mathrm{expanded}\}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible completion set at node N.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact state partition and the classification of expanded as terminal are framework-dependent; the generic branch-and-bound locator does not reliably support this operational vocabulary without full-text confirmation.

children.title: Bounding Sources
children.top_down_role: Search-facing classification only; the mathematical construction of relaxations and decompositions belongs to their owning chapters.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Derived Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective lower bounds obtained from a sound propagation fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(N\), apply sound constraint propagation to obtain a fixpoint domain store \(D^{*}\). Suppose propagation produces an objective-domain enclosure \(f(x)\in[\ell,u]\) for every feasible completion \(x\in F_N\). Then \(L_P(N)=\ell\) is a valid node lower bound for minimization. More generally, any value computed from \(D^{*}\) that is proved not to exceed \(f(x)\) for all \(x\in F_N\) is propagation-derived. If \(L_P(N)\geq U\), where \(U\) is the verified incumbent value, the node is safely prunable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower endpoint of a sound propagated objective enclosure bounds every feasible completion and can prune the node when it reaches the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: Propagation preserves every feasible completion of node \(N\).
The objective enclosure is valid for all assignments represented by \(D^{*}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_P(N)=\ell\leq\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\), hence \(L_P(N)\geq U\) certifies pruning.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound property is plausible, but no source establishes the assumed objective-domain enclosure or the exact relationship between the propagation fixpoint and feasible completions.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Specific Combinatorial Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-structure lower-bound certificate for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For node \(N\), a problem-specific combinatorial lower-bound certificate consists of a witness \(w\) and a polynomially checkable predicate \(V(N,w,B)\in\{0,1\}\) such that \(V(N,w,B)=1\) implies \(f(x)\geq B\) for every feasible completion \(x\in F_N\). The witness may encode a counting, packing, covering, matching, scheduling, or resource argument derived directly from the problem structure. When the verifier accepts, \(B\) is a valid lower bound; together with a verified incumbent value \(U\), the inequality \(B\geq U\) certifies that node \(N\) cannot contain a strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomially verifiable counting, packing, scheduling, or resource witness can certify a node lower bound and justify pruning when that bound reaches the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(F_N\) is the set of feasible completions of node \(N\).
The verifier \(V\) is sound for the modeled problem class.
\(U\) is attained by a verified feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(N,w,B)=1\Longrightarrow B\leq\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\); if \(B\geq U\), node \(N\) is prunable.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Based Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds for minimization nodes obtained by enlarging the node-feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feasible set at a search node be \(F\subseteq X\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and define \(z_F=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\). If \(R\subseteq X\) is a relaxation satisfying \(F\subseteq R\), then \[b_R:=\inf\{f(x):x\in R\}\le z_F.\] Thus \(b_R\) is a valid node lower bound. Given an incumbent value \(U\), the node may be pruned whenever \(b_R\ge U\). If two relaxations satisfy \(F\subseteq R_1\subseteq R_2\), then their bounds obey \(b_{R_2}\le b_{R_1}\le z_F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing over a superset of a node’s feasible region gives a valid lower bound; tighter nested relaxations cannot weaken that bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq X\).
\(f\) is bounded below on \(R\), allowing extended-real values if necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_R\le z_F\), and \(b_R\ge U\) certifies safe pruning.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the current search node
objective value of the best known feasible solution

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Based Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive lower bounds obtained from a separable relaxation of a minimization node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(m\ge 1\), let \(F\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be a node-feasible set, and let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\). Suppose \(R=R_1\times\cdots\times R_m\) satisfies \(F\subseteq R\). For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define the finite value \(b_i=\inf\{f_i(y):y\in R_i\}\in\mathbb{R}\). Then \[b_D:=\sum_{i=1}^m b_i=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x\in R\right\}\le\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}.\] Hence \(b_D\) is a valid lower bound for the original minimization node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a product relaxation with a separable objective and finite component infima, the sum of the component infima is a valid lower bound for the coupled minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(m\ge 1\).
\(F\subseteq R_1\times\cdots\times R_m\).
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the component infimum \(b_i\) is a finite real number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^m b_i\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: relaxed feasible region of component i

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-First Incumbent Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete depth-first branch-and-bound for a finite minimization search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a LIFO stack with the root node, set the incumbent value to \(U=+\infty\), and record no incumbent solution. Repeatedly pop the most recently inserted node, propagate its constraints, and discard it if it is infeasible or if its valid lower bound \(b\) satisfies \(b\ge U\). Whenever processing the node produces a feasible solution \(x\) with \(f(x)<U\), record \(x\) and set \(U=f(x)\). After this update, fathom the node only if propagation or complete evaluation proves that it has no unevaluated feasible completion with value below \(U\). Otherwise branch into finitely many children whose feasible sets cover all such completions and push the children onto the stack. Stop when the stack is empty; return the recorded incumbent, or report infeasibility if no feasible solution was found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explore the newest open node first, update the incumbent whenever a better solution is found, and continue branching unless the node is validly fathomed.
assumptions_latex: The branching tree is finite, and the children of each branched node cover every feasible completion not already conclusively evaluated.
Every pruning bound \(b\) is a valid lower bound for minimization.
A node is otherwise fathomed only when it has no unevaluated feasible completion that can improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon exhaustion, the returned incumbent is globally optimal, or the problem is infeasible if no incumbent exists.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at a node
a feasible solution produced while processing a node

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Bound Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-first branch-and-bound ordered by valid minimization lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the open set \(O\) with the root node, set the incumbent value to \(U=+\infty\), and assign every open node \(v\) a valid lower bound \(b(v)\). While \(O\ne\varnothing\), select a node \(v\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in O}b(w)\). If \(b(v)\ge U\), stop: the incumbent is optimal. Otherwise remove \(v\) from \(O\), propagate it, and discard it if it is infeasible. Whenever processing \(v\) produces a feasible solution \(x\) with \(f(x)<U\), record \(x\) and set \(U=f(x)\). Fathom \(v\) only if it has no unevaluated feasible completion with value below \(U\); otherwise branch and insert children covering all such completions, each with a valid bound. If \(O\) becomes empty, return the incumbent as optimal, or report infeasibility if no incumbent exists. At early optimality termination, \(\min_{w\in O}b(w)\) is a global lower bound equal to or greater than \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Always process an open node with the smallest valid lower bound, update incumbents without prematurely discarding remaining completions, and stop when no open node can improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: Every node bound \(b(v)\) is valid for every feasible completion in that node's subtree.
Branching is exhaustive, and the resulting search tree is finite.
A processed node is otherwise fathomed only when it has no unevaluated feasible completion that can improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite exhaustion or the condition \(\min_{v\in O}b(v)\ge U\) certifies global optimality when an incumbent exists; exhaustion without an incumbent certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for node v

children.title: Diving Search Phases
children.top_down_role: Covers phases prioritizing rapid descent toward complete candidate solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Diving Search Phases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The depth-oriented phase of a hybrid dive-to-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an open node \(v_0\). During a diving phase, repeatedly propagate the current node \(v_k\). If it is infeasible or its valid bound satisfies \(b(v_k)\ge U\), end the phase. If it supplies a feasible solution improving \(U\), update the incumbent and end or continue according to the fixed phase policy. Otherwise branch, retain all unselected children in the global open set, choose one child \(v_{k+1}\) by the diving heuristic, and continue. The phase also ends upon reaching a prescribed depth, node, failure, or time limit; all retained nodes remain eligible for later complete search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diving phase follows one heuristic child repeatedly while retaining alternatives, and ends at pruning, a solution, or a preset resource limit.
assumptions_latex: Unselected children are retained unless validly pruned.
Every bound used for pruning is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The phase explores one descent without sacrificing completeness when retained nodes are subsequently processed fairly.

notation.meaning: node at depth k of the current dive
valid bound at the current node

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Diving Search Phases leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no citation supports this particular retained-alternatives phase model, its stopping events, or its completeness qualification.

children.title: Best-Bound Search Phases
children.top_down_role: Covers phases prioritizing nodes according to objective-bound quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Bound Search Phases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bound-oriented phase of a hybrid dive-to-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O\) be the retained open-node set after a diving phase. During a best-bound phase, repeatedly select \(v\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in O}b(w)\), remove \(v\) from \(O\), propagate it, and discard it if infeasible or if \(b(v)\ge U\). Update the incumbent when an improving feasible solution is found; otherwise branch and insert every unpruned child into \(O\). End the phase when \(O=\varnothing\), when \(\min_{w\in O}b(w)\ge U\), or when the phase-switching policy triggers another dive. Preserve all remaining open nodes across the transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A best-bound phase processes retained nodes in increasing lower-bound order until optimality, exhaustion, or a policy-triggered return to diving.
assumptions_latex: Bounds \(b(v)\) are valid for their node subtrees.
Open nodes survive phase transitions unless validly pruned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The phase monotonically raises the global lower-bound frontier or proves that the incumbent cannot be improved.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound of node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the stated hybrid best-bound phase. Valid subtree bounds alone do not ensure that the displayed lower-bound frontier rises monotonically after branching unless a bound-consistency condition or an appropriate global-bound convention is added.

children.title: Phase-Switching Policies
children.top_down_role: Covers triggers for moving between diving behavior and bound-oriented behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Switching Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fairness condition ensuring completeness of alternating diving and best-bound phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an infinite sequence of search phases with retained open sets \(O_t\). A phase-switching policy is fair if every node \(v\) that enters some \(O_t\) and is never validly pruned is selected after finitely many subsequent node selections. Equivalently, no permanently eligible node may be postponed forever by repeated diving. A sufficient implementation is to impose a finite budget on every dive and to execute best-bound phases whose cumulative node budget is unbounded, with persistent open-node priorities. Under finite branching and exhaustive branching disjunctions, fairness makes the hybrid traversal complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A switching policy is fair when every unpruned open node is eventually selected; finite dives and unbounded cumulative best-bound work suffice.
assumptions_latex: Branching is finite and exhaustive.
Open nodes persist across phase changes unless validly pruned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fair phase switching yields complete enumeration of the unpruned search tree.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fairness definition is plausible, but the proposed sufficient implementation is not established: finite dive budgets and unbounded cumulative best-bound work do not alone preclude starvation without a precise persistent priority discipline. The meaning of completeness on an infinite tree also requires qualification and a source.

children.title: Hybrid Search Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers imbalance, excessive switching, plus loss of anytime or proof-search effectiveness.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Search Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of completeness caused by starvation under unfair phase switching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\ge1\), let a binary search tree have a retained right child \(r_k\) at the start of dive \(k\), and let the diving heuristic always choose a newly generated left child. Suppose every dive is restarted or extended before any retained right child is selected. Place the unique feasible optimum below \(r_1\), and let every visited left node have a valid bound strictly below the incumbent value. Then no visited node is prunable, yet the optimum is never reached. Thus retaining alternatives alone does not ensure completeness: without fairness or a finite global tree, repeated dives can starve an improving subtree indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated dives can postpone a retained improving subtree forever; without fairness or finiteness, the hybrid search need not find or prove the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The search tree may be infinite or generated without a finite global depth bound.
The switching policy may postpone a retained node indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hybrid dive-to-bound search is not complete when persistent open nodes can be starved.

notation.meaning: right child retained during dive k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind correctly identifies a failure boundary, and starvation is a plausible incompleteness mechanism. However, the constructed infinite-tree model and its claimed applicability to hybrid dive-to-bound search have no inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Anytime Objective Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interruptible finite minimization search maintaining feasible incumbents and certified lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the incumbent value to \(U_0=+\infty\) and the open-node set \(O_0\) with the root, whose bound is valid. After each search step \(t\), let \(U_t\) be the least objective value among the feasible solutions found so far, with \(U_t=+\infty\) if none has been found. If \(O_t\ne\varnothing\), define \[L_t:=\min\left\{U_t,\min_{v\in O_t}b(v)\right\};\] if \(O_t=\varnothing\) and an incumbent exists, define \(L_t:=U_t\). At any interruption with a finite incumbent, return its solution together with the certificate \(L_t\le z^*\le U_t\) and absolute gap \(U_t-L_t\). Continue processing nodes fairly, branching exhaustively and retaining every node not validly fathomed. On a finite search tree, uninterrupted execution eventually exhausts the open set or reaches \(L_t=U_t\), thereby certifying optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every interruption with a feasible incumbent, return the best solution found and a valid lower bound capped by its value; complete fair search on a finite tree eventually closes the certified gap.
assumptions_latex: Each open-node bound \(b(v)\) is valid for every feasible completion in that node's subtree.
Every feasible solution not already evaluated remains represented by an open node unless validly fathomed.
Branching is exhaustive, node processing is fair, and the complete search tree is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \(U_t<+\infty\), one has \(L_t\le z^*\le U_t\); equality \(L_t=U_t\) certifies optimality.

notation.meaning: open-node set after search step t
best feasible objective found by time t
certified global lower bound at time t
optimal objective value when the problem is feasible

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Objective Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain constraint optimization with one scalar minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite set of complete assignments, let \(C:X\to\{0,1\}\) encode constraint satisfaction, and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be a scalar objective. The single-objective minimization problem is \[z^*=\min\{f(x):x\in X,\ C(x)=1\}.\] A solution is any feasible assignment \(x^*\) attaining \(z^*\). If the feasible set is empty, the problem is infeasible. A maximization problem is represented by replacing \(f\) with \(-f\). A valid search bound at a node must bound this same scalar objective over every feasible completion of that node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-objective optimization chooses a feasible assignment minimizing one scalar function; maximization is obtained by negating that function.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite.
\(f(x)\) is defined for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimizer \(x^*\) satisfies \(C(x^*)=1\) and \(f(x^*)\le f(x)\) for every feasible \(x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-domain single-objective definition is precise, internally consistent, and appropriate for the leaf, but the record supplies neither an inspectable citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered multiobjective minimization with strict priority among objective components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a nonempty feasible set and let \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_p):F\to\mathbb{R}^p\). For distinct vectors \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}^p\), write \(a<_{\mathrm{lex}}b\) when, at the smallest index \(j\) satisfying \(a_j\ne b_j\), one has \(a_j<b_j\). A point \(x^*\in F\) is lexicographically optimal if no \(x\in F\) satisfies \(f(x)<_{\mathrm{lex}}f(x^*)\). For finite \(F\), it can be obtained by successively minimizing \(f_j\) over the feasible points fixed to the previously attained optimal values of \(f_1,\ldots,f_{j-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographic optimization minimizes the first objective, then the second without worsening the first, and continues in the prescribed priority order.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and nonempty.
The priority order is \(f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The successive restricted minimizations return a lexicographically minimal objective vector.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lexicographic order and successive finite-set optimization statement are mathematically coherent and fit the leaf, but no source or standard-field rationale is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Solution Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration of all nondominated objective vectors over a finite feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be finite and let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be minimized componentwise. Initialize \(P=\varnothing\). Enumerate every \(x\in F\). If some \(y\in P\) satisfies \(f(y)\le f(x)\) componentwise, discard \(x\). Otherwise remove every \(y\in P\) satisfying \(f(x)\le f(y)\) componentwise and insert \(x\) into \(P\). Equal objective vectors may be represented by one assignment or by all assignments, according to the declared output convention. After all feasible assignments have been processed, return \(P\); its objective vectors are exactly the nondominated vectors attainable on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate feasible assignments, discard dominated ones, and remove stored points dominated by each new point; the final set is exactly the Pareto frontier.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and can be completely enumerated.
All \(p\) objective components are minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(P)=\{f(x):x\in F\text{ and no }y\in F\text{ strictly dominates }x\}\), up to duplicate vectors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite enumeration algorithm is plausible and its content kind fits the leaf, but it has no citation. The conclusion also invokes strict dominance without defining it, and the output alternates between one representative per objective vector and all assignments without selecting a fixed convention.

children.title: Soft Constraint Objectives
children.top_down_role: Covers objectives induced by permitted constraint violations.

knowledge_statements.title: Soft Constraint Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain soft constraints represented by nonnegative violation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite set of decision variables with finite domains, let \(H\) be a set of hard constraints, and let \(S=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}\) be soft constraints. For each \(i\), choose a violation-cost function \(p_i\) from complete assignments to \(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\) such that \(p_i(x)=0\) whenever \(x\) satisfies \(c_i\). Given an aggregation map \(A:\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^m\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\), a soft-constraint objective is
\[P(x)=A\bigl(p_1(x),\ldots,p_m(x)\bigr),\]
and the associated optimization problem minimizes \(P(x)\) over assignments satisfying every constraint in \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A soft-constraint objective aggregates nonnegative costs for violated preferences while requiring every hard constraint to hold.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and all variable domains are finite.
\(p_i(x)\ge 0\), with \(p_i(x)=0\) whenever \(c_i\) is satisfied.
\(A\) is a specified nonnegative aggregation map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{A(p_1(x),\ldots,p_m(x)):x\models H\}\) defines the soft-constraint optimization problem.

notation.meaning: violation cost of soft constraint i

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the soft-constraint formalization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Soft Constraint Objectives leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no citation or inspectable locator supports the selected formalization and aggregation model.

children.title: Weighted Constraint Objectives
children.top_down_role: Covers objectives differentiated by constraint-specific importance or penalty weight.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Constraint Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted additive specialization of a finite soft-constraint objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a set of hard constraints and let \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\) be soft constraints with nonnegative violation measures \(v_i(x)\). Assign each soft constraint a weight \(w_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\). The weighted constraint objective is
\[P_w(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i v_i(x),\]
minimized over complete assignments \(x\) satisfying \(H\). For Boolean violation indicators, \(v_i(x)=1\) exactly when \(c_i\) is violated and \(v_i(x)=0\) otherwise; then \(P_w(x)\) is the total weight of violated soft constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted objective minimizes the sum of each soft constraint's violation measure multiplied by its nonnegative importance weight.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i\ge0\) and \(v_i(x)\ge0\) for every \(i\).
Candidate assignments satisfy all constraints in \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\models H}\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i v_i(x)\) is the weighted soft-constraint objective.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports weighted soft constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted additive definition fits the leaf and correctly specializes soft-constraint objectives, but it has no supporting source or locator.

children.title: Penalty Aggregation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers structural choices for combining violation penalties into optimization criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Aggregation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common scalar and ordered aggregations of soft-constraint penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a violation vector \(p(x)=(p_1(x),\ldots,p_m(x))\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^m\), standard aggregation regimes include the weighted sum
\[A_{\Sigma}(p)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i p_i,\]
the bottleneck penalty \(A_{\max}(p)=\max_i w_i p_i\), and lexicographic minimization of an ordered vector \((p_{\pi(1)},\ldots,p_{\pi(m)})\). The first two produce scalar objectives. The lexicographic regime declares \(p\) preferable to \(q\) when, at the first ordered component where they differ, the component of \(p\) is smaller.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalties may be aggregated additively, by their worst weighted component, or lexicographically according to a priority order.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i(x)\ge0\) and \(w_i\ge0\).
\(\pi\) is a permutation specifying lexicographic priority.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each stated regime induces a well-defined preorder for comparing feasible assignments by their penalty vectors.
review_flags: The supplied locators do not identify a source for these penalty aggregation regimes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation appropriately catalogs aggregation regimes, but no source supports the selected list. The lexicographic sentence also introduces p and q as comparison vectors without explicitly stating their domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal certificate for a finite-domain minimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(z^*=\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\), where \(F\) is the set of complete assignments satisfying all model constraints. An incumbent feasibility certificate is a complete assignment \(\bar x\), together with evaluable constraint values and objective value \(U=f(\bar x)\), for which direct checking establishes \(\bar x\in F\). The certificate proves that the model is feasible and, for minimization, that \(z^*\le U\). It does not by itself prove that \(\bar x\) is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checkable feasible assignment certifies feasibility and supplies an incumbent objective value, hence an upper bound for minimization.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(f\) are defined by evaluable model expressions.
The problem is stated as minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in F\) and \(U=f(\bar x)\) certify \(F\ne\varnothing\) and \(z^*\le U\).

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate from complete branch-and-bound exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z^*=\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\), suppose a finite search partitions \(F\) among terminal nodes. Let \(\bar x\in F\) have value \(U=f(\bar x)\). For every terminal node \(t\), provide a checkable certificate that its region is infeasible or a valid lower bound \(L_t\ge U\). If every search region is covered and every node is thus closed, then no feasible assignment has objective below \(U\). Consequently \(z^*=U\), and \(\bar x\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent is optimal when exhaustive search covers every region and certifiably excludes any solution with a better objective.
assumptions_latex: The search tree finitely covers the entire feasible set.
Each terminal node has a valid infeasibility certificate or lower bound.
\(\bar x\in F\) and \(U=f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L_t\ge U\) for every non-infeasible terminal region, then \(z^*=U\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for terminal node t

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and relative gap status for minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) be the value of a feasible incumbent for a minimization problem and let \(L\) be a valid global lower bound, so \(L\le z^*\le U\). The absolute gap is \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L\). Given a fixed scaling floor \(\delta>0\), the relative gap is
\[g_{\mathrm{rel}}=\frac{U-L}{\max\{\delta,|U|,|L|\}}.\]
The pair \((L,U)\) certifies that the unknown optimum lies in \([L,U]\). If either gap is at most its declared tolerance, it certifies optimality to that tolerance; if \(L=U\), it certifies exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid primal and dual bounds enclose the optimum; their difference reports absolute or scaled relative optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is attained by a feasible incumbent.
\(L\) is a valid global lower bound.
\(\delta>0\) and all tolerances are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^*\in[L,U]\), with exact optimality when \(L=U\).

notation.meaning: global dual or relaxation lower bound

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

review_flags: Relative-gap normalization is an explicit local convention.

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.title: Interrupted-Search Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified information retained when optimization search stops early.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a minimization search is interrupted after maintaining a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\) with value \(U\) and a valid lower bound \(L\) for every unexplored or active search region. Let \(L_{\mathrm{glob}}\) be the minimum of those regional bounds, also including any bound needed for regions not yet expanded. Then the interruption status certifies
\[L_{\mathrm{glob}}\le z^*\le U.\]
It certifies feasibility and the displayed gap, but not exact optimality unless \(L_{\mathrm{glob}}=U\). If no incumbent exists, it certifies neither feasibility nor a finite primal bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Early termination preserves valid bounds and any incumbent, but does not certify optimality unless the bounds coincide.
assumptions_latex: All retained regional lower bounds remain valid.
The reported incumbent, if present, is feasible.
The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With an incumbent, \(z^*\in[L_{\mathrm{glob}},U]\); exact optimality requires \(L_{\mathrm{glob}}=U\).

notation.meaning: best certified global lower bound at interruption

assumptions_latex: The search minimizes an objective and prunes by comparing node lower bounds with \(U\).
Every \(L_N\) is valid but may be non-tight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \(L_N<U\), objective dominance alone cannot prune node \(N\).

notation.meaning: lower bound at search node N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search degradation when node bounds remain far below the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization branch-and-bound with incumbent value \(U\). A node with valid lower bound \(L_N\) can be pruned by objective dominance only when \(L_N\ge U\). Thus, if a family of instances has many open nodes satisfying \(L_N<U\), although every feasible completion in those nodes has value at least \(U\), objective-dominance pruning cannot close those nodes. In the limiting case where \(L_N\) remains equal to a common trivial bound strictly below \(U\) throughout the tree, objective-dominance pruning closes no node before feasibility reasoning or exhaustive enumeration resolves it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds that remain below the incumbent cannot prune nodes by objective dominance, potentially reducing optimization search to near-exhaustive enumeration.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Objective Bounds

assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized by a search using incumbent-dominance pruning.
Node lower bounds \(L_N\) are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U_t=+\infty\), no finitely bounded node is incumbent-pruned; if \(L_N<U_t\), node \(N\) is not incumbent-pruned.

notation.meaning: incumbent value after t explored nodes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed primal solutions weaken incumbent-based pruning in minimization.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a minimization search, let \(U_t\) denote the incumbent value after \(t\) explored nodes, with \(U_t=+\infty\) before the first feasible assignment. A node \(N\) having lower bound \(L_N\) is prunable by incumbent dominance only if \(L_N\ge U_t\). Therefore, before the first incumbent no node with finite \(L_N\) is pruned by this rule; while \(U_t\) is poor, every node satisfying \(L_N<U_t\) remains unpruned by this rule. Delayed discovery of a strong incumbent can consequently enlarge the explored search tree when other pruning mechanisms and node bounds are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Until a good feasible solution is found, incumbent-dominance comparisons prune few or no nodes and may substantially enlarge the explored search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Propagation Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an incumbent cutoff to reduce variable domains locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a minimization node have current domain product \(D_N\), objective expression \(f\), and incumbent cutoff \(f(x)<U\). Objective propagation is ineffective at that node when enforcing the solver's chosen local consistency on the cutoff removes no value from any current variable domain, although some assignments in \(D_N\) violate the cutoff. Formally, if \(P\) is the propagation operator, the bottleneck condition is
\[P(D_N,f<U)=D_N\quad\text{and}\quad\exists x\in D_N:\ f(x)\ge U.\]
Then the cutoff's global exclusion is invisible to that propagator and must be exposed by branching or stronger inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective cutoff bottlenecks when local propagation removes nothing despite the current domains containing assignments that violate the cutoff.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a sound contracting propagation operator.
\(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the displayed condition, objective propagation yields no domain reduction at node \(N\).

notation.meaning: current domain product at node N

review_flags: No supplied locator supports this CP-specific propagation boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the displayed fixed-point condition captures ineffective cutoff propagation under a chosen local consistency. However, this CP-specific formalization has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Computation Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-node bounding cost can outweigh reductions in explored nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Compare a baseline search exploring \(N_0\) nodes at average non-bounding cost \(c_0\) with a strengthened search exploring \(N_1\) nodes, incurring average ordinary cost \(c_1\) and additional bound-computation cost \(b_1\) per node. Ignoring shared fixed costs, strengthened bounding is slower whenever
\[N_1(c_1+b_1)>N_0c_0.\]
Equivalently, its reduction in node count is insufficient when \(N_1/N_0>c_0/(c_1+b_1)\). This boundary concerns total computational work; stronger bounds may still reduce the search tree while increasing runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger bound is counterproductive when its per-node cost exceeds the computational savings from exploring fewer nodes.
assumptions_latex: The displayed average costs use the same computational resource and implementation context.
Fixed costs are equal or separately removed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(N_1(c_1+b_1)>N_0c_0\), the strengthened search has greater modeled total work.

notation.meaning: nodes explored by search variant j
additional bound cost per strengthened-search node

review_flags: The arithmetic boundary is explicit, but no supplied locator supports the runtime model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the work comparison is arithmetically sound under positive node counts and costs, but no source supports the runtime model or its interpretation.

children.title: Relaxation Selection

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of variables released from an incumbent in finite-domain LNS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a feasible incumbent \(x^{(k)}\), variables \(X\), a neighborhood-size rule, and a selection policy \(\sigma\). Choose a relaxation set \(R_k\subseteq X\) according to \(\sigma(x^{(k)},k)\), and fix every variable \(i\in X\setminus R_k\) to \(x_i^{(k)}\). Search the induced neighborhood
\[N_k=\{x:x_i=x_i^{(k)}\text{ for all }i\notin R_k\}\]
subject to the original constraints and the desired objective cutoff. Return an improving feasible assignment if found; otherwise retain \(x^{(k)}\). Stop under the declared iteration, time, or no-improvement limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LNS selects variables to release, fixes the remainder to the incumbent, and searches the resulting restricted neighborhood for improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(x^{(k)}\) satisfies the original hard constraints.
\(R_k\) is selected before reconstruction search.
The reconstruction subproblem preserves all original constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns either a feasible improving assignment in \(N_k\) or the unchanged incumbent \(x^{(k)}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically covers large-neighborhood-search relaxation selection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithmic role is plausible, but the statement covers reconstruction search, incumbent replacement, and stopping rules in addition to relaxation selection, overlapping the sibling Reconstruction Search and coupling containers. No LNS source is supplied to resolve the intended local scope.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reconstruction subproblem is \[\min\{f(x):x\in F,\ x_i=\bar x_i\text{ for every }i\in V\setminus R\}.\] Reconstruction search applies constraint propagation and a complete or resource-bounded CP search to this subproblem. It returns the best feasible solution found, or reports that none was found within the prescribed search limit. An improving return \(x'\) satisfies \(f(x')<f(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Relatedness-Based Destruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-neighborhood destroy operator using a symmetric pairwise relatedness score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an incumbent assignment \(\bar x\), variables \(V\), destruction size \(q\le |V|\), and symmetric relatedness \(r:V\times V\to\mathbb R\), choose a seed \(i_1\in V\) and set \(D_1=\{i_1\}\). For \(t=1,\ldots,q-1\), select \(i_{t+1}\in V\setminus D_t\) maximizing \(R(i,D_t)=\max_{j\in D_t}r(i,j)\), with a fixed or randomized tie rule, and set \(D_{t+1}=D_t\cup\{i_{t+1}\}\). knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Based Destruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Destruction defined by distance in a variable-interaction graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected variable-interaction graph, let \(\bar x\) be an incumbent, and let \(q\le |V|\). Choose a seed \(s\in V\), compute shortest-path distances \(d_G(s,i)\), and order \(V\) by nondecreasing \(d_G(s,i)\), resolving equal and infinite distances by a prescribed tie rule. Let \(D\) be the first \(q\) variables in this order. The operator unassigns exactly the variables in \(D\) and imposes \(x_i=\bar x_i\) for every \(i\in V\setminus D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a graph seed and relax the q variables closest to it in the interaction graph, fixing every other variable to its incumbent value.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite and \(1\le q\le |V|\).
Shortest-path distances use nonnegative edge lengths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned set satisfies \(|D|=q\) and is ordered outward from \(s\) by graph distance.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: graph-distance neighborhoods are a standard precise connectivity-based construction
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A specialized LNS source is needed to validate this graph-distance variant. The record also alternates between an unweighted graph and unspecified nonnegative edge lengths, so the intended distance model requires clarification.

children.title: Substructure-Based Destruction
children.top_down_role: Covers destruction sets aligned with recognized problem substructures.

knowledge_statements.title: Substructure-Based Destruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Destruction selects modeled substructures without replacement before resolving a size boundary.
