knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite variable set, \(\mathcal S\subseteq 2^V\) a finite family of modeled substructures, \(\bar x\) an incumbent assignment, and \(q\) an integer with \(1\le q\le |V|\). Select distinct substructures \(S_1,S_2,\ldots\) by a prescribed rule such that each selection strictly enlarges \(U_k=\bigcup_{j=1}^k S_j\), and stop at the first \(k\) for which \(|U_k|\ge q\). If \(|U_k|>q\), retain \(U_{k-1}\) and choose exactly \(q-|U_{k-1}|\) variables from \(S_k\setminus U_{k-1}\) by a prescribed boundary rule. Return the resulting set \(D\), unassign its variables, and impose \(x_i=\bar x_i\) for every \(i\in V\setminus D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select distinct modeled substructures that each add a new variable until their union reaches q variables, truncating the final substructure by a prescribed boundary rule when necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(\left|\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal S}S\right|\ge q\).
The selection rule chooses only an unselected substructure that adds at least one variable until the accumulated union reaches size \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The construction terminates and returns a substructure-derived set \(D\subseteq V\) with \(|D|=q\).

notation.meaning: union of the first k selected substructures

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: strictly expanding block-union selection yields a terminating cardinality-q construction

children.title: Connectivity-Aware Destruction
children.top_down_role: Covers operator variants that preserve or exploit connectivity within the released region.

knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity-Aware Destruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-constrained destruction explicitly rewards internal connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a weighted undirected interaction graph \(G=(V,E,w)\), incumbent \(\bar x\), and size \(q\), assign each \(D\subseteq V\) the connectivity score \(C(D)=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E,\ i,j\in D}w_{ij}\). Choose \(D\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{S\subseteq V,\ |S|=q}C(S)\), using a prescribed deterministic or randomized rule among maximizers. Unassign variables in \(D\) and impose \(x_i=\bar x_i\) for every \(i\in V\setminus D\). An approximate implementation must state its returned-score guarantee or its explicit termination rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select q variables whose induced interaction subgraph has maximum total edge weight, then fix every variable outside that set to the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E,w)\) is finite with \(w_{ij}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact operator returns a cardinality-\(q\) set maximizing \(C(D)\) over all such sets.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: induced-edge weight is a precise mathematical proxy for connectivity-aware selection
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact cardinality-constrained optimization is coherent and algorithm is the correct kind, but internal edge weight is only one possible connectivity proxy. A specialized source is needed to establish that this formulation matches the intended leaf.

children.title: Conflict-Guided Destruction
children.top_down_role: Covers destruction driven by recorded conflicts or repeated failure concentration.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Guided Destruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Destruction ranks variables by accumulated participation in failed-search conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be the variables and let \(\mathcal C\) be a multiset of recorded conflicts, where each \(C\in\mathcal C\) contains the variables implicated in a failed search state and has weight \(a_C\ge0\). Define \(s_i=\sum_{C\in\mathcal C:i\in C}a_C\). For destruction size \(q\), choose the \(q\) variables with largest \(s_i\), resolving ties by a prescribed rule. Return this set \(D\), unassign its variables, and fix every \(i\in V\setminus D\) to the incumbent value \(\bar x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score each variable by weighted conflict participation and relax the q highest-scoring variables, preserving incumbent values elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and the recorded conflict multiset \(\mathcal C\) are finite.
\(a_C\ge0\) and \(1\le q\le |V|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) contains exactly \(q\) variables of greatest aggregated conflict score under the stated tie rule.

notation.meaning: aggregated conflict score of variable i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weighted conflict participation is a standard search-evidence score
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted participation rule is precise and fits an algorithm container, but conflict representations and aggregation schemes vary. No source supports this particular top-q formulation.

children.title: Explanation-Guided Destruction
children.top_down_role: Covers destruction driven by explanatory dependencies from propagation or failure analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-Guided Destruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Destruction uses propagation explanations as weighted variable hyperedges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be the variables and \(\mathcal E\) a multiset of propagation explanations, each represented by a variable set \(E\subseteq V\) with weight \(a_E\ge0\). Choose a seed \(i_1\) and set \(D_1=\{i_1\}\). For \(t<q\), define \(r(i,D_t)=\sum_{E\in\mathcal E:i\in E,\ E\cap D_t\ne\varnothing}a_E\), choose a maximizer \(i_{t+1}\in V\setminus D_t\), and set \(D_{t+1}=D_t\cup\{i_{t+1}\}\). Return \(D_q\), unassign it, and fix variables outside it to their incumbent values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a seed, repeatedly relax the variable most strongly linked to the current set through recorded propagation explanations.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(\mathcal E\) are finite, and \(1\le q\le |V|\).
Each explanation has a nonnegative weight and identifies its participating variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The operator returns \(|D_q|=q\), with every added variable maximizing weighted explanatory overlap with the current set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explanations form hyperedges supporting a precise relatedness score
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hyperedge-overlap construction is mathematically coherent, but it is a solver-dependent formalization rather than a uniquely standard explanation-guided destroy operator. Specialized evidence is required.

children.title: Search-Evidence Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Covers consolidation of historical evidence used to rank destruction candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Evidence Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponentially decayed aggregation of variable-level evidence from successive search events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For variables \(V\), event times \(t=1,2,\ldots\), decay \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), and nonnegative event contributions \(e_i^{(t)}\), initialize \(s_i^{(0)}=0\) and update \(s_i^{(t)}=\lambda s_i^{(t-1)}+e_i^{(t)}\). Equivalently, after \(T\) events,
\[s_i^{(T)}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\lambda^{T-t}e_i^{(t)}.\]
Thus \(s_i^{(T)}\) combines conflicts, explanations, failures, or other evidence once each event has been mapped to \(e_i^{(t)}\). A destruction rule may rank variables by these scores, with ties resolved independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain each variable’s search-evidence score by exponential decay; the current score equals a recency-weighted sum of all recorded event contributions.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite, \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), and \(e_i^{(t)}\ge0\).
Each search event has a specified variable-level contribution map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(i\in V\) and \(T\ge1\), the recursive and weighted-sum representations of \(s_i^{(T)}\) coincide.

notation.meaning: event-t evidence contributed to variable i
aggregated evidence score after T events

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exponential decay has an elementary recursive and closed-form representation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive and closed-form expressions agree, and representation is the correct content kind. Nevertheless, no citation supports exponential decay as the intended search-evidence aggregation mechanism in this LNS context.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Contribution Destruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Destruction ranks incumbent variables by assigned additive objective contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization model with finite variables \(V\), incumbent \(\bar x\), and additively represented objective \(f(x)=c_0+\sum_{i\in V}f_i(x_i)\). Let \(b_i\) be a prescribed reference value and define the incumbent contribution score \(s_i=|f_i(\bar x_i)-f_i(b_i)|\). For a destruction size \(q\), select the \(q\) variables with largest \(s_i\), using a prescribed tie rule. Unassign the selected set \(D\) and impose \(x_i=\bar x_i\) for every \(i\in V\setminus D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an additive objective, relax the q variables with the largest incumbent objective contributions relative to specified reference values.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and \(1\le q\le |V|\).
The objective decomposition and reference values \(b_i\) are fixed before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned set \(D\) consists of exactly \(q\) variables having the greatest scores \(s_i\).

notation.meaning: objective term assigned to variable i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive objective terms permit a precise contribution ranking
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolute deviation from reference values is not a uniquely standard objective-contribution score, and the record does not explicitly require each reference value to lie in the domain of its objective term. A source is needed to determine the intended formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete CP Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimization of the finite CP neighborhood induced by a destroy set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite, let each domain \(D_i\) be finite, let \(F\subseteq\prod_{i\in V}D_i\) be the feasible set of a constraint optimization problem with objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), let \(\bar x\in F\) be an incumbent, and let \(R\subseteq V\) be the released variables. Define \(N(\bar x,R)=\{x\in F:x_i=\bar x_i\text{ for every }i\in V\setminus R\}\). Run a sound and complete CP optimization search over \(N(\bar x,R)\), terminating only after optimality has been established, and return \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in N(\bar x,R)}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix all variables outside the released set and completely optimize the resulting finite CP neighborhood, which contains the incumbent and is therefore nonempty.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and every domain \(D_i\) are finite.
The CP optimization procedure is sound and complete and uses valid objective bounds.
\(\bar x\in F\) and \(R\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search terminates and returns an optimizer of \(f\) over the nonempty neighborhood \(N(\bar x,R)\).

notation.meaning: feasible assignments of the original CP model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exhaustive finite-domain CP optimization establishes neighborhood optimality

children.title: Budgeted CP Repair
children.top_down_role: Covers CP repair constrained by time, nodes, failures, or comparable resource budgets.

knowledge_statements.title: Budgeted CP Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CP neighborhood search stopped by an explicit resource budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a repair neighborhood \(N(\bar x,R)\), objective \(f\), and resource budget \(B\), run a sound CP branch-and-bound search while counting a specified resource, such as expanded nodes, propagation calls, or elapsed time. Stop when the neighborhood search finishes or the count first reaches \(B\). Return the best feasible assignment found in \(N(\bar x,R)\); if none was found, return \(\bot\). Report optimality or infeasibility only when the search completed with a valid certificate before budget exhaustion; otherwise mark the result as incomplete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search the repair neighborhood until completion or budget exhaustion, returning the best repair found and claiming completeness only when certified.
assumptions_latex: \(B\ge0\) and the counted resource is specified before search.
Every returned assignment is checked against the repair neighborhood constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is feasible or \(\bot\); without completed search, neither \(\bot\) nor the incumbent repair certifies neighborhood infeasibility or optimality.

notation.meaning: no feasible repair found within the budget

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: resource-limited branch-and-bound has a standard incomplete-search contract
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incomplete-search contract is coherent and appropriately classified as an algorithm, but the source inventory does not support this CP-LNS repair regime or its budget semantics.

children.title: Discrepancy-Limited CP Repair
children.top_down_role: Covers CP repair constrained by deviation from preferred branching choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrepancy-Limited CP Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repair restricted by deviations from a prescribed branching heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N(\bar x,R)\) be a finite repair neighborhood with objective \(f:N(\bar x,R)\to\mathbb R\), and let a deterministic branching heuristic designate one preferred child at every internal search node. Assign discrepancy cost \(0\) to a preferred branch and \(1\) to every nonpreferred branch. For \(\Delta\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), run a sound and complete CP optimization search over exactly those root-to-leaf paths whose accumulated discrepancy cost is at most \(\Delta\). After exhausting that restricted region, return a feasible repair minimizing \(f\) there, or certify that the restricted region contains no feasible repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completely optimize over repair-search paths making at most Delta nonpreferred branching choices, or certify that this restricted region has no feasible repair.
assumptions_latex: \(N(\bar x,R)\) is finite.
The preferred child and discrepancy cost are defined at every branch.
The restricted CP optimization search is sound and complete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon exhaustion, the output minimizes \(f\) among feasible repairs reached with discrepancy at most \(\Delta\), or validly certifies that no such repair exists.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicitly defined discrepancy bound restricts search paths by nonpreferred branches

children.title: Joint Repair-Limit Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers repair configurations combining resource ceilings with discrepancy restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Repair-Limit Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repair simultaneously restricted by discrepancy and resource limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N(\bar x,R)\) be a finite repair neighborhood with objective \(f:N(\bar x,R)\to\mathbb R\), let a preferred-child branching heuristic define nonnegative discrepancy costs, and let \(\Delta\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(B\ge0\) be a discrepancy limit and a specified resource budget. Search only nodes whose root-to-node accumulated discrepancy is at most \(\Delta\), while counting the specified resource. Stop when this discrepancy-restricted region is exhausted or the resource count reaches \(B\). Return the feasible repair of least observed objective value, or \(\bot\) if none was found. Certify optimality or infeasibility within the discrepancy-restricted region only when that entire region has been soundly exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search a discrepancy-limited repair region subject to a resource budget, returning the best repair found and making completeness claims only after exhausting the restricted region.
assumptions_latex: \(N(\bar x,R)\) is finite, and discrepancy costs are defined at every branch.
\(\Delta\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), \(B\ge0\), and the counted resource is specified before search.
Every returned assignment is checked for membership in \(N(\bar x,R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Budget exhaustion yields only an incomplete best-so-far result; exhaustion of the discrepancy-restricted region establishes optimality with respect to \(f\) there or establishes its infeasibility.

notation.meaning: no feasible repair found before termination

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: intersecting explicit resource and discrepancy restrictions defines a joint stopping regime

children.title: Greedy Repair
children.top_down_role: Covers repair driven by locally ranked insertion or reassignment choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential greedy reconstruction with propagation; no backtracking guarantee is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the partial assignment \(p\) with \(p_i=x_i^{0}\) for every \(i\notin U\). While an unassigned variable remains, choose an admissible pair \((i,v)\) minimizing \(s(i,v\mid p)\) among values \(v\) whose tentative assignment survives propagation, set \(p_i=v\), and propagate to a fixpoint. If no admissible pair exists, return failure. When all variables are assigned, return \(x=p\) provided \(x\in F\); otherwise return failure. The score may combine incremental objective cost, domain impact, and constraint slack, but its chosen definition is fixed during one repair call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the retained incumbent values, repeatedly choose the best propagation-consistent variable-value assignment. Return the completed feasible assignment, or failure when no admissible choice remains.
assumptions_latex: The current incumbent is a feasible assignment \(x^{0}\in F\) for a finite-domain constraint model on variables indexed by \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with objective \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\).
A destruction step fixes variables outside \(U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and every candidate extension is checked by constraint propagation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a feasible repaired assignment, or failure if no admissible value can be selected.

notation.meaning: feasible assignments of the original constraint model
greedy score for assigning value v to variable i under partial assignment p
number of variables in the constraint model

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Constructive Repair
children.top_down_role: Covers repair that incrementally builds a complete feasible candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Constructive Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic propagation-guided constructive repair, allowing policy-specific backtracking or restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(p_i=x_i^{0}\) for \(i\notin U\), leave variables in \(U\) unassigned, and propagate the residual model. Repeatedly select an unassigned variable \(i\), choose \(v\) from its current domain, extend \(p\) by \(p_i=v\), and propagate. If propagation produces an empty domain, apply the policy's declared recovery rule, which may be backtracking, restarting, or immediate failure. Stop successfully only when every variable is assigned and all constraints hold. Return the resulting \(x\in F\), or report failure if the construction budget or recovery rule terminates first.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain nondestroyed values, construct values for released variables under propagation, and optionally recover from dead ends. Success requires a complete feasible assignment.
assumptions_latex: A finite-domain constraint model has feasible set \(F\), incumbent \(x^{0}\in F\), and a destroyed variable set \(U\).
A construction policy can select an unassigned variable and a value from its current propagated domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The repair succeeds exactly when construction reaches a complete assignment in \(F\); otherwise it reports failure under its stopping rule.

children.title: Hybrid Construction Policies
children.top_down_role: Covers repair regimes mixing greedy selection with broader construction guidance.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Construction Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid means policy selection or switching within one constructive repair call.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the residual problem from the retained incumbent values. At each construction decision \(t\), compute \(j_t=h(z_t)\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), invoke \(\pi_{j_t}\) to propose the next assignment or recovery action, and propagate the result. Update \(z_{t+1}\) and the controller's statistics using the observed domain reduction, objective change, failure, or elapsed resource. Policies may alternate deterministically or be selected adaptively. Stop on a complete feasible assignment, exhaustion of the repair budget, or satisfaction of the declared failure condition; return the feasible assignment when one exists and failure otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A controller selects or switches among constructive policies using the current repair state and feedback. Only a fully feasible completed assignment is returned as success.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many construction policies \(\Pi=\{\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_m\}\) sharing the same residual repair model.
A controller observes a repair state descriptor \(z_t\) and maintains policy-selection information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned assignment is accepted only if it satisfies the original constraints; policy mixing does not itself imply completeness or improvement.

assumptions_latex: The original problem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\), with incumbent \(x^{0}\in F\).
A destruction step releases coordinates \(U\) and fixes \(x_i=x_i^{0}\) for every \(i\notin U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any feasible optimizer output is a valid repair, and an exact solve yields an objective-minimizing assignment within the induced neighborhood.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the original model

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual optimization over released variables; solver technology is unspecified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the residual neighborhood \(N_U(x^{0})=\{x\in F:x_i=x_i^{0}\text{ for all }i\notin U\}\). Submit \(\min\{f(x):x\in N_U(x^{0})\}\) to an optimization solver with a declared time, node, conflict, or iteration budget. If the solver produces a feasible point \(\hat x\), return the best such point according to \(f\); otherwise report repair failure. If the residual problem is solved to proven optimality and is feasible, then \(\hat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in N_U(x^{0})}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix nondestroyed incumbent values and optimize over the resulting residual neighborhood. Return the best feasible solver output; exact solution gives the neighborhood optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Based Repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-neighborhood optimization algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits Optimization-Based Repair, but no inspectable source supports the LNS repair formulation and exact-optimality claim.

children.title: MIP-Based Repair
children.top_down_role: Covers repair subproblems delegated to mixed-integer optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: MIP-Based Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MIP encoding and bounded branch-and-bound solution of a residual LNS neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Build \(P_U\), optionally warm-start the MIP solver with \(x^{0}\), and solve \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in P_U\}\) subject to a declared resource limit. Return the best MIP-feasible solution \(\hat x\) found, or failure if none is found. If branch-and-bound terminates with an optimality certificate, then \(c^{\mathsf T}\hat x=\min_{x\in P_U}c^{\mathsf T}x\). If it terminates early, feasibility of \(\hat x\), rather than its bound gap, is sufficient for repair validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode the residual neighborhood as a MIP, solve it under a resource limit, and return the best feasible solution. Proven optimal termination supplies neighborhood optimality.
assumptions_latex: The original model has a feasible incumbent \(x^{0}\), and destruction releases the coordinate set \(U\).
The induced repair neighborhood admits a mixed-integer linear formulation \(P_U=\{x:Ax\le b,\ x_j\in\mathbb{Z}\text{ for }j\in I,\ x_i=x_i^{0}\text{ for }i\notin U\}\).
The repair objective is linear, \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible solver output repairs the incumbent, while a proved optimum minimizes \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(P_U\).

children.title: SAT-Based Repair
children.top_down_role: Covers repair subproblems delegated to Boolean satisfiability technology.

knowledge_statements.title: SAT-Based Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving SAT encoding, with optional objective-bound iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct \(\Phi_U\) after substituting retained incumbent values. Invoke a SAT solver under a declared conflict or time limit. If it returns a model \(y\models\Phi_U\), decode \(x=d(y)\), verify \(x\in F\), and return \(x\). For optimization, repeatedly add a stricter encoded bound than the best known objective and retain the best decoded feasible model. Return failure when the budget expires without a model; return infeasibility only when the solver proves \(\Phi_U\) unsatisfiable and the encoding preserves satisfiability in both directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode the residual neighborhood as SAT, solve it within a budget, decode and verify any model, and optionally tighten objective bounds across successive calls.
assumptions_latex: The original model has feasible set \(F\), and its residual repair constraints over released variables \(U\) have a satisfiability-preserving propositional encoding \(\Phi_U\).
Any optimization objective is represented by an explicit sequence of Boolean bounds or a weighted Boolean objective.
A decoding map \(d\) maps Boolean models of \(\Phi_U\) to assignments of the original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A decoded satisfying assignment is a valid repair after verification in \(F\); unsatisfiability is conclusive only when the encoding is faithful and the SAT call completes without a resource cutoff.

notation.meaning: feasible assignments of the original model
propositional encoding of the residual repair problem
decoding map from Boolean models to original assignments

children.title: CP-Based Repair
children.top_down_role: Covers repair subproblems handled through constraint-programming search.

knowledge_statements.title: CP-Based Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Native CP propagation and search on the residual neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Post the original constraints together with \(x_i=x_i^{0}\) for all \(i\notin U\), propagate to a fixpoint, and search over the remaining domains using the declared branching rule. Maintain the best complete assignment found according to \(f\) when an objective is present. Stop at the first feasible assignment, at proven neighborhood optimality, at proven infeasibility, or when the resource limit is reached, according to the repair policy. Return the best complete assignment \(\hat x\in N_U(x^{0})\), or failure if no such assignment was found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix retained values and use native CP propagation and branching on released variables. Return the best complete feasible assignment found or report the applicable failure outcome.
assumptions_latex: The original finite-domain constraint model has feasible set \(F\), incumbent \(x^{0}\in F\), released variables \(U\), and optionally an objective \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\).
The CP solver supports domain restriction, propagation, branching, and a declared resource limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned complete assignment belongs to \(F\); exhaustive CP search proves residual infeasibility when no resource cutoff occurs.

children.title: Cross-Solver Repair Portfolios
children.top_down_role: Covers selection or coordination among heterogeneous repair backends.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Solver Repair Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential or parallel allocation among heterogeneous residual-repair solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a residual neighborhood, choose allocations \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\ge 0\) satisfying \(\sum_{j=1}^{m}b_j\le B\). Run selected solvers sequentially or in parallel, translating the residual model into each solver's representation. Decode every candidate into the original variables, verify all original constraints, and maintain the feasible candidate minimizing \(q\). The scheduler may reallocate unused budget using observed progress. At budget exhaustion, return the best verified candidate; if none exists, return failure. A solver's proof is retained only when its encoding and decoding preserve the claimed feasibility or optimality property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate a repair budget among heterogeneous solvers, verify all decoded candidates in the original model, and return the feasible result with the best common evaluation score.
assumptions_latex: A finite portfolio \(S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_m\}\) contains repair procedures with sound decoding and feasibility verification.
A scheduler assigns each selected solver a nonnegative resource allocation whose sum does not exceed \(B\).
Verified feasible candidates are compared by a common scalar score \(q\) to be minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The portfolio returns the verified feasible repair with minimum observed score \(q\) within budget \(B\), and otherwise returns failure; completeness requires at least one complete solver to receive sufficient resources.

notation.meaning: common scalar evaluation score for verified feasible repairs

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Destruction Degree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-based fixed destruction; weighted or fractional destruction is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed-destruction-degree policy satisfies \(\lvert U_t\rvert=k\) for every LNS iteration \(t\), where \(k\) is independent of acceptance, repair success, elapsed time, and search history. The selection rule determining which \(k\) variables enter \(U_t\) may depend on the incumbent or randomization, but the cardinality may not. The boundary cases \(k=0\) and \(k=n\) respectively produce no released variables and complete destruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a constant number of variables to release at every LNS iteration. Variable identities may change, but the destroyed-set cardinality does not.
assumptions_latex: The model has \(n\) repairable variables and each LNS iteration selects a destroyed set \(U_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
A constant destruction parameter \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) is chosen before the iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iteration releases exactly \(k\) variables, so the destruction degree is invariant across search history and repair outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Reactive Neighborhood Sizing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback-controlled cardinality of the destroyed variable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(k_0\in[k_{\min},k_{\max}]\cap\mathbb{Z}\). At iteration \(t\), destroy exactly \(k_t\) variables, invoke repair under its declared budget, and record outcome \(r_t\). Update \(k_{t+1}=R(k_t,r_t)\), with \(R\) mapping into \([k_{\min},k_{\max}]\cap\mathbb{Z}\). The rule must specify how each relevant outcome changes or preserves size. Continue until the global LNS stopping condition holds, and output the best feasible incumbent encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After each repair, update the bounded destruction size from observed success, improvement, failure, or effort. The next neighborhood therefore responds to search feedback.
assumptions_latex: At iteration \(t\), the destruction size is \(k_t\in\{k_{\min},\ldots,k_{\max}\}\).
After repair, an observable outcome \(r_t\) is available, such as success, improvement, timeout, or search effort.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next neighborhood size is a bounded function of the observed search history rather than a fixed constant.

children.title: Progressive Neighborhood Expansion
children.top_down_role: Covers staged increases in the amount of incumbent structure released.

assumptions_latex: Neighborhood sizes satisfy integers \(1\le k_{\min}<k_{\max}\le n\).
An expansion factor \(\alpha>1\) and a declared expansion trigger are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever the trigger fires below \(k_{\max}\), the next destruction size strictly increases and never exceeds \(k_{\max}\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone size increase while the expansion regime remains active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(k_0\in[k_{\min},k_{\max}]\cap\mathbb{Z}\). After iteration \(t\), if the declared expansion trigger fires, set \(k_{t+1}=\min\{k_{\max},\max\{k_t+1,\lceil\alpha k_t\rceil\}\}\); otherwise retain \(k_{t+1}=k_t\) until another sizing regime is selected. Destroy exactly \(k_{t+1}\) variables at the next iteration. Thus expansion is strict whenever triggered with \(k_t<k_{\max}\), and repeated triggers reach \(k_{\max}\) in finitely many updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an expansion trigger fires, increase the destroyed-set size by a bounded multiplicative update. Repeated triggers eventually reach the configured maximum.
knowledge_statements.title: Progressive Neighborhood Expansion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded monotone update is mathematically correct, its algorithm role fits Progressive Neighborhood Expansion, and all notation is introduced. No inspectable source supports this specific expansion policy or its finite-arrival claim.

children.title: Progressive Neighborhood Contraction
children.top_down_role: Covers staged decreases in neighborhood scope to restore repair focus or feasibility.

assumptions_latex: Neighborhood sizes satisfy integers \(1\le k_{\min}<k_{\max}\le n\).
A contraction factor \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and a declared contraction trigger are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever the trigger fires above \(k_{\min}\), the next destruction size strictly decreases and never falls below \(k_{\min}\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone size decrease while the contraction regime remains active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(k_0\in[k_{\min},k_{\max}]\cap\mathbb{Z}\). After iteration \(t\), if the declared contraction trigger fires, set \(k_{t+1}=\max\{k_{\min},\min\{k_t-1,\lfloor\beta k_t\rfloor\}\}\); otherwise retain \(k_{t+1}=k_t\) until another sizing regime is selected. Destroy exactly \(k_{t+1}\) variables at the next iteration. Thus contraction is strict whenever triggered with \(k_t>k_{\min}\), and repeated triggers reach \(k_{\min}\) in finitely many updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a contraction trigger fires, decrease the destroyed-set size by a bounded multiplicative update. Repeated triggers eventually reach the configured minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Progressive Neighborhood Contraction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded monotone update is mathematically correct, its algorithm role fits Progressive Neighborhood Contraction, and all notation is introduced. No inspectable source supports this specific contraction policy or its finite-arrival claim.

children.title: Sizing-Direction Switching
children.top_down_role: Covers triggers for reversing the current neighborhood-sizing direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Sizing-Direction Switching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reactive switching between neighborhood expansion and contraction in large-neighborhood search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k_t\in\{k_{\min},\ldots,k_{\max}\}\) be the destruction size and \(d_t\in\{-1,+1\}\) its direction. After repair attempt \(t\), observe success \(s_t\in\{0,1\}\), where success means that an admissible solution satisfying the acceptance rule was found within budget. Given step \(\Delta\ge 1\) and failure threshold \(q\ge 1\), retain \(d_{t+1}=d_t\) unless either \(q\) consecutive failures occur or \(k_t\) reaches the boundary toward which \(d_t\) points; then set \(d_{t+1}=-d_t\). Update \[k_{t+1}=\min\{k_{\max},\max\{k_{\min},k_t+d_{t+1}\Delta\}\}.\] Output the repaired solution when accepted and the updated state \((k_{t+1},d_{t+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move destruction size in one direction, reverse after persistent failure or at a size boundary, and retain the resulting sizing state.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le k_{\min}\le k_{\max}\)
Each repair attempt returns a success indicator within a finite budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k_{t+1}\in\{k_{\min},\ldots,k_{\max}\}\), with direction reversed at the specified switching events.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The container and algorithm kind fit, but the exact reversal policy is design-specific and uncited. The state needed to detect q consecutive failures is also not explicitly maintained.

knowledge_statements.title: Repair-Budget-Aware Sizing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selects destruction size using an explicit computational budget for neighborhood repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For destruction sizes \(k\in K\), let \(\widehat T_t(k)>0\) estimate the repair resource required at iteration \(t\), and let \(B_t>0\) be the available resource budget. Given a desired size \(k_t^{\mathrm{des}}\), choose \[k_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{k\in K:\,\widehat T_t(k)\le B_t}|k-k_t^{\mathrm{des}}|.\] If the feasible index set is empty, choose a designated fallback size \(k_{\min}\). Destroy \(k_t\) decision components, run repair until it terminates or consumes \(B_t\), and update \(\widehat T_{t+1}\) from the observed resource use. Return any repaired solution produced within budget and the updated estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the desired destruction size when its predicted repair cost fits the budget; otherwise use the nearest affordable size or a fallback.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb N\) is finite and nonempty.
Resource consumption is observed on a common nonnegative scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected nonfallback size satisfies \(\widehat T_t(k_t)\le B_t\).

notation.meaning: predicted repair resource for size k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits repair-budget-aware sizing and is internally coherent, but its estimator, affordability rule, and fallback policy require an authoritative LNS source.

children.title: LNS Incumbent Trajectory Control
children.top_down_role: Only the LNS-facing interfaces are retained here; general acceptance metaheuristics belong to the local-search chapter.

knowledge_statements.title: Improving-Only Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict incumbent acceptance for a minimization-form large-neighborhood search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the feasible set, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be minimized, let \(x_t\in X\) be the incumbent, and let \(y_t\in X\) be a repaired candidate. The improving-only acceptance predicate is \[A_t(y_t)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(y_t)<f(x_t).\] The incumbent update is \[x_{t+1}=\begin{cases}y_t,&A_t(y_t)=1,\\x_t,&A_t(y_t)=0.\end{cases}\] Consequently, every accepted move is strictly improving and the incumbent-value sequence is nonincreasing: \(f(x_{t+1})\le f(x_t)\). Infeasible or absent repair outputs are rejected by convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a repaired candidate exactly when its objective is strictly better than the current feasible incumbent; otherwise retain the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\in X\)
The objective is expressed in minimization form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_t(y_t)=1\iff f(y_t)<f(x_t)\), and \(f(x_{t+1})\le f(x_t)\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly formalizes strict improving-only acceptance for minimization, but no inspectable citation supports its placement as LNS candidate knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Acceptance Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A common interface encompassing threshold, probabilistic, and history-dependent LNS acceptance rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_t\in X\) be the incumbent, \(y_t\in X\) a feasible repaired candidate, \(h_t\in H\) an acceptance state, and \(U_t\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\). A nonmonotone acceptance interface is specified by measurable maps \(p_t:X\times X\times H\to[0,1]\) and \(\Phi_t:H\times X\times X\times\{0,1\}\to H\). Set \[a_t=\mathbf 1\!\left\{U_t\le p_t(x_t,y_t,h_t)\right\},\qquad x_{t+1}=a_ty_t+(1-a_t)x_t,\qquad h_{t+1}=\Phi_t(h_t,x_t,y_t,a_t).\] Nonimproving moves are possible exactly when \(p_t(x,y,h)>0\) for some \(f(y)\ge f(x)\). Deterministic threshold rules arise when \(p_t\) is indicator-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent acceptance by a state-dependent probability and a state update, allowing deterministic or randomized acceptance of nonimproving repaired candidates.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the feasible solution set.
The objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is minimized.
\(U_t\) is independent of the current acceptance decision state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(a_t=1\mid x_t,y_t,h_t)=p_t(x_t,y_t,h_t)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the container and consistently covers deterministic and randomized rules, but this general interface is an uncited formalization rather than a sourced standard formulation.

children.title: Elite-Solution Management
children.top_down_role: Covers retention, diversity, replacement, plus capacity policies for elite solution sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Elite-Solution Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maintains a bounded archive of feasible LNS solutions using explicit quality and near-duplicate filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_t\subseteq X\) be an elite archive of capacity \(M\ge 1\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be minimized, and let \(\delta:X\times X\to\mathbb R_+\) measure dissimilarity. For a feasible candidate \(y_t\), if some \(e\in E_t\) satisfies \(\delta(y_t,e)<\rho\) and \(f(e)\le f(y_t)\), set \(E_{t+1}=E_t\). Otherwise remove every \(e\in E_t\) satisfying \(\delta(y_t,e)<\rho\) and \(f(y_t)\le f(e)\), insert \(y_t\), and, if the resulting set has more than \(M\) members, retain its \(M\) smallest-objective members using a fixed tie-breaking order. Infeasible candidates leave the archive unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject a feasible candidate dominated by a nearby archive member; otherwise replace nearby no-better members, insert the candidate, and retain at most M best members.
assumptions_latex: \(E_t\subseteq X\) and \(|E_t|\le M\)
\(M\ge 1\) and \(\rho\ge 0\)
A deterministic tie-breaking order is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{t+1}\subseteq X\) and \(|E_{t+1}|\le M\).

children.title: Reference-Solution Management
children.top_down_role: Covers selection, persistence, plus refresh policies for the solution guiding neighborhood generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference-Solution Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controls the solution from which an LNS neighborhood is generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_t\subseteq X\) be a nonempty elite archive and let \(r_t\in E_t\) be the current reference solution. After the archive update produces a finite nonempty set \(E_{t+1}\subseteq X\), let \(G_t\in\{0,1\}\) be a refresh predicate and let \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid E_{t+1})\) be a probability distribution supported on \(E_{t+1}\). Set \[r_{t+1}=\begin{cases}r_t,&G_t=0\text{ and }r_t\in E_{t+1},\\R_t,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad R_t\sim\pi_t(\cdot\mid E_{t+1}).\] The next destroy operator fixes and relaxes variables relative to \(r_{t+1}\). If \(r_t\notin E_{t+1}\), refresh is mandatory. Output \(r_{t+1}\) together with any updated selection state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep the current neighborhood reference when no refresh is requested and it remains archived; otherwise draw a replacement from the updated elite archive.
assumptions_latex: \(E_{t+1}\subseteq X\) is finite and nonempty.
\(\pi_t(e\mid E_{t+1})\ge 0\) for every \(e\in E_{t+1}\), and \(\sum_{e\in E_{t+1}}\pi_t(e\mid E_{t+1})=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{t+1}\in E_{t+1}\) almost surely.

children.title: Elite-to-Reference Promotion
children.top_down_role: Covers movement of stored elite solutions into the active reference role.

knowledge_statements.title: Elite-to-Reference Promotion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility and trigger condition for replacing an LNS reference by an elite solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_t\in X\) be the current reference, \(E_t\subseteq X\) the elite archive, and \(S_t:E_t\times X\to\mathbb R\) a promotion score, with larger values preferred. Given eligibility predicate \(Q_t:E_t\times X\to\{0,1\}\) and threshold \(\tau_t\), define \[P_t=\{e\in E_t:Q_t(e,r_t)=1,\ S_t(e,r_t)\ge\tau_t\}.\] Promotion occurs precisely when \(P_t\ne\varnothing\); then \[r_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{e\in P_t}S_t(e,r_t),\] using a fixed tie-breaker. If \(P_t=\varnothing\), set \(r_{t+1}=r_t\). Thus only eligible archived solutions meeting the promotion threshold can become references.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Promote the highest-scoring eligible elite solution when it meets a threshold; otherwise keep the current reference.
assumptions_latex: \(E_t\) is finite.
A deterministic tie-breaking order is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_t\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow r_{t+1}\in P_t\), while \(P_t=\varnothing\Rightarrow r_{t+1}=r_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits elite-to-reference promotion and is mathematically coherent, but the score, eligibility rule, and threshold are wholly policy-dependent and uncited.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: A Survey of Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search Algorithms and Applications
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: A Survey of Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search Algorithms and Applications

children.title: Destroy Operator Portfolios
children.top_down_role: Covers collections of alternative neighborhood-destruction operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Destroy Operator Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite family of neighborhood-destruction mappings used by adaptive large-neighborhood search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) be the feasible set. A destroy-operator portfolio is a finite indexed family \(\mathcal D=\{D_i:i\in I\}\) such that each possibly randomized map \(D_i\) sends a reference solution \(x\in X\) and state \(h\in H\) to a partial assignment \(p=D_i(x,h)\). Every variable fixed by \(p\) takes its value from \(x\); the remaining variables form the relaxed set \(R_i(x,h)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The associated neighborhood is \[N_i(x,h)=\{y\in X:y_j=x_j\text{ for every }j\notin R_i(x,h)\}.\] Portfolio selection chooses an index in \(I\) before repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A destroy portfolio is a finite family of mappings that relax selected variables of a reference solution and thereby define repair neighborhoods.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and nonempty.
Each reference solution belongs to \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in N_i(x,h)\subseteq X\) for every \(i\in I\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the destroy-portfolio container, but no cited ALNS source supports this particular partial-assignment formalization.

children.title: Repair Operator Portfolios
children.top_down_role: Covers collections of alternative reconstruction or repair operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Repair Operator Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite family of procedures for completing destroyed partial assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a set of partial assignments and \(X\) the feasible set. A repair-operator portfolio is a finite indexed family \(\mathcal R=\{R_j:j\in J\}\) of possibly randomized, budgeted procedures. For \(p\in P\), state \(h\in H\), and budget \(B\ge0\), each procedure returns \[R_j(p,h,B)\in X(p)\cup\{\bot\},\qquad X(p)=\{x\in X:x\text{ extends }p\},\] where \(\bot\) denotes failure to produce a completion within budget. A valid repair may use propagation, constructive insertion, local search, or exact subproblem search, but any nonfailure output must preserve every assignment fixed by \(p\) and satisfy all original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repair portfolio is a finite family of budgeted completion procedures whose successful outputs extend the destroyed partial assignment and are feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and nonempty.
All operators use the same original feasible set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_j(p,h,B)\ne\bot\Rightarrow R_j(p,h,B)\in X(p)\).

notation.meaning: feasible completions of partial assignment p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly specifies successful repair outputs as feasible extensions, but its budgeted procedure model has no inspectable supporting source.

children.title: Paired Operator Selection
children.top_down_role: Covers selection of a destroy operator together with a compatible repair operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Paired Operator Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selects a compatible destroy-repair pair as one adaptive action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) and \(J\) index destroy and repair portfolios, and let \(C\subseteq I\times J\) be the nonempty set of compatible pairs. At iteration \(t\), assign each pair a positive weight \(w_{ij,t}\) and select \[(i_t,j_t)\sim p_t,\qquad p_t(i,j)=\frac{w_{ij,t}}{\sum_{(a,b)\in C}w_{ab,t}}\quad((i,j)\in C).\] Apply destroy operator \(i_t\), then repair operator \(j_t\), observe reward \(q_t\), and update the chosen weight by \[w_{i_tj_t,t+1}=(1-\lambda)w_{i_tj_t,t}+\lambda q_t,\] leaving other weights unchanged. Output the repaired candidate and updated pair weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a compatible destroy-repair pair from pair weights, execute it, and update the selected pair's weight from its observed reward.
assumptions_latex: \(C\ne\varnothing\)
\(w_{ij,t}>0\) for every \((i,j)\in C\)
\(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(q_t>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_t\) is a probability distribution supported exactly on \(C\), and updated weights remain positive.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits paired operator selection and its probability and positivity conclusions follow from the assumptions, but the pairwise reward update is a specific uncited policy.

children.title: Operator Compatibility Structure
children.top_down_role: Covers structural restrictions or affinities among portfolio components.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator Compatibility Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bipartite representation of admissible destroy-repair compositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) and \(J\) index destroy and repair operators. Their compatibility structure is the bipartite graph \(G=(I\mathbin{\dot\cup}J,C)\), equivalently the matrix \(M\in\{0,1\}^{I\times J}\), with \[M_{ij}=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(i,j)\in C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R_j(D_i(x,h),h,B)\text{ is type-valid for every admissible }(x,h,B).\] Here type-valid means that the destroy output belongs to the repair operator's declared input domain and that every successful repair output is a feasible completion. A paired selection distribution \(p\) respects compatibility exactly when \(p(i,j)=0\) whenever \(M_{ij}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode valid destroy-repair compositions as edges of a bipartite graph or ones in a binary matrix, and forbid selection outside those edges.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(J\) are finite.
Every operator has a declared input-output contract.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is compatibility-respecting if and only if \(\operatorname{supp}(p)\subseteq C\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bipartite representation fits the container, but universal type-validity is a formalization choice requiring an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Performance-Based Operator Scoring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Updates adaptive operator scores from observed search outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For operators \(i\in I\), initialize scores \(s_{i,0}\in\mathbb R\) and counts \(n_{i,0}=0\). When operator \(i_t\) is applied at iteration \(t\), compute a bounded reward \(q_t\) from its outcome, such as prescribed values for a new global best, an improving accepted solution, another accepted solution, or rejection. With reaction factor \(0<\lambda\le1\), update \[s_{i_t,t+1}=(1-\lambda)s_{i_t,t}+\lambda q_t,\qquad n_{i_t,t+1}=n_{i_t,t}+1,\] and leave unselected scores and counts unchanged. Subsequent selection uses a specified increasing transformation of scores, with explicit exploration ensuring that no eligible operator is permanently excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign outcome-dependent rewards, exponentially smooth the selected operator's score, and use increasing score-based probabilities while retaining exploration.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and nonempty.
Rewards satisfy \(q_t\in[q_{\min},q_{\max}]\).
The selection rule assigns positive probability to every eligible operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(s_{i,0}\in[q_{\min},q_{\max}]\), then \(s_{i,t}\in[q_{\min},q_{\max}]\) for all \(t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits performance-based scoring and the bounded-score conclusion is correct, but the reward categories, smoothing update, selection transform, and exploration requirement need an authoritative ALNS source.

children.title: Bandit-Guided Selection
children.top_down_role: Covers operator choice framed through reward-driven exploration versus exploitation.

knowledge_statements.title: Bandit-Guided Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: UCB selection of destroy–repair operators using observed LNS rewards.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given operators \(\mathcal O=\{1,\ldots,K\}\), initialize \(n_i=0\) and \(S_i=0\). At iteration \(t\), select every untried operator once; thereafter choose \[i_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in\mathcal O}\left(\frac{S_i}{n_i}+c\sqrt{\frac{\log t}{n_i}}\right).\] Apply \(i_t\) to the current incumbent, run the associated repair search, and observe a bounded reward \(r_t\in[0,1]\). Update \(n_{i_t}\leftarrow n_{i_t}+1\) and \(S_{i_t}\leftarrow S_{i_t}+r_t\); leave other statistics unchanged. Stop at the prescribed search limit and return the best feasible solution encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select each LNS operator by an upper-confidence score combining its average observed reward with an exploration bonus, then update only the selected operator’s statistics.
assumptions_latex: \(K<\infty\) and \(c>0\).
Each selected operator yields an observable reward \(r_t\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i_t\) is selected by the stated upper-confidence rule, and the algorithm outputs the best feasible solution observed.

notation.meaning: selection count and cumulative reward of operator i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, and the UCB rule is internally coherent, but no citation supports this reward model or its use for LNS operator selection.

children.title: Learned Operator Selection
children.top_down_role: Covers predictive or policy-based selection learned from search observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Learned Operator Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Context-dependent LNS operator selection learned from recorded search outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal O\) be a finite operator portfolio and let \(\phi_t\in\mathbb R^d\) encode the incumbent, search history, and instance state at iteration \(t\). Given a predictor \(g_\theta(\phi,i)\), choose \[i_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in\mathcal O}g_\theta(\phi_t,i),\] optionally subject to a specified exploration policy. Apply \(i_t\), observe reward \(r_t\), append \((\phi_t,i_t,r_t)\) to the training data, and update \(\theta\) by the prescribed supervised, contextual-bandit, or reinforcement-learning rule. At termination, return the best feasible solution found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode the current search state, predict each operator’s utility, select an operator with optional exploration, and update the predictor from the resulting reward.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal O\) is finite and every context \(\phi_t\) is observable before selection.
The learning rule and exploration policy are fixed as part of the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected operator maximizes the current predicted utility, subject to the declared exploration policy.

notation.meaning: features describing the iteration-t search context

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but supervised learning, contextual bandits, and reinforcement learning do not share the single generic update claimed here. A targeted source is needed to select and specify a supported regime.

children.title: Selection-Feedback Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers attribution horizons, reward signals, plus delayed feedback affecting adaptive selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection-Feedback Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information regimes governing feedback available to an adaptive LNS selector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite operator set \(\mathcal O\), let \(r_t(i)\) denote the reward that operator \(i\) would yield in context \(t\), and let \(i_t\) be the selected operator. A full-information regime reveals \(r_t(i)\) for every \(i\in\mathcal O\); a bandit regime reveals only \(r_t(i_t)\); and a delayed regime reveals the designated feedback after a delay \(d_t\ge 1\). Feedback is censored when the prescribed search limit can prevent an initiated operator’s reward from being observed. The selector’s update at time \(t\) may use only rewards revealed by that time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selection feedback may expose all operator rewards, only the chosen operator’s reward, delayed rewards, or rewards censored by termination.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal O\) is finite.
A reward and its observation time are defined for every executed operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selector’s admissible history consists exactly of feedback revealed no later than the current decision time.

notation.meaning: potential reward of operator i in context t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the feedback-regime leaf, but no source supports this taxonomy, and rewards for unexecuted operators require an explicit potential-outcome model in state-changing LNS.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Parameter Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online adjustment of LNS parameters from measured search performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda\) be an admissible parameter set, \(\lambda_t\in\Lambda\) the parameters used at iteration \(t\), and \(y_t\) an observed performance signal. Initialize \(\lambda_1\in\Lambda\). After executing the LNS iteration with \(\lambda_t\), update \[\lambda_{t+1}=\Pi_\Lambda\!\left(U(\lambda_t,y_t,h_t)\right),\] where \(h_t\) is the available search history, \(U\) is a specified feedback controller, and \(\Pi_\Lambda\) restores admissibility. Stop at the search limit and return the best feasible solution found together with the final parameter state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run LNS with current parameters, measure performance, apply a declared feedback update, and project the new parameters back into their admissible domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\Lambda\ne\varnothing\) and a projection or admissibility map \(\Pi_\Lambda\) is defined.
The signal \(y_t\) is observable after iteration \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_t\in\Lambda\) for every executed iteration, and the best observed feasible solution is returned.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is plausible, but the projection-and-controller template is not a specific adaptive LNS method and has no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Guided LNS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LNS neighborhoods defined by fixing variables to incumbent-solution values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-domain constraint optimization problem with variables \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\), feasible set \(F\), objective \(f\) to minimize, and incumbent \(x^t\in F\). Select a relaxation set \(R_t\subseteq X\), impose \(x_j=x_j^t\) for every \(x_j\notin R_t\), and solve the resulting subproblem within a prescribed resource limit. If it yields \(y\in F\) with \(f(y)<f(x^t)\), set \(x^{t+1}=y\); otherwise retain \(x^{t+1}=x^t\). Repeat until the global stopping condition and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax selected variables while fixing all others to their incumbent values; accept a strictly improving feasible repair and otherwise retain the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: All variables have finite domains and an initial incumbent \(x^0\in F\) is available.
The objective \(f\) is minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every incumbent is feasible and \(f(x^{t+1})\le f(x^t)\) at each iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and incumbent-fixing construction match solution-guided LNS, but the strict-improvement acceptance rule is only one variant and lacks a targeted source.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Guided LNS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LNS neighborhood construction driven by CP propagation effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^t\) be a feasible incumbent for a finite-domain constraint model. Compute propagation scores \(p_t(j)\) for variables \(x_j\), using a declared statistic such as domain reduction, failure participation, or induced fixing under incumbent assignments. Choose a relaxation set \(R_t\) from these scores, fix \(x_j=x_j^t\) for \(x_j\notin R_t\), propagate the restricted model to a fixpoint, and search the residual subproblem within a resource limit. Accept any feasible candidate satisfying the declared acceptance rule; otherwise retain \(x^t\). Return the best feasible incumbent at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score variables by measured propagation effects, relax a score-derived subset, propagate the restricted model, and search the remaining neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: The constraint propagators terminate and are sound.
The propagation statistic and score-to-neighborhood rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted candidate satisfies the original constraints, and the output is the best feasible incumbent observed.

notation.meaning: propagation score of variable j at iteration t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but domain reduction, failure participation, and induced fixing are distinct propagation-guidance mechanisms. A targeted source must identify and support the intended variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-Guided LNS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LNS neighborhoods constructed from explanations of failures or objective bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^t\) be a feasible incumbent and let the CP solver provide sound explanations, each represented by a set of assignments sufficient for a propagation, conflict, or objective-bound inference. From explanations collected during recent neighborhood searches, compute assignment scores \(e_t(a)\). Select a set of incumbent assignments to relax according to those scores, retain all remaining incumbent assignments, propagate, and search the resulting subproblem within a resource limit. Update the explanation statistics from the search outcome, apply the declared acceptance rule, and return the best feasible incumbent encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use solver explanations to score incumbent assignments, relax selected high-priority assignments, and update the scores after searching the resulting neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: Every recorded explanation is sound for the modeled constraints.
The explanation-scoring and relaxation rules are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained assignments define a valid restricted subproblem, and every reported incumbent is feasible for the original model.

notation.meaning: iteration-t score of incumbent assignment a
a variable–value assignment from the incumbent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the explanation representation, scoring direction, and neighborhood-construction rule are method-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart-Based LNS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated bounded neighborhood searches with restart-triggered diversification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from a feasible incumbent \(x^0\), execute consecutive LNS epochs. In epoch \(k\), initialize the neighborhood policy and search state, then perform bounded destroy–repair iterations until a restart trigger \(T_k\) occurs, such as a failure, time, node, or stagnation threshold. Preserve the best feasible incumbent, discard the designated epoch-local state, update the restart schedule or neighborhood parameters, and begin epoch \(k+1\) from that incumbent or from a declared diversified seed. Stop at the global resource limit and return the best feasible solution found across all epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition LNS into bounded epochs; at each trigger preserve the best incumbent, reset designated local state, optionally diversify, and begin a new epoch.
assumptions_latex: An initial feasible incumbent is available.
Each restart trigger and the state retained across restarts are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned solution is the best feasible incumbent observed over all completed and partial epochs.

notation.meaning: incumbent retained at the start of epoch k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but retained state, restart triggers, and diversified reseeding define materially different methods and require a targeted source.

children.title: Parallel LNS Execution
children.top_down_role: Covers concurrent LNS workers exploring separate neighborhoods or trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel LNS Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent execution of multiple bounded LNS workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(P\ge2\) workers and an initial feasible incumbent, assign each worker \(p\) an LNS policy \(\pi_p\), local state, and resource allocation. Workers concurrently generate and solve neighborhoods, maintain local best solutions, and publish feasible improvements according to a specified communication schedule. A worker may incorporate published information only at synchronization points prescribed by the execution model. When the global stopping condition holds, synchronize the workers and return a feasible solution having minimum objective value among all solutions published or retained locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run several LNS workers concurrently under declared communication and synchronization rules, then return the best feasible solution held by any worker.
assumptions_latex: \(P\ge2\) and every worker uses sound feasibility checking.
Published solutions are transmitted without changing their variable-value interpretation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output objective equals the minimum objective among all feasible solutions retained or published by the workers at termination.

notation.meaning: LNS policy assigned to worker p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but synchronous and asynchronous parallel LNS have different publication, consistency, and termination semantics. No source supports the stated model.

children.title: Cooperative LNS Coordination
children.top_down_role: Covers collaboration policies among concurrent or distributed LNS workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Cooperative LNS Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination protocol for parallel LNS workers sharing search information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) LNS workers maintain local states \(s_p^t\). At each declared communication event, worker \(p\) publishes a message \(m_p^t=E_p(s_p^t)\) containing permitted information, such as an incumbent, bound, operator statistic, or explored-region descriptor. A coordinator applies a deterministic or randomized aggregation rule \(A\) to available messages and sends directives \(d_p^t=A_p(m_1^t,\ldots,m_P^t)\). Each worker updates only through its local transition rule \(s_p^{t+1}=U_p(s_p^t,d_p^t)\). At termination, return the best globally reported feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers publish specified search information; a coordinator aggregates it into directives that update worker states while preserving each worker’s local search rule.
assumptions_latex: All message, aggregation, and update rules are specified.
Every solution accepted as an incumbent is independently checked for feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coordination changes worker states only through declared messages and directives, and the returned solution is globally reported and feasible.

notation.meaning: state of worker p at communication event t
coordinator directive sent to worker p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but this is a generic coordinator abstraction rather than a sourced cooperative LNS protocol; aggregation and update semantics remain architecture-dependent.

children.title: Incumbent Exchange
children.top_down_role: Covers communication of improved or diverse solutions between workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving exchange of improving incumbents among LNS workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, worker \(p\) maintains a feasible incumbent \(x_p\). Whenever it obtains a feasible candidate \(y\) with \(f(y)<f(x_p)\), it atomically publishes \((y,f(y))\). Upon receiving a published pair \((z,v)\), a worker verifies feasibility and \(v=f(z)\), then replaces its incumbent exactly when \(v<f(x_p)\); otherwise it ignores the message. Neighborhood searches already in progress may finish under their original incumbent, but subsequent neighborhoods use the latest accepted incumbent. At termination, return the best verified published incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers publish strict feasible improvements and adopt a received solution only after validating it and confirming that its objective improves their incumbent.
assumptions_latex: All workers solve the same minimization model and use the same objective convention.
Publication and reception preserve complete solution assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each worker’s accepted incumbent values are nonincreasing, and the returned incumbent is feasible.

notation.meaning: published feasible solution and objective value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but strict-improvement adoption and delayed use by in-progress searches are protocol choices that need support from a parallel-LNS source.

children.title: Shared Operator Learning
children.top_down_role: Covers aggregation of operator-performance evidence across workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Operator Learning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed updating of common LNS operator-performance statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) workers select operators from a common finite set \(\mathcal O\). Worker \(p\) records observations \((i,r,w)\), where \(i\in\mathcal O\), \(r\) is the measured reward, and \(w>0\) is its aggregation weight. At synchronization event \(t\), aggregate all newly reported observations by \[N_i^{t+1}=N_i^t+\sum w,
\qquad S_i^{t+1}=S_i^t+\sum wr,
\] with each sum restricted to new reports for operator \(i\). Broadcast the resulting statistics; each worker applies its declared selection rule using \(N_i^{t+1}\) and \(S_i^{t+1}\). Count every observation exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers pool weighted operator outcomes into shared counts and rewards, then use the broadcast aggregate statistics for subsequent operator selection.
assumptions_latex: All workers use the same operator identifiers and reward scale.
Every reported observation has a unique identifier preventing duplicate aggregation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_i^t\) and \(S_i^t\) equal the aggregate weight and weighted reward of all uniquely incorporated reports for operator \(i\).

notation.meaning: shared aggregate weight for operator i
shared weighted reward total for operator i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, and the aggregation invariant is coherent, but no source supports this weighted sharing protocol; reward normalization, report staleness, and synchronization semantics are unspecified.

children.title: Under-Destruction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers neighborhoods too restricted to permit meaningful structural change.

knowledge_statements.title: Under-Destruction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational definition for minimization LNS with incumbent-conditioned repair neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite feasible set, let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\) be minimized, and let \(N_D(x)\subseteq F\) be the neighborhood obtained by relaxing variables \(D\) while fixing their complement to incumbent \(x\). For thresholds \(d_{\min}\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\), an LNS run is in an under-destruction regime at \(x\) when every destruction set in the current operator support satisfies \( |D|\le d_{\min}\) and \[\Pr\!\left(\exists y\in N_D(x):f(y)<f(x)\right)\le\varepsilon.\] Thus the supported neighborhoods are too restricted to expose an improving repair with more than probability \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under-destruction occurs when all supported relaxations are small and the probability that their repair neighborhoods contain an improving solution is at most a chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and nonempty.
The probability is taken over the current destruction-operator distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\exists y\in N_D(x):f(y)<f(x))\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Feasible repair neighborhood after relaxing variables D at incumbent x.
Operational upper bound defining insufficient destruction.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operationalizes under-destruction by neighborhood size and improvement availability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operational definition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the size and improvement-probability criterion is a proposed formalization with no cited LNS source.

children.title: Search Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Covers repeated repair outcomes with little objective or structural progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Search Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window incumbent stagnation, distinct from failure to generate feasible repairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization LNS run, let \(x_t\in F\) denote the incumbent after completed iteration \(t\), and define \(b_t=f(x_t)\). Given a window length \(W\ge1\) and tolerance \(\delta\ge0\), stagnation is present at iteration \(t\ge W\) precisely when \[b_{t-W}-b_t\le\delta.\] For strict-improvement acceptance and \(\delta=0\), this is equivalent to \(b_{t-W}=b_{t-W+1}=\cdots=b_t\); feasible candidate generation may nevertheless continue throughout the window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A run stagnates when its incumbent objective improves by no more than a specified tolerance during a fixed number of completed iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is minimized and incumbent values are nonincreasing.
\(W\ge1\) and \(t\ge W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_{t-W}-b_t\le\delta\).

notation.meaning: Incumbent objective value after iteration t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-window condition is mathematically precise and matches the title, but no inspectable source supports this particular LNS stagnation definition or its tolerance convention.

children.title: Stagnation Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Covers observable signals distinguishing limited neighborhood reach from ordinary slow progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic separating absent improvement, low novelty, and repair failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input completed LNS iterations \(t-W+1,\ldots,t\), candidates \(y_i\) when produced, feasibility indicators \(s_i\), incumbent values \(b_i\), and thresholds \((\delta,
u_0,ho_0)\). Compute \[\Delta=b_{t-W}-b_t,\qquad 
u= rac{|\{y_i:i=t-W+1,\ldots,t\}|}{W},\qquad ho= rac1W\sum_{i=t-W+1}^{t}s_i.\] Report stagnation when \(\Delta\le\delta\). Label it low-novelty when additionally \(
u\le
u_0\), and repair-limited when additionally \(ho\leho_0\). Otherwise retain the unclassified-stagnation label. Output the label and the triple \((\Delta,
u,ho)\).
